IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p231/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p231/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p231/r6.claim: Some interpreters say Jonah left angry at his people, a reading they use to avoid saying that he was angry with God.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p231/r6.anchor: وقالوا في قوله: وذا النون إذ ذهب مغاضبا: إنه غاضب قومه! استيحاشا من أن يكون مع تأييد الله وعصمته وتوفيقه وتطهيره، يخرج مغاضبا لربه.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p231/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p231/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p231/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba rejects anger at either God or Jonah's people: Jonah had warned them of a timed punishment, then withdrew awaiting it.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p231/r7.anchor: ولم يذهب مغاضبا لربه ولا لقومه، لأنه بعث إليهم فدعاهم برهة من الدهر فلم يستجيبوا، ووعدهم عن الله فلم يرغبوا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p231/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p231/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p231/r8.claim: When Nineveh repented near the appointed time, people brought nursing mothers and children, pleaded with God, and the punishment was lifted for a time.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p231/r8.anchor: فلما حضر الوقت أو قرب فكر القوم واعتبروا، فتابوا إلى الله وأنابوا، وخرجوا بالمراضيع وأطفالها يجأرون ويتضرعون، فكشف الله تعالى عنهم العذاب

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p231/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p231/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p231/r9.claim: If Jonah left angry at unbelieving people who deserved opposition, their punishment of him by the fish, darkness, and prolonged grief would be inexplicable.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p231/r9.anchor: فإن كان نبي الله، صلى الله عليه وسلم، ذهب مغاضبا على قومه قبل أن يؤمنوا، فإنما راغم من استحق في الله أن يراغم

NASHR:v2p147/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p147/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p147/r6.claim: Codices differ on the al-Anbiya phrase an la ilaha illa anta: most write it separately and some join it.
NASHR:v2p147/r6.anchor: واختلف المصاحف في قوله تعالى: في سورة الأنبياء أن لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك ففي أكثرها مقطوع، وفي بعضها موصول

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p92/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p92/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p92/r2.claim: Jonah, Zacharias, John, Mary, and Jesus exemplify that no one can impede God's mercy when He wills to aid His servants; all means are in His control.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p92/r2.anchor: when God wants to show mercy to His servants, none can impede His intentions

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p437#3/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p437#3/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p437#3/r7.claim: النون means whale or fish, plural نينان; the source reports the phrase النينان قبله الحمر.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p437#3/r7.anchor: النون: الحوت ويجمع على نينان، وروي: النينان قبله الحمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r9.claim: Maghāḍiban is an accusative circumstantial phrase; it can mean angry, with the reciprocal form used without reciprocity, as in the verbs for punishing or travelling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r9.anchor: وانتصب مغاضبا على الحال. فقيل: معناه غضبان وهو من المفاعلة التي لا تقتضي اشتراكا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r10.claim: One reading is that Jonah angered his people by leaving and making them fear punishment, while they had angered him by rejecting his call; he left before divine permission, as prophets did when punishment approached.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r10.anchor: وقيل مغاضبا لقومه أغضبهم بمفارقته وتخوفهم حلول العذاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r11.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r11.claim: A story says Jonah left angry with King Hezekiah after the king assigned him to fight a ruler who had insulted the Israelites; Jonah asked whether God had commanded or named him, and left when the king persisted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r11.anchor: وقيل مغاضبا للملك حزقيا حين عينه لغزو ملك كان قد عاب في بني إسرائيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r12.claim: Accounts that Jonah was angry with God and descriptions of how are to be discarded as incompatible with prophethood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r12.anchor: وقول من قال مغاضبا لربه وحكى في المغاضبة لربه كيفيات يجب اطراحه إذ لا يناسب شيء منها منصب النبوة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r13.speaker: الحسن والشعبي وابن جبير وابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r13.claim: The author interprets these scholars’ phrase ‘angry with his Lord’ as meaning angry for the sake of his Lord and religion, with the lām causal rather than a direct-object marker.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r13.anchor: وينبغي أن يتأول لمن قال ذلك من العلماء كالحسن والشعبي وابن جبير وغيرهم من التابعين، وابن مسعود من الصحابة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r14.speaker: أبو شرف
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r14.claim: Abu Sharaf reads mughḍaban as a passive participle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r14.anchor: وقرأ أبو شرف مغضبا اسم مفعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r15.claim: The author explains lan naqdira as ‘we will not constrain him,’ deriving it from qadr rather than power.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r15.anchor: فظن أن لن نقدر عليه أي نضيق عليه من القدر لا من القدرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r16.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r16.claim: An alternative explanation derives the phrase from qudra and takes it to mean that God would not test Jonah.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r16.anchor: وقيل: من القدرة بمعنى أن لن نقدر عليه الابتلاء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r17.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r17.claim: The majority reads naqdira with the majestic first-person nūn and no doubling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r17.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور نقدر بنون العظمة مخففا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r18.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى وأبو شرف والكلبي وحميد بن قيس ويعقوب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r18.claim: These readers use a yāʾ form with ḍamma and a light dāl.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r18.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي ليلى وأبو شرف والكلبي وحميد بن قيس ويعقوب بضم الياء وفتح الدال مخففا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r19.speaker: عيسى والحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r19.claim: Isa and al-Hasan read the yāʾ with fatḥa and the dāl with kasra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r19.anchor: وعيسى والحسن بالياء مفتوحة وكسر الدال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r20.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب واليماني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r20.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib and al-Yamani read a doubled form with yāʾ, ḍamma, and fatḥa on qāf and dāl.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r20.anchor: وعلي بن أبي طالب واليماني بضم الياء وفتح القاف والدال مشددة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r21.speaker: الزهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r21.claim: Al-Zuhri reads a doubled form with nūn, ḍamma, fatḥa on qāf, and kasra on dāl.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r21.anchor: والزهري بالنون مضمومة وفتح القاف وكسر الدال مشددة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r22.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r22.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r22.claim: The omitted sentences around Jonah’s cry are explained in Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt, where the author says he will discuss Jonah’s story.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r22.anchor: فنادى في الظلمات في الكلام جمل محذوفة قد أوضحت في سورة والصافات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r23.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r23.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r23.claim: The plural ‘darknesses’ conveys their dense layering; they are explained as the whale’s belly, the sea, and the night.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r23.anchor: وجمع الظلمات لشدة تكاثفها فكأنها ظلمة مع ظلمة. وقيل: ظلمات بطن الحوت والبحر والليل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r24.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r24.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r24.claim: Another explanation says a second whale swallowed the first, leaving Jonah in the darkness of two whale bellies and the sea.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p460#2/r24.anchor: ابتلع حوته حوت آخر فصار في ظلمتي بطني الحوتين وظلمة البحر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p461/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p461/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p461/r1.claim: A report says Jonah prostrated inside the whale after hearing the fish glorify God on the sea floor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p461/r1.anchor: وروي أن يونس سجد في جوف الحوت حين سمع تسبيح الحيتان في قعر البحر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p461/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p461/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p461/r2.claim: The particle an is explanatory because the preceding call has the meaning of saying; alternatively, an omitted bi makes it a lightened form of the heavy particle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p461/r2.anchor: وأن في أن لا إله إلا أنت تفسيرية لأنه سبق فنادى وهو في معنى القول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p461/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p461/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p461/r3.claim: The supplication first confines divinity to God, then declares Him free of نقص, and then admits what follows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p461/r3.anchor: حصر الألوهية فيه تعالى ثم نزهه عن سمات النقص ثم أقر بما بعد ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p461/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p461/r4.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p461/r4.claim: The Prophet says no distressed person who calls on God with this supplication will fail to be answered; no grading is stated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p461/r4.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ما من مكروب يدعو بهذا الدعاء إلا استجيب له»

ALUSI-FULL:v17p109/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p109/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p109/r4.claim: Some describe Jonah’s lapse as an effect of divine indulgence; familiarity falls below pure servitude because the will has not been wholly effaced.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p109/r4.anchor: قيل إن ذلك رشحة من دن خمر الدلال وذكروا أن مقام الدل دون مقام العبودية المحضة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p109/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p109/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p109/r5.claim: Jonah’s confession means that a desire for anything other than God stirred secretly within him, contrary to what he truly willed.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p109/r5.anchor: أي حيث اختلج في سري أن أريد غيره ما أردت

SIBAWAYH:وذلكإنلعلوليتوأخواتهاورويدورويد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكإنلعلوليتوأخواتهاورويدورويد.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكإنلعلوليتوأخواتهاورويدورويد.claim: With لعل, ليت, رويد, عليك, هلم and similar particles, attached object pronouns behave as with verbs, but are weaker: عليكه and رويده are possible while detached إياه is not normally used.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكإنلعلوليتوأخواتهاورويدورويد.anchor: فعلامات الإضمار حالهن هاهنا كحالهن في الفعل لا تقوى أن تقول عليك إياه

SIBAWAYH:وذلكإنلعلوليتوأخواتهاورويدورويد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكإنلعلوليتوأخواتهاورويدورويد.speaker: يونس
SIBAWAYH:وذلكإنلعلوليتوأخواتهاورويدورويد.claim: Yūnus heard some Arabs say عليكني spontaneously; others avoid نى and نا here because عليك بي and عليك بنا suffice.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكإنلعلوليتوأخواتهاورويدورويد.anchor: وحدثنا يونس أنه سمع [ من العرب ]

SIBAWAYH:وذلكإنلعلوليتوأخواتهاورويدورويد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكإنلعلوليتوأخواتهاورويدورويد.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكإنلعلوليتوأخواتهاورويدورويد.claim: Detached إياك is awkward after رأيت when the clitic already expresses the same object; this economy also explains why comparable forms after إن and ضرب زيد are rejected.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكإنلعلوليتوأخواتهاورويدورويد.anchor: قبيح أن تقول رأيت فيها إياك

SIBAWAYH:وذلكإنلعلوليتوأخواتهاورويدورويد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكإنلعلوليتوأخواتهاورويدورويد.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكإنلعلوليتوأخواتهاورويدورويد.claim: Exceptive clauses such as ما أتاني إلا أنت and ما رأيت إلا إياك are different: moving إلا makes the statement impossible, while deleting it reverses the meaning.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكإنلعلوليتوأخواتهاورويدورويد.anchor: أنت وما رأيت إلا إياك فإنه لا يدخل على هذا

SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r1.claim: ذا النون means the whale; its plural is نينان, parallel to حوت and حيتان, and the name reflects its swallowing Jonah.
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r1.anchor: { وذا النون }: الحوت، ويجمع على نينان، كحوت وحيتان. وسمي بذلك، لأن النون ابتلعه.

SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r2.claim: مغاضبا is a circumstantial accusative describing the subject of ذهب.
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r2.anchor: حال من فاعل " ذهب ". والمفاعلة هنا تحتمل أن تكون على بابها

SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r3.claim: The reciprocal form can mean Jonah and his people were angry with one another when they initially did not believe.
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r3.anchor: والمفاعلة هنا تحتمل أن تكون على بابها من المشاركة. أي: غاضب قومه وغاضبوه،

SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r4.speaker: بعض التفاسير
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r4.claim: Some commentaries say Jonah was مغاضبا لربه; if this report is sound from a credible authority, ل is causal, meaning for the Lord and His religion, not an object marker.
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r4.anchor: وفي بعض التفاسير: مغاضبا لربه. فإن صح ذلك عمن يعتبر قوله، فينبغي أن تكون اللام للتعليل

SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r5.claim: The word may instead mean angry, without reciprocity, like عاقبت and سافرت.
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r5.anchor: أن تكون بمعنى: غضبان فلا مشاركة كعاقبت وسافرت.

SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r6.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r6.claim: The general reading has مغاضبا as an active participle.

SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r7.speaker: أبو شرف
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r7.claim: Abu Sharaf is reported to read مغاضبا with fatḥa on the ḍād in a passive construction.
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو شرف " مغاضبا " بفتح الضاد على ما لم يسم فاعله.

SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reports Abu Sharaf's reading without the alif, مغضبا, from أَغْضَبْتُهُ.
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r8.anchor: ونقله الزمخشري عن أبي شرف " مغضبا " دون ألف من أغضبته فهو مغضب.

SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r9.claim: أن is a lightened form of إن, with an omitted pronoun of the matter as its subject and لن نقدر as its predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r9.anchor: هذه المخففة، واسمها ضمير الشأن محذوف. و { لن نقدر } هو الخبر.

SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r10.claim: Here نقدر means constrain, as in verses describing a constricted provision; the omitted object is the places or directions.

SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r11.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r11.claim: The general reading uses first-person plural, an open nūn and an ungeminated, lightly pronounced dāl.
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r11.anchor: وتخفيف الدال. والمفعول محذوف أي: الجهات والأماكن.

SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r12.speaker: الزهري
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r12.claim: Al-Zuhri reads with a ḍamma on the dāl and a doubled consonant.

SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r13.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى وأبو شرف والكلبي وحميد بن قيس
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r13.claim: Ibn Abi Layla, Abu Sharaf, al-Kalbi, and Humayd ibn Qays read with passive yā and a light dāl.
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r13.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي ليلى وأبو شرف والكلبي وحميد بن قيس " يقدر " بضم الياء من تحت وفتح الدال خفيفة

SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r14.speaker: الحسن وعيسى بن عمر
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r14.claim: Al-Hasan and Isa ibn Umar read with fatḥa on yā and kasra on a light dāl.
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r14.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعيسى بن عمر بفتح الياء وكسر الدال خفيفة.

SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r15.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب واليماني
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r15.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib and al-Yamani read with ḍamma on yā and kasra on a doubled dāl; in the two active readings just described, the subject is a pronoun referring to God.
SAMIN-DURR:21:87/r15.anchor: وعلي بن أبي طالب واليماني بضم الياء وكسر الدال مشددة. والفاعل على هذين الوجهين ضمير يعود على الله تعالى.

SAMIN-DURR:21:87#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:87#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:87#2/r1.claim: أن may be the lightened إن, with its omitted subject pronoun and the following negative clause as predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:21:87#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أنها المخففة من الثقيلة. فاسمها كا تقدم محذوف.

SAMIN-DURR:21:87#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:87#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:87#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, أن is explanatory because it follows a word that implies speech, though it is not itself a verb of saying.
SAMIN-DURR:21:87#2/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنها تفسيرية؛ لأنها بعد ما هو بمعنى القول لا حروفه.

ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r1.claim: ذو النون is Jonah, and the nūn is the fish; the command means remember Jonah.
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r1.anchor: يونس، والنون السمكة، والمعنى واذكر ذا النون

ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r2.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r2.claim: Reports differ on whether Jonah left in anger at his people or at a king.
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r2.anchor: ذهب مغاضبا قومه، وقيل إنه ذهب مغاضبا ملكا من الملوك.

ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r3.claim: He thought God would not decree the appointed confinement in the fish; here نقدر means يقدر, to decree or measure out.
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r3.anchor: أي ظن أن لن نقدر عليه ما قدرناه من كونه في بطن الحوت، ويقدر بمعنى يقدر.

ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r4.speaker: الحسن
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r4.claim: Al-Hasan called Jonah a servant who fled from his Lord; Zajjaj clarifies this means fleeing God's punishment, not thinking escape could evade God or His decree.
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r4.anchor: وقد روي عن الحسن أنه قال عبد أبق من ربه، وتأويل قول الحسن أنه هرب من عذاب ربه،

ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r5.claim: The preferred explanation is the darkness of night, sea, and the fish's belly: Jonah entered them successively.
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r5.anchor: أحدهما يعنى به ظلمة الليل وظلمة البحر.

ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r6.claim: Another possible sense is that most of Jonah's calls and prayers occurred in the darkness of night.
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r6.anchor: أن يكون أكثر دعائه وندائه كان في ظلمات الليل.

ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r7.claim: Zajjaj favors the first explanation because Jonah in the fish could not distinguish night from the other darknesses.
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r7.anchor: والأجود التفسير الأول لأنه في بطن الحوت لا أحسبه كان يفصل بين ظلمة الليل

ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r8.claim: The darknesses could coincide, with the fish's belly darkened by both night and sea, making the darkness extreme.
ZAJJAJ:v3p402/r8.anchor: وجائز أن يكون الظلمات اتفقت في وقت واحد، فتكون ظلمة بطن الحوت في الليل والبحر نهاية في الشدة.

ASAD-NOTES:21:87/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:87/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:87/r1.claim: In anger Jonah assumes God has no power over him, then cries out in distress, affirming God's oneness and glory and confessing his wrongdoing.
ASAD-NOTES:21:87/r1.anchor: when he went off in wrath, thinking that We had no power over him![83] But then he cried out

ASAD-NOTES:21:87#n82/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:87#n82/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:87#n82/r1.claim: The “great fish” refers to Jonah, whose swallowing by a great fish is also mentioned at 37:139 onward and narrated in the Book of Jonah.
ASAD-NOTES:21:87#n82/r1.anchor: the Prophet Jonah, who is said to have been swallowed by a "great fish", as mentioned in 37:139 ff.

ASAD-NOTES:21:87#n83/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:87#n83/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:87#n83/r1.claim: Asad says Jonah was sent to Nineveh; after his preaching was ignored, he angrily abandoned his mission, which 37:140 likens to a runaway slave's flight.
ASAD-NOTES:21:87#n83/r1.anchor: Jonah was a prophet sent to the people of Nineveh, the capital of Assyria. At first his preaching was disregarded

ASAD-NOTES:21:87#n83/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:87#n83/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:87#n83/r2.claim: Jonah's temporary punishment and later rescue and redemption form an allegory; this and the next verse allude to his punishment, repentance, and salvation, also told in 37:139-148.
ASAD-NOTES:21:87#n83/r2.anchor: The allegory of his temporary punishment and his subsequent rescue and redemption is referred to elsewhere in the Qur'an

ASAD-NOTES:21:87#n83/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:87#n83/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:87#n83/r3.claim: The redemption of Jonah's people is separately mentioned in 10:98 and 37:147-148.
ASAD-NOTES:21:87#n83/r3.anchor: The redemption of Jonah's people is mentioned in 10:98 and 37:147-148.

ASAD-NOTES:21:87#n84/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:87#n84/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:87#n84/r1.claim: The final confession literally says, “I was among the wrongdoers.”

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p878/r10.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p878/r10.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p878/r10.claim: Jonah and Lot are not descendants of Abraham; both left their people as migrants, and the Qur'an pairs them in al-Ṣāffāt, where Jonah leaves angry and Lot says he is migrating to his Lord.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p878/r10.anchor: ويونس ليس من ذرية إبراهيم وكذلك لوط ليس من ذرية إبراهيم، ويونس ولوط كلاهما مهاجر

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p134/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p134/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p134/r3.claim: The passage names Jonah, Zacharias, and Mary in connection with desperate appeals to God, which He answered through special mercy, making the impossible possible.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p134/r3.anchor: After that Jonah (sws), Zacharias (sws) and Mary (sws) are mentioned. They called upon their Lord in hopeless and desperate circumstances.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p134/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p134/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p134/r4.claim: These messengers' lives teach the sūra's addressees not to become arrogant when granted divine favors and blessings.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p134/r4.anchor: There is a great lesson in the lives of these messengers for the addressees of this sūrah who were showing arrogance on being granted favours and blessings from God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p134/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p134/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p134/r5.claim: These examples also guide the Prophet's oppressed Companions, who were facing precarious trials and could see only darkness ahead.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p134/r5.anchor: they also provide guidance to the oppressed companions of the Prophet (sws) who at that time were passing through very precarious trials and could see nothing but darkness in front of them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r1.claim: Dhu al-Nun means “companion of the fish”: Jonah received the title after being swallowed, and it also conveys affection.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r2.claim: Jonah was sent to Nineveh; its population of 120,000 in the Book of Jonah accords with Qur’an 37:147, which says 100,000 or more.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r3.claim: After long preaching met rejection, Jonah left in dejection, thinking there was no point in enduring hardship among people who ignored him; such despair is natural for a truthful person.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r3.anchor: he left them. He thought that when he could not penetrate into these stone-hearted people

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r4.claim: A messenger may leave his people only by God’s decision and permission; God knows when a nation can no longer accept truth and when it should face punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r4.anchor: messenger cannot leave his nation without God’s permission

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r5.claim: Jonah thought he had discharged his duty after warning his people and could consign them to God and migrate, expecting relief from his trial.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r5.anchor: he had fulfilled his obligation before God and he should consign such a wretched nation to Him and migrate from them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r6.claim: Jonah’s thought came from pure zeal for truth, but the trial God had set for his people still had to run its course.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r6.anchor: the trials which the Almighty has subjected his people to are bound to take their course.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r7.claim: Disenchanted with his people, Jonah boarded a departing ship, which later encountered a storm.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p143/r7.anchor: he embarked on a ship which was about to set off for a journey. After sailing for sometime, the ship was caught in a storm.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r1.claim: The sailors followed a superstition that a runaway slave aboard caused the storm and that throwing him overboard would end it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r1.anchor: he was thrown overboard, they would not be delivered from the storm.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r2.claim: Lots were cast, and the author says Jonah was assigned to cast them, perhaps because the sailors considered him most respectable; the lot fell on Jonah and he was thrown overboard.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r2.anchor: it was Jonah (sws) who was given the responsibility of casting lots.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r3.claim: A large fish, probably a whale, swallowed Jonah; when he saw his escape attempt had brought him into greater darkness, he prayed sincerely from the heart.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r3.anchor: A large fish, most probably a whale, swallowed him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r4.claim: God accepted Jonah’s sincere prayer, the fish cast him ashore, and God grew a pumpkin-like plant to shade his weakened body.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r4.anchor: the fish cast him on the sandy shore. There, in order to save his emaciated body from the heat of the sun

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r5.claim: After Jonah recovered, God sent him again to warn Nineveh; the withered sheltering plant made him grieve, and God taught him to consider the people He had created and raised.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r5.anchor: if he has been aggrieved by the withering away of a trivial creeper

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r6.claim: God directed Jonah back to Nineveh, where his renewed warning moved everyone from ordinary people to the king to profess faith and repent.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r6.anchor: Such was the profound effect of his call that everyone from the common man to the king started to tremble.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r7.claim: The king removed his royal robe, put on sackcloth, and ordered the people to abandon evil, fast, plead to God, and repent.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r7.anchor: The king took off his royal robe and attired himself in sackcloth.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r8.claim: The author reconstructs Jonah’s account to correct exegetes’ confused reports, relying on indications and statements in the Bible and Qur’an and pointing readers to al-Saffat for more.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r8.anchor: I have presented the above details to give its true picture.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r9.claim: The object of “angry” is suppressed because context makes clear that Jonah left his nation while sad and angry.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r9.anchor: because of concomitant indications. The implication is: he left his nation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r10.claim: Jonah left in anger because he had done all he could to warn his people, but they ignored him, humiliated truth, and mocked his message.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r10.anchor: he did all that he could to warn them, but they completely ignored him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r11.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r11.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r11.claim: Jonah thought that leaving could deliver him from the affliction his nation had put him through.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p144/r11.anchor: he thought that in this manner he would be able to deliver himself from the trial his nation had put him through.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r1.claim: Jonah’s zeal made him overlook that God had commissioned him; deserting without God’s permission could expose him to a greater trial.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r1.anchor: if he deserts it without His permission, he could face an

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r2.claim: Jonah did not think he could escape God’s accountability; he hoped to distance himself from wicked people and live peacefully, but a messenger is like a soldier who cannot leave his post without permission.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r2.anchor: This thought in itself is not a sin, but a messenger, as just indicated, is like a soldier deputed at a front.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r3.claim: Although the act seemed innocent, it implied that Jonah could escape God’s trial by his own choice; God exposed this hidden implication to correct him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r3.anchor: This hidden aspect was not evident to Jonah (sws). For this reason, it was made plain before him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r4.claim: A person can miss the mistaken idea implicit in an innocent act until a wise guide points it out; God corrects messengers because they exemplify conduct for humanity and even slight deviations can have far-reaching consequences.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r4.anchor: Since messengers of God are an example for all mankind, even a slight deviation from them is checked by God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r5.claim: The author prefers this reading as reasonable and free of blame toward Jonah; it avoids the exegetes’ strained linguistic reinterpretations, which still failed to solve the difficulty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r5.anchor: This interpretation is in consonance with the norms sense and reason and also does not entail any blame on Jonah (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r6.claim: The ship’s details are omitted and only Jonah’s prayer in the fish’s belly is reported so the account can stress God’s acceptance of a servant’s plea in hopeless danger, provided he trusts and calls only on God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r6.anchor: the purpose is not to divulge its details but to show that the gracious God accepts the supplications of His servant

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r7.speaker: Book of Jonah
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r7.claim: The Bible’s Book of Jonah gives a parallel prayer in which Jonah calls to the Lord from distress and says his cry was heard.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r7.anchor: In the Book of Jonah of the Bible, this supplication is mentioned

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r8.claim: The plural “darknesses” intensifies and expands the darkness; Arabic plurals can express vastness, as in al-Mashariq and al-Magharib, and here denotes darkness in the fish’s belly and deep sea.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r8.anchor: in the Arabic language, at times a plural denotes vastness.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r9.claim: The wording shows that God does not need a public forum or broadcast technology to hear a servant’s call in the deep sea.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p145/r9.anchor: The purpose is to show that no one should be misled by the fact that God needs a public forum

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p146/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p146/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p146/r1.claim: God hears and answers His servants’ cries even in the pitch darkness of the deep sea.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p146/r1.anchor: He listens to the cries of His servants in the pitch darkness of the deep sea and responds to them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p146/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p146/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p146/r2.claim: Jonah asked for nothing in the prayer; he confessed his fault and entrusted the matter to his Lord, whose verdict would be best, wise, and merciful.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p146/r2.anchor: Jonah (sws) has not expressed any desire or demand; he only expressed and confessed his mistake.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p146/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p146/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p146/r3.claim: The prayer first affirms that only God deserves worship and obedience and that all matters return to Him, then declares Him free of defect and admits Jonah wronged himself rather than God wronging him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p146/r3.anchor: First of all, he expressed that only God is worthy of worship and obedience and all matters turn to Him.

NASHR:v1p344/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p344/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p344/r3.claim: A semantic cause for lengthening is emphatic negation; although weaker than a phonetic cause, the author endorses madd al-taʿẓīm in لا إله إلا الله, لا إله إلا هو, and لا إله إلا أنت through routes of qasr readers.
NASHR:v1p344/r3.anchor: ومنه مد التعظيم في نحو (لا إله إلا الله)

NASHR:v1p344/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p344/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p344/r4.claim: Abū Maʿshar al-Ṭabarī, al-Hudhali, Ibn Mihrān, al-Jajānī and others document this emphasis-lengthening, also called madd al-mubālagha; the author read it through their routes.
NASHR:v1p344/r4.anchor: أبو معشر الطبري وأبو القاسم الهذلي، وابن مهران

QIRAAT-ER:21:87:11#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:21:87:11#1/r1.speaker: Pss
QIRAAT-ER:21:87:11#1/r1.claim: The passive yuqdara means that a decree would be imposed on him and removes the divine agent, presenting the decree impersonally.
QIRAAT-ER:21:87:11#1/r1.anchor: Pss, mutawatir: "Passive: ""it would be decreed upon him"" — removes the divine agent entirely

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p27#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p27#4/r1.speaker: قتادة والكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p27#4/r1.claim: Qatada and al-Kalbi explain the phrase as Jonah thinking that God would not decree punishment against him.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p27#4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة والكلبي ﴿ فظن أن لن نقدر عليه ﴾ قالا ظن أن لن نقضي عليه العقوبة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p27#4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p27#4/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p27#4/r2.claim: Qatada identifies the three darknesses as the fish’s belly, the sea, and the night.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p27#4/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فنادى في الظلمات ﴾ قال ظلمة بطن الحوت وظلمة البحر وظلمة الليل

MUSNAD-AHMAD:1462/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:1462/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:1462/r1.claim: Saʿd reports that the Prophet identified Jonah's invocation in the fish as a prayer; a Muslim who uses it in any need receives a response.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:1462/r1.anchor: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكر لنا أول دعوة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p82#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p82#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p82#4/r1.claim: Dhu al-Nun means Jonah, son of Matti; Ibn Hajar authenticates Matti as his father's name but says no connected genealogy is found in the reports.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p82#4/r1.anchor: يونس عليه السلام ابن متي وهو اسم أبيه على ما في صحيح البخاري وغيره وصححه ابن حجر

ALUSI-FULL:v17p82#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p82#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p82#4/r2.claim: It is also said that Jonah lived in the era of the Persian interregnum kings.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p82#4/r2.anchor: وقد قيل إنه كان في زمن ملوك الطوائف من الفرس

ALUSI-FULL:v17p82#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p82#4/r3.speaker: ابن الأثير
ALUSI-FULL:v17p82#4/r3.claim: Ibn al-Athir and others say Matti was Jonah's mother; no prophet besides Jonah and Jesus is named through his mother.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p82#4/r3.anchor: وقال ابن الأثير كغيره إنه اسم أمه ولم ينسب أحد من الأنبياء إلى أمه غيره وغير عيسى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p82#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p82#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p82#4/r4.claim: The Jews call him Yonah son of Amitai; other forms given are Yonah ben Amittai and Yunān ben Amāthi.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p82#4/r4.anchor: واليهود قالوا بما تقدم إلا أنهم سموه يونه بن اميتاي وبعضهم يقول يونان بن أماثي

ALUSI-FULL:v17p82#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p82#4/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p82#4/r5.claim: Al-nun means the fish; its plurals are nīnān, cited in al-Bahr, and anwān, cited in al-Qamus.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p82#4/r5.anchor: والنون الحوت كما أشرنا إليه ويجمع على نينان كما في البحر وأنوان أيضا كما في القاموس

ALUSI-FULL:v17p83/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p83/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p83/r1.claim: Jonah left angry at his people because of their stubbornness and persistent rejection despite his prolonged preaching.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p83/r1.anchor: أي غضبان على قومه لشدة شكيمتهم وتمادي إصرارهم مع طول دعوته إياهم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p83/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p83/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p83/r2.claim: His departure was a migration from his people, but God had not commanded him to leave.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p83/r2.anchor: وكان ذهابه هذا هجرة عنهم لكنه لم يؤمر به

ALUSI-FULL:v17p83/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p83/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p83/r3.claim: An alternative says Jonah was angry at King Hezekiah; Ibn Abbas's account has Hezekiah send him after an invasion despite no divine order, then recounts the storm and lots, the fish, Jonah's restoration and gourd, his return to Nineveh, and the people's repentance and belief.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p83/r3.anchor: على الملك حزقيل فقد روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال

ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r1.speaker: اليهود
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r1.claim: The Jewish account says Jonah fled God's order to warn Nineveh, boarded at Jaffa for Tarshish, was swallowed after lots, then went to Nineveh; al-Alusi rejects this as an unworthy flight for prophets and calls the Jews liars.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r1.anchor: وكون المراد مغاضبا لربه عز وجل مقتضى زعم اليهود فإنهم زعموا أن الله تعالى أمره أن يذهب إلى نينوى وينذر أهلها

ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r2.claim: Mughāḍiban is an accusative circumstantial expression; its reciprocal form need not denote reciprocal action, as in 'I punished the thief' or 'I traveled,' and may intensify the sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r2.anchor: على الحال وهو من المفاعلة التي لا تقتضي اشتراكا نحو عاقبت اللص وسافرت

ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r3.claim: An alternative reads the reciprocal form literally: Jonah was angry at his people for disbelief, while they were angry at his departure because they feared punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r3.anchor: وقيل المفاعلة على ظاهرها فإنه عليه السلام غضب على قومه لكفرهم وهم غضبوا عليه بالذهاب

ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r4.speaker: أبو سرف
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r4.claim: Abu Sarf reads the passive participle mughḍaban.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r4.anchor: قرأ أبو سرف ( مغضبا ) اسم مفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r5.claim: Al-Alusi explains lan naqdira as God decreeing punishment or similar for Jonah, or constraining him by confinement or another hardship.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r5.anchor: أي أنه أي الشأن لن نقدر ونقضي عليه بعقوبة ونحوها أو لن نضيق عليه في أمره بحبس ونحوه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r6.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز والزهري
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r6.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz and al-Zuhri read naqdira with a doubled, inflected dāl, supporting the sense 'decree/judge.'
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r6.anchor: قراءة عمر بن عبد العزيز والزهري ( نقدر ) بالنون مضمومة وفتح القاف

ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r7.speaker: علي واليماني
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r7.claim: Ali and al-Yamani read yuqaddiru in a form from taqdīr, likewise carrying the familiar sense of decree or judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r7.anchor: قراءة علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه واليماني ( يقدر ) بضم الياء وفتح القاف

ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r8.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r8.claim: The root can also mean to constrict, as al-Raghib records.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بمعنى التضيق فإنه ورد بهذا المعنى أيضا كما ذكره الراغب

ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r9.speaker: معاوية وابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r9.claim: Muawiya understood the phrase as God's lacking power and found that impossible even for a prophet; Ibn Abbas explained it as decree or constriction instead.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r9.anchor: وظن معاوية رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه من القدرة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r10.claim: If taken from 'ability,' it may be a metaphor for God exercising His power against Jonah.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r10.anchor: وجوز أن يكون من القدرة وتكون مجازا عن أعمالها أي فظن أن لن نعمل قدرتنا فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r11.claim: Alternatively, the wording is a parable: Jonah acted as though God would not constrain him when he left his people without waiting for God's command.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r11.anchor: أو يكون الكلام من باب التمثيل أي فعل فعل من ظن أن لن نقدر عليه في مراغمته قومه من غير انتظار لأمرنا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r12.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r12.claim: Some suggest Satan prompted a fleeting thought that God would not constrain Jonah, which he then rebutted with proof; they compare the believers' Satanic suggestions in 33:10.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r12.anchor: وقيل : يجوز أن يسبق ذلك وهمه عليه السلام بوسوسة الشيطان ثم يردعه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r13.speaker: صاحب الفرائد
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r13.claim: The author of al-Faraid rejects this as too remote for a believer, especially an infallible prophet, and potentially unbelief; 33:10 includes the sincere and others, fleeting thoughts are not settled beliefs, and such a thought would not excuse the departure.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r13.anchor: تعقبه صاحب الفرائد بأن مثله عن المؤمن بعيد فضلا عن النبي المعصوم لأنه كفر

ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r14.claim: A reply says ẓann can figuratively mean an unweighted passing thought, which is not blameworthy; the blame concerns leaving angrily, not the thought as his motive.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r14.anchor: وأجيب بأن الظن بمعنى الهجس في الخاطر من غير ترجيح مجاز مستعمل والعتب على ذهابه مغاضبا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r15.claim: Al-Alusi concludes that the fleeting-thought explanation is possible but has little merit.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r15.anchor: ومع هذا هو وجه لا وجاهة له

ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r16.claim: The fa in fanādā is an explanatory resumption: events such as the lot and the fish's swallowing are understood between the clauses.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r16.anchor: الفاء فصيحة أي فكان ما كان من المساهمة والتقام الحوت فنادى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r17.claim: The plural can intensify the single darkness of the whale's belly; alternatively, it denotes the belly, sea, and night, or two whale bellies together with sea and night. Al-Sirafi's verse illustrates people lost in darkness.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r17.anchor: في الظلمة الشديدة المتكاثفة في بطن الحوت جعلت الظلمة لشدتها كأنها ظلمات

ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r18.speaker: السيرافي
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r18.claim: Al-Sirafi's cited verse describes people as alike in the darkness of night, whether their eyes are sound or defective.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r18.anchor: أنشد السيرافي : وليل تقول الناس في ظلماته سواء

ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r19.claim: The clause may mean 'that there is no god but You,' with an omitted preposition, lightened anna, and suppressed pronoun of the matter; or an may be explanatory, meaning 'namely, no god but You.'
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r19.anchor: أي بأنه لا إله إلا أنت على أن أن مخففة من الثقيلة والجار مقدر وضمير الشأن محذوف أو أي لا إله إلا أنت على أنها مفسرة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r20.claim: Jonah declares God exalted above incapacity and above being the cause of his trial without any cause on Jonah's part.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p84/r20.anchor: أنزهك تنزيها لائقا بك من أن يعجزك شيء أو أن يكون ابتلائي بهذا من غير سبب من جهتي

ALUSI-FULL:v17p85/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p85/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p85/r1.claim: Jonah wronged himself by exposing himself to danger through a hasty migration without God's order, contrary to prophetic practice; he admits his fault and displays repentance to be relieved of distress.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p85/r1.anchor: لأنفسهم بتعريضهم للهلكة حيث بادرت إلى المهاجرة من غير أمر على خلاف معتاد الأنبياء عليهم السلام

TIRMIDHI:3505/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3505/r1.speaker: النبي
TIRMIDHI:3505/r1.claim: Saʿd reports that the Prophet identified Jonah’s prayer in the whale’s belly and said that a Muslim who uses it for any need will have it answered; Tirmidhi gives no grade here.
TIRMIDHI:3505/r1.anchor: دعوة ذي النون إذ دعا وهو في بطن الحوت لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r2.claim: The man of the fish is Jonah son of Mattā.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r2.anchor: {وذا النون} أي: اذكر صاحب الحوت وهو يونس بن متى،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, as transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, says Jonah left angry with his people; they lived in Palestine, where a king captured nine and a half tribes, leaving one and a half.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r3.anchor: فقال الضحاك: مغاضبا لقومه، وهو رواية العوفي وغيره عن ابن عباس، قال: كان يونس وقومه يسكنون فلسطين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r4.claim: In the same account, God told the prophet Isaiah to tell King Hezekiah to send a strong prophet, promising to put fear in the captors so they would release the Israelites.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r4.anchor: فأوحى الله إلى شعياء النبي أن سر إلى حزقيل الملك، وقل له حتى يوجه نبيا قويا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r5.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r5.claim: Jonah objected that God had not ordered or named him and that other strong prophets were available; pressed by the king, he left angry with the prophet, king, and people and boarded the Roman Sea.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r5.anchor: فقال له يونس: هل أمرك الله بإخراجي؟ قال: لا قال: فهل سماني لك؟ قال: لا قال: فهاهنا غيري أنبياء أقوياء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r6.speaker: عروة بن الزبير وسعيد بن جبير وجماعة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r6.claim: ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and others say Jonah was upset when God lifted the threatened punishment; ashamed that his people might call him a liar, he did not know why it had lifted, and his anger was pride at seeming to break his word rather than resentment of God’s decree.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r6.anchor: وقال عروة بن الزبير وسعيد بن جبير وجماعة: ذهب عن قومه مغاضبا لربه إذ كشف عن قومه العذاب بعدما أوعدهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r7.claim: Another report says Jonah feared his people customarily killed anyone who had been proved to lie, after the promised punishment failed to arrive.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r7.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار أنه كان من عادة قومه أن يقتلوا من جربوا عليه الكذب فخشي أن يقتلوه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r8.claim: The reciprocal form can describe an action by one person, as in traveling or punishing; here it means simply that Jonah was angry.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r8.anchor: والمغاضبة هاهنا كالمفاعلة التي تكون من واحد، كالمسافرة والمعاقبة، فمعنى قوله مغاضبا أي غضبان.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Jonah was angry with his Lord after being ordered to go warn and summon his people; he asked for time to prepare, but was told the matter was urgent and was not even granted time to put on a shoe.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p349#2/r9.anchor: وقال الحسن: إنما غضب ربه عز وجل من أجل أنه أمره بالمسير إلى قومه لينذرهم بأسه ويدعوهم إليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Gabriel told Jonah to warn Nineveh; Jonah asked for a mount, was told the matter was urgent, and angrily set out for the ship.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r1.anchor: وعن ابن عباس، قال: أتى جبريل يونس فقال: انطلق إلى أهل نينوى فأنذرهم، قال: ألتمس دابة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r2.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih describes Jonah as righteous but narrow-tempered; the weight of prophethood overwhelmed him, so he cast it aside and fled, and God excluded him from the messengers of firm resolve.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r2.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه: إن يونس بن متى كان عبدا صالحا وكان في خلقه ضيق، فلما حمل عليه أثقال النبوة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r3.claim: The account is linked to the commands to Muhammad to be patient like the messengers of firm resolve and not to be like the man of the fish.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r3.anchor: وقال لنبيه [محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم] (6) {فاصبر كما صبر أولو العزم من الرسل}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r4.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك والكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r4.claim: Mujāhid, Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and al-Kalbī, also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, explain the phrase as Jonah thinking God would not decree punishment for him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r4.anchor: قاله مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك والكلبي، وهو رواية العوفي عن ابن عباس يقال: قدر الله الشيء تقديرا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r5.claim: The verb qadara can mean to decree, and qadara and qaddara are used with the same meaning, as in 56:60.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r5.anchor: يقال: قدر الله الشيء تقديرا وقدر يقدر قدرا بمعنى واحد، ومنه قوله: {نحن قدرنا بينكم الموت} (الواقعة: 60)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r6.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز والزهري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r6.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and al-Zuhrī read the verb with shadda, supporting the interpretation ‘decree.’
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r6.anchor: دليل هذا التأويل قراءة عمر بن عبد العزيز والزهري: {فظن أن لن نقدر عليه} بالتشديد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r7.speaker: عطاء وكثير من العلماء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r7.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and many scholars understand it as thinking God would not constrict Jonah’s confinement, using the sense of restricting provision in 13:26.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r7.anchor: وقال عطاء وكثير من العلماء: معناه فظن أن لن نضيق عليه الحبس، من قوله تعالى: {الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the phrase as a rhetorical question: did Jonah think his Lord was unable to overpower him?
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r8.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: هو استفهام معناه: أفظن أنه يعجز ربه، فلا يقدر عليه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r9.speaker: يعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r9.claim: Yaʿqūb reads the verb passively, with ḍamma on yāʾ, and lightly rather than with a doubled consonant.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r9.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب يقدر [بضم الياء] (1) على المجهول

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r10.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that after sinning Jonah left angry with his Lord, Satan led him to think God would not decree punishment, and God cast him into the fish for forty days and nights rather than leave him to Satan because of his prior worship.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r10.anchor: وعن الحسن قال: بلغني أن يونس لما أصاب الذنب انطلق مغاضبا لربه واستزله الشيطان حتى ظن أن لن نقدر عليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r11.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r11.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says Jonah remained in the fish for seven days.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r11.anchor: وقال عطاء: سبعة أيام [وقيل: ثلاثة أيام] (3)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r12.claim: Another report gives Jonah’s time in the fish as three days.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r12.anchor: وقال عطاء: سبعة أيام [وقيل: ثلاثة أيام] (3)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r13.claim: Other accounts say the fish traveled with Jonah for six thousand years or took him to the lowest reaches of the seventh earth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r13.anchor: وقيل: إن الحوت ذهب به مسيرة ستة آلاف سنة. وقيل: بلغ به تخوم الأرض السابعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r14.claim: One account says Jonah repented in the fish’s belly, acknowledged his sin, vowed to worship no one else, and God released him by mercy.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r14.anchor: وراجع نفسه فقال: لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين، حين عصيتك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r15.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r15.claim: The preceding interpretations, in which Jonah left angry with his people or the king, better suit the standing of prophets.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r15.anchor: والتأويلات المتقدمة أولى بحال الأنبياء أنه ذهب مغاضبا لقومه أو للملك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r16.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r16.claim: The darknesses are those of night, sea, and the fish’s belly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p350/r16.anchor: ظلمة الليل وظلمة البحر وظلمة بطن الحوت، {أن لا إله إلا أنت

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r1.claim: Dhu al-Nūn, the companion of the whale, is Jonah son of Mattā.

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r2.claim: Frustrated by prolonged resistance, Jonah left before being commanded or before the threatened punishment was due; the people repented, but he did not know and thought they had deceived him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r2.anchor: لما برم بطول دعوتهم وشدة شكيمتهم وتمادي إصرارهم مهاجرا عنهم، قبل أن يؤمر

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r3.claim: The form may intensify anger, or mean he angered his people by leaving, since they feared punishment would follow.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r3.anchor: وهو من بناء المغالبة للمبالغة أو لأنه أغضبهم بالمهاجرة لخوفهم لحوق العذاب عندها

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r4.anchor: وقرىء «مغضبا». { فظن أن لن نقدر عليه }

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r5.claim: The phrase may mean God would not constrict Jonah or decree punishment for him; an intensive reading supports the latter.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r5.anchor: لن نضيق عليه أو لن نقضي عليه بالعقوبة من القدر

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r6.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r6.claim: Another view treats it as a comparison to one who thinks he can flee God's decree by leaving without waiting for God's order, or as a fleeting satanic thought hyperbolically called a supposition.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r6.anchor: وقيل هو تمثيل لحاله بحال من ظن أن لن نقدر عليه في مراغمته قومه

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r7.speaker: يعقوب
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r7.claim: Other readings use yāʾ, a passive construction by Yaʿqūb, and a doubled consonant in that form.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r7.anchor: وقرىء بالياء وقرأ يعقوب على البناء للمفعول وقرىء به مثقلا

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r8.claim: The darkness may be exceptionally dense, or the three dark places of the whale's belly, sea and night.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r8.anchor: في الظلمة الشديدة المتكاثفة أو ظلمات بطن الحوت والبحر والليل

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r9.claim: Jonah confesses that none but God is divine.

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r10.claim: God is exalted above any incapacity; nothing can defeat Him.

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r11.claim: Jonah wronged himself by leaving hastily before receiving God's command.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r11.anchor: بالمبادرة إلى المهاجرة. وعن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r12.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:87/r12.claim: The Prophet says no distressed person who invokes God with this supplication fails to have it answered.

BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r1.claim: To understand a Qur'anic word, begin with Arabic as the Qur'an's language and seek its original lexical sense across concrete and figurative uses.
BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r1.anchor: فنلتمس الدلالة اللغوية الأصيلة الى تعطينا حس العربية للمادة فى ختلف

BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r2.claim: Determine a word's Qur'anic nuance by surveying its forms throughout the Qur'an and considering its local verse and surah contexts and its broader Qur'anic context.
BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r2.anchor: وتدبر سياقها الخاص فى الآية والسورة

BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r3.claim: Interpret expression through the context of the clear scripture and accept exegetical views only when its text can bear them.
BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r3.anchor: وتعرض عليه أقوال المفسرين فتقبل منها ما يقبله النص

BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r4.claim: Reject interpolated Israelite material, sectarian bias, and innovations in interpretation as intrusions on exegesis.
BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r4.anchor: ونتحاشى ما أقحم على كتب التفسير من مدسوس الإسرائيليات

BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r5.claim: Use the Arabic Qur'an as the authority for syntactic parsing and rhetorical analysis; assess grammarians' and rhetoricians' rules against it rather than forcing the text to fit them.
BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r5.anchor: نعرض عليه قواعد النحويين والبلاغيين ولا نعرضه عليها

BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r6.claim: The Qur'an is the authenticated summit of Arabic eloquence, not a text of poetic necessity that can be subjected to the loose interpretations sometimes allowed for poetic evidence.
BINTSHATI:v1pdf11/r6.anchor: إذ القرآن هو الذروة العليا فى نقاء أصالته وفيا بيانه

BINTSHATI:v2p8/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p8/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p8/r1.claim: A Qur'anic word may receive a particular sense from its many lexical possibilities, or acquire an additional nuance from its context.
BINTSHATI:v2p8/r1.anchor: ثم يكون للنص بعد ذلك أن يحدد لكل لفظ دلالته الخاصة، من شتى الدلالات المعجمية، أو يضيف إليها ملحظاً ينفرد به

BINTSHATI:v2p8/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p8/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p8/r2.claim: Calling a sense or form specifically Qur'anic does not invalidate other dictionary meanings or other forms known in eloquent Arabic; it identifies the Qur'an's distinctive diction.
BINTSHATI:v2p8/r2.anchor: والقول بدلالة خاصة للكلمة القرآنية، لا يعني تخطئة سائر الدلالات المعجمية، كما أن إيثار القرآن لصيغة بعينها

BINTSHATI:v2p8/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p8/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p8/r3.claim: Inductively observed rhetorical and stylistic features need not be forced under grammarians' and rhetoricians' rules; those rules should be tested against the Qur'an's higher expression.
BINTSHATI:v2p8/r3.anchor: والأمر كذلك فيما يهدى إليه الاستقراء من وجوه بيانية وظواهر أسلوبية، تقدمها منه دون أن نخشى فيها مخالفة لبعض قواعد النحويين

BINTSHATI:v2p8/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p8/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p8/r4.claim: The author calls for reassessing school grammar and rhetorical rules through inductive reflection on the Qur'an, accepts commentators only where text and context support them, and flags strained or sectarian and Israelite intrusions.
BINTSHATI:v2p8/r4.anchor: كما ننتفع بجهود المفسرين حين نعرض أقوالهم على القرآن الكريم، فنقبل منها ما يحتمله نصاً وسياقاً

BINTSHATI:v2p8/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p8/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p8/r5.claim: Reports on occasions of revelation matter for understanding the circumstances accompanying a verse, while the author signals a qualification about statements from Companions who witnessed the revelation.
BINTSHATI:v2p8/r5.anchor: أولاهما: أن المرويات في أسباب النزول موضع اعتبار

BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r27.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r27.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r27.claim: Jonah left angry with his people and departed without waiting for God's specific permission to emigrate.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r27.anchor: اي على هيئة الغاضب لقومه بالهجرة عنهم , ولربه بالخروج عنهم دون الانتظار لإذن خاص منه بالهجرة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r28.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r28.speaker: الحسن
BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r28.claim: Biqaʿi prefers al-Hasan's explanation that Jonah thought God would not punish him for this sin, a figurative expression of the consequence by its cause.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r28.anchor: وروي عن الحسن أن معنى { فظن أن لن نقدر عليه } أن لن نعاقبه بهذا الذنب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r29.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r29.speaker: مجاهد
BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r29.claim: Mujahid is reported to give the same explanation as al-Hasan: Jonah thought he would not be punished for his departure.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r29.anchor: رواه البهيقي في كتاب الأسماء والصفات عن قتادة عنه وعن مجاهد مثله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r30.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r30.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r30.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to explain the phrase as Jonah thinking God would not decree punishment for him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r30.anchor: من غير طريق عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما معناه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r31.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r31.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r31.claim: An alternate report from Ibn Abbas through al-Asbahani explains the phrase as thinking God would not constrict his departure.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r31.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما معناه , وكذا قال الأصبهاني عنه أن معناه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r32.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r32.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r32.claim: The constriction explanation derives from q-d-r meaning tightness, rather than q-d-r meaning ability.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p103/r32.anchor: من القدر الذي معناه الضيق , لا من القدرة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r1.speaker: الفراء
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r1.claim: Al-Farra says the verb has a doubled reading and can mean to decree or determine.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r1.anchor: وروى البهيقي أيضا عن الفراء نقدر بمعنى نقدر - مشددا وبحكم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r2.speaker: أبو صخر الهذلي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r2.claim: A line by Abu Sakhr al-Hudhali uses nقدر in support of the reported sense of determining or decreeing.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r2.anchor: وأنشد عن ابن الأنباري عن أبي صخر الهذلي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r3.claim: God admonished Jonah until he surrendered and cast himself into the sea; the whale swallowed him and descended to the sea floor, while God kept Jonah from becoming its food.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r3.anchor: فاقتضت حكمتنا أن عاتبناه حتى استسلم فألقى نفسه في البحر فالتقمه الحوت

BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir transmits from Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, and others that Jonah's darknesses were the whale's belly, the deep sea, and night.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r4.anchor: فهي ظلمات ثلاث - نقله ابن كثير عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس وغيرهما رضي الله عنهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r5.claim: Jonah first affirms God's exclusive divinity, then declares Him free of every imperfection; only God can rescue him from such a plight.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r5.anchor: أي تنزهت عن كل نقص , فلا يقدر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r6.claim: Jonah confesses that he wronged himself by leaving his people before permission and asks forgiveness, as a powerful person is expected to pardon.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r6.anchor: في خروجي من بين قومي فبل الإذن

BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r8.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r8.claim: Al-Razi says every person seeking refuge with God should begin with monotheism, then glorification and praise, then confession, seeking forgiveness, and apology; this is the proper order for every supplication.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p105/r8.anchor: وقال الرازي في اللوامع : وشرط كل من يلتجىء إلى الله

DURR-FULL:v5p664/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jonah left angry at his people; he thought God would not decree punishment or trial for his angry departure, and his punishment was the whale taking him.
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وذا النون إذ ذهب مغاضبا} يقول: غضب على قومه

DURR-FULL:v5p664/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r4.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says Jonah went away angry with his people.
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله: {وذا النون إذ ذهب مغاضبا} قال: مغاضبا لقومه

DURR-FULL:v5p664/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r5.speaker: عمرو بن قيس
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r5.claim: Amr ibn Qays says there could be several prophets under one leading prophet, and Jonah was angry with that prophet after the latter was told to send him to a people.
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r5.anchor: عن عمرو بن قيس قال: كانت تكون أنبياء جميعا يكون عليهم واحد فكان يوحى إلى ذلك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v5p664/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jonah thought he would not be overtaken by the punishment that in fact befell him.
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {فظن أن لن نقدر عليه} قال: ظن أن لن يأخذه العذاب الذي أصابه

DURR-FULL:v5p664/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r7.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says Jonah fled like a runaway and thought he would not be punished; his prior good works were a credit through which God caught up with him.
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r7.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله: {إذ ذهب مغاضبا} قال: انطلق آبقا {فظن أن لن نقدر عليه} فكان له سلف من عمل صالح

DURR-FULL:v5p664/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r8.claim: Mujahid says Jonah thought God would not punish him for this.
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {فظن أن لن نقدر عليه} قال: ظن أن لن نعاقبه بذلك

DURR-FULL:v5p664/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r9.speaker: عطية
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r9.claim: Atiyya glosses the phrase as Jonah thinking God would not decree punishment for him.
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r9.anchor: عن عطية في قوله: {فظن أن لن نقدر عليه} قال: أن لن نقضي عليه

DURR-FULL:v5p664/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r10.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak says Jonah thought God would decree no punishment or trial for his anger at and departure from his people.
DURR-FULL:v5p664/r10.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله: {فظن أن لن نقدر عليه}

DURR-FULL:v5p666/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن الحارث
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r1.claim: When the whale swallowed Jonah and cast him to the earth's depths, he heard the earth glorifying God, which prompted his own invocation.
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الحارث قال: لما التقم الحوت يونس نبذ به إلى قرار الأرض فسمع تسبيح الأرض فذاك الذي حاجه فناداه

DURR-FULL:v5p666/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r2.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r2.claim: Al-Hasan glosses qadara as punishment and identifies the darknesses as night, sea, and the whale's belly.
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r2.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله: {فظن أن لن نقدر عليه} قال: ظن أن لن نعاقبه {فنادى في الظلمات} قال: ظلمة الليل

DURR-FULL:v5p666/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r3.speaker: الملائكة
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r3.claim: The angels recognize the invocation as a familiar voice coming from a strange land.
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r3.anchor: قال الملائكة: صوت معروف في أرض غريبة

DURR-FULL:v5p666/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r4.speaker: قتادة والكلبي
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r4.claim: Qatada and al-Kalbi understand the phrase as Jonah thinking God would not decree punishment for him.
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r4.anchor: عن قتادة والكلبي {فظن أن لن نقدر عليه} قالا: ظن أن لن نقضي عليه العقوبة

DURR-FULL:v5p666/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the three darknesses as night, sea, and the whale's belly.
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {فنادى في الظلمات} قال: ظلمة الليل وظلمة البحر وظلمة بطن الحوت

DURR-FULL:v5p666/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب، عمرو بن ميمون، قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Amr ibn Maymun, and Qatada give the same three darknesses: night, sea, and whale's belly.
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r6.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب وعمرو بن ميمون وقتادة مثله

DURR-FULL:v5p666/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r7.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr is also reported to give the same explanation of the three darknesses.

DURR-FULL:v5p666/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r8.claim: Ibn Masud names the darknesses as night, the whale's belly, and the sea.
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r8.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه {فنادى في الظلمات} قال: ظلمة الليل وظلمة بطن الحوت وظلمة البحر

DURR-FULL:v5p666/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r9.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r9.claim: God ordered one fish not to harm Jonah's flesh or bones; after another fish swallowed it, Jonah called from the darkness of one fish, then the second, then the sea.
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r9.anchor: عن سالم بن أبي الجعد قال: أوحى الله تعالى إلى الحوت أن: لا تضر له لحما ولا عظما ثم ابتلع الحوت حوت آخر

DURR-FULL:v5p666/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r10.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak says tasbih means prayer throughout the Qur'an except in Jonah's words here.
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r10.anchor: عن الضحاك قال: كل تسبيح في القرآن صلاة إلا قوله: {سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين}

DURR-FULL:v5p666/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r11.claim: Answering Muawiya, Ibn Abbas says Jonah thought his sin would not reach the point of punishment, while never doubting that God could punish him if He willed.
DURR-FULL:v5p666/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن معاوية قال له يوما: إني قد ضربتني أمواج القرآن البارحة في آيتين لم أعرف تأويلهما

DURR-FULL:v5p667/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p667/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p667/r1.claim: Jonah announced that punishment would come in the morning; his people gathered their children and young animals, pleaded and wept, and God relented and turned the punishment away.
DURR-FULL:v5p667/r1.anchor: ن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: لما دعا يونس قومه أوحى الله إليه أن العذاب يصبحهم

DURR-FULL:v5p667/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p667/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p667/r2.claim: After the punishment was averted, Jonah left angrily, boarded a ship, and was cast into the sea when lots fell on him for a third time.
DURR-FULL:v5p667/r2.anchor: ن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: لما دعا يونس قومه أوحى الله إليه أن العذاب يصبحهم

DURR-FULL:v5p667/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p667/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p667/r3.claim: God sent a fish called al-Najm to carry Jonah as a prisoner through the seas, not as food, and commanded it not to injure his skin or break his bones.
DURR-FULL:v5p667/r3.anchor: ن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: لما دعا يونس قومه أوحى الله إليه أن العذاب يصبحهم

DURR-FULL:v5p667/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p667/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p667/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the whale took Jonah to the seventh earth; hearing the earth's glorification stirred him to supplicate, and he emerged hairless and without nails, sheltered and fed beneath a tree whose leaves later dried.
DURR-FULL:v5p667/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: لما التقم الحوت يونس ذهب به حتى أوقفه بالأرض السابعة فسمع تسبيح الأرض

DURR-FULL:v5p668/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p668/r1.speaker: الله تعالى
DURR-FULL:v5p668/r1.claim: In the continuing account, God rebukes Jonah for grieving over a withered tree but not over a hundred thousand or more people facing punishment.
DURR-FULL:v5p668/r1.anchor: فشكا ذلك إلى ربه فقال: تحزن على شجرة يبست ولا تحزن على مائة ألف أو يزيدون يعذبون

DURR-FULL:v5p668/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p668/r2.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v5p668/r2.claim: Anas transmits a Prophetic report: Jonah's prayer rose to the Throne, the angels recognized his familiar voice in a strange land and appealed to his past worship, so God ordered the fish to cast him ashore and caused a gourd to grow over him.
DURR-FULL:v5p668/r2.anchor: عن أنس رفعه: أن يونس حين بدا له أن يدعو الله بالكلمات حين ناداه في بطن الحوت قال: اللهم {لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين}

DURR-FULL:v5p668/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p668/r3.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v5p668/r3.claim: Ali transmits a Prophetic warning that no servant should claim to be better than Jonah, who glorified God in the darknesses.
DURR-FULL:v5p668/r3.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه مرفوعا: ليس لعبد أن يقول أنا خير من يونس بن متى سبح الله في الظلمات

DURR-FULL:v5p668/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p668/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p668/r4.claim: The Prophet says no Muslim has called on God with Jonah's prayer for any matter without receiving a response.
