DURR-FULL:v5p668/r4.anchor: عن سعد بن أبي وقاص رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: دعوة ذي النون إذ هو في بطن الحوت

DURR-FULL:v5p668/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p668/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p668/r5.claim: The Prophet says Jonah's invocation is for Jonah and for believers who use it; the promise to save believers in 21:88 is God's condition for anyone who calls upon Him with it.
DURR-FULL:v5p668/r5.anchor: عن سعد رضي الله عنه: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: اسم الله الذي دعي به أجاب وإذا سئل به أعطى

DURR-FULL:v5p668/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p668/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p668/r6.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra calls this invocation a refuge for the prophets and says Jonah called it in the darkness of the whale's belly.
DURR-FULL:v5p668/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: هذه الآية مفزع للأنبياء

DURR-FULL:v5p669/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r1.claim: Al-Hasan identifies Jonah's prayer as God's greatest name, by which a caller is answered and a petitioner is given what he asks.
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r1.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه قال: اسم الله الأعظم الذي إذا دعي به أجاب وإذا سئل به أعطى

DURR-FULL:v5p669/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r2.claim: A report from Sa'd says a Muslim who invokes the greatest name in this prayer forty times while ill and dies receives a martyr's reward; if he recovers, he is forgiven.
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r2.anchor: عن سعد بن أبي وقاص رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: هل أدلكم على اسم الله الأعظم دعاء يونس

DURR-FULL:v5p669/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophet's statement that whoever says he is better than Jonah son of Matta has lied.
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: من قال أنا خير من يونس بن متى فقد كذب

DURR-FULL:v5p669/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet describing Jonah at a mountain pass, riding a camel with a fiber halter and wearing a wool garment while saying the pilgrimage response.
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مر على ثنية فقال: ما هذه

DURR-FULL:v5p669/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet forbade claiming superiority over Jonah son of Matta, explaining that Jonah sinned and then his Lord chose him.
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: لا ينبغي لأحد أن يقول أنا خير من يونس بن متى

DURR-FULL:v5p669/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r6.claim: Ibn Masud transmits the Prophet's warning that none should say they are better than Jonah son of Matta.
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r6.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: لا يقولن أحدكم أنا خير من يونس بن متى

DURR-FULL:v5p669/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r7.claim: Abu Hurayra also transmits the Prophet's warning that none should claim to be better than Jonah son of Matta.
DURR-FULL:v5p669/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: لا ينبغي لأحد أن يقول أنا خير من يونس بن متى

BURSEVI:v5p394/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p394/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p394/r1.claim: Affliction hastens punishment for idolaters and unbelievers, but for patient believers it raises their rank, erases sins, and transforms their base being; patience and gratitude are called for in both good and adversity.
BURSEVI:v5p394/r1.anchor: بل هو في حقهم تعجيل لعذابهم وفي حق المؤمنين الصابرين تكميل لدرجاتهم وحط من خطيآتهم وإكسير لنحاس وجودهم

BURSEVI:v5p394/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p394/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p394/r2.claim: The author cites Masnavi verses calling patience a rare alchemy and key to relief, urging gratitude for good and ill, and counseling patience because every blessing is paired with sorrow.
BURSEVI:v5p394/r2.anchor: صد هزاران كيميا حق آفريد كيميايى همو صبر آدم نديد

BURSEVI:v5p394/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p394/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p394/r3.claim: Dhu al-Nun, the one associated with the fish, is the prophet Yunus ibn Matta; the author vocalizes Matta with an open mīm and doubled, open tāʾ.
BURSEVI:v5p394/r3.anchor: {وذا النون} أي : واذكر صاحب النون أي : الحوت والمراد يونس بن متى

BURSEVI:v5p394/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p394/r4.speaker: جامع الأصول
BURSEVI:v5p394/r4.claim: Jami al-Usul says Matta was the name of Yunus's mother.
BURSEVI:v5p394/r4.anchor: قيل : هو اسم أم يونس كذا في "جامع الأصول"

BURSEVI:v5p394/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p394/r5.speaker: عطاء
BURSEVI:v5p394/r5.claim: Atā asked Kaʿb whether Matta was Yunus's father or mother; Kaʿb said it was his father's name and that his mother Badura descended from Aaron.
BURSEVI:v5p394/r5.anchor: قال عطاء : سألت كعبا عن متى أهو اسم أبيه أم أمه فقال : اسم أبيه

BURSEVI:v5p394/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p394/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p394/r6.claim: Yunus was called Dhu al-Nun because the fish swallowed him.
BURSEVI:v5p394/r6.anchor: وسمي يونس بذي النون لأنه ابتلعه الحوت

BURSEVI:v5p394/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p394/r7.speaker: السهيلي
BURSEVI:v5p394/r7.claim: Al-Suhayli says Dhu al-Nun is more honorific than companion of the fish in a passage praising Yunus; dhu makes the following noun principal, and nun is nobler than hut because it is an alphabet letter appearing at a surah's opening.
BURSEVI:v5p394/r7.anchor: قال الإمام السهيلي أضافه هنا إلى النون وقد قال في سورة القلم

BURSEVI:v5p394/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p394/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p394/r8.claim: The verse commands recalling Yunus's departure in anger from the people of Nineveh near Mosul, after their long resistance to his preaching; he emigrated before being ordered to do so.
BURSEVI:v5p394/r8.anchor: أي : اذكر خبره وقت ذهابه حال كونه {مغاضبا} مراغما لقومه

BURSEVI:v5p394/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p394/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p394/r9.claim: The form of the verb conveys the completeness and intensity of Yunus's anger.
BURSEVI:v5p394/r9.anchor: وبناء المفاعلة للدلالة على كمال غضبه والمبالغة فيه

BURSEVI:v5p394/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p394/r10.speaker: نجم الدين
BURSEVI:v5p394/r10.claim: An alternative account says Yunus warned his people of a fixed-time punishment and left; after they repented and punishment was averted, he thought they had made him a liar and departed angry. Najm al-Din's account is preferred by people of certainty.
BURSEVI:v5p394/r10.anchor: وهذا القول أنسب بتقرير الشيخ نجم الدين في "تأويلاته"

BURSEVI:v5p394/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p394/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p394/r11.claim: Here naqdir means constrain, not be unable: Arabic uses the verb for restricting one's household, and Yunus's state is presented as though he thought God would not constrict him.
BURSEVI:v5p394/r11.anchor: لن نضيق عليه الأمر يقال قدر على عياله قدرا ضيق

BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r1.claim: The Najmiyya reading says intense anger clouds judgment and veils faith's light, so one may think something unworthy of God, even if a prophet; Muhammad's strength was to speak only truth in anger and calm.
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r1.anchor: في "التأويلات النجمية" يشير إلى أن الإنسان إذا استولى عليه الغضب يلتبس عليه عقله

BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r2.claim: The author adds that God's grace toward sinful servants means He reproves prophets for wishing punishment on their people or disliking its removal, and wants them to seek forgiveness for them.
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r2.anchor: وفيه إشارة أخرى وهي أن الله تعالى من كمال فضله وكرمه على عباده وإن كانوا عصاة

BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r3.claim: A report says Yunus boarded a ship that stopped at sea; the sailors drew lots three times and chose him each time, so he confessed, threw himself overboard, and was swallowed by a fish that God commanded not to harm him but to hold him as a prisoner.
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r3.anchor: روي أنه حين خرج مغاضبا أتى بحر الروم فوجد قوما هيأوا السفينة فركب معهم

BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r4.claim: The fā in fanādā is explanatory: the omitted events of the lots and the fish's swallowing occurred, then Yunus called out.
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r4.anchor: الفاء فصيحة أي : فكان ما كان من القرعة والتقام الحوت

BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r5.claim: The darknesses may be one overwhelming darkness or the combined darknesses of the fish's belly, the sea, and the night.
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r5.anchor: في الظلمة الشديدة المتكافئة أو في ظلمات بطن الحوت والبحر والليل

BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r6.speaker: السمرقندي
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r6.claim: Al-Samarqandi suggests the darknesses came from six directions, like a Prophetic report about a person surrounded by darkness in front, behind, on both sides, above, and below.
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r6.anchor: وقال الشيخ السمرقندي في تفسيره وعندي والله أعلم أن تلك الظلمات كانت من الجهات الست

BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r7.claim: A Prophetic report describes a member of the community enclosed in six directions of darkness and bewildered.
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r7.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام : "ورأيت رجلا من أمتي من بين يديه ظلمة

BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p394#2/r8.claim: An means that Yunus called out by declaring that there is no god but God.

BURSEVI:v5p395/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p395/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p395/r1.claim: The Najmiyya reading likens the noble spirit cast into worldly life to Yunus swallowed by the whale of the commanding soul; by God's command the soul must not harm it, serving instead as its enclosure and prison.
BURSEVI:v5p395/r1.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" يشير إلى أن الروح الشريف إذا ألقي في بحر الدنيا

BURSEVI:v5p395/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p395/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p395/r2.claim: The spirit's rare safety from the soul's harm is like Yunus's safety in the fish; in the darkness of soul, body, and world, it calls on God alone to preserve it and inspire remembrance.
BURSEVI:v5p395/r2.anchor: ومن سلامة الروح أن يناديه في ظلمة النفس وظلمة القالب وظلمة الدنيا

BURSEVI:v5p395/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p395/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p395/r3.claim: Yunus declares God above incapacity and recognizes that his affliction did not occur without a cause on his own part.
BURSEVI:v5p395/r3.anchor: أنزهك تنزيها لائقا بك من أن يعجزك شيء وأن يكون ابتلائي هذا بغير سبب من جهتي

BURSEVI:v5p395/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p395/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p395/r4.claim: The Najmiyya interpretation says Yunus declared God free of injustice toward him, even though God creates human acts.
BURSEVI:v5p395/r4.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : نزهه عن الظلم عليه وإن كان فعله بخلق فيه كما قال تعالى :

BURSEVI:v5p395/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p395/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p395/r5.claim: Yunus ascribes wrongdoing to himself, acknowledging that he exposed himself to danger by hastily emigrating; this self-blame observes proper spiritual etiquette.
BURSEVI:v5p395/r5.anchor: ونسب الظلم إلى نفسه اعترافا واستحقاقا ورعاية للأدب فقال : {إني كنت من الظالمين}

BURSEVI:v5p395/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p395/r6.speaker: عرائس البقلى
BURSEVI:v5p395/r6.claim: Al-Baqli says God intended Yunus to have an ascent and witnessing in the fish's belly; there he saw, beneath the earth, what Muhammad saw above the Throne, became bewildered, and denied his mistaken thoughts of God.
BURSEVI:v5p395/r6.anchor: وفي "عرائس البقلى" قدس سره أن الله أراد ليونس معراجا ومشاهدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to say that King Hezekiah had five prophets, including Jonah, and selected Jonah for Nineveh; Jonah refused, citing other prophets, and left angry at the king.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r1.anchor: وقد روي عن ابن عباس أن ( حزقيال ) ملك إسرائيل كان في زمنه خمسة أنبياء منهم يونس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur calls the Hezekiah account remote from other Qur'anic passages and the books of the Israelites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r2.anchor: وهذا بعيد من القرآن في آيات أخرى ومن كتب بني إسرائيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r3.claim: The lesson of the verse does not depend on identifying the particular story behind Jonah's departure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r3.anchor: ومحل العبرة من الآية لا يتوقف على تعيين القصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r4.claim: The wording implies Jonah left without divine authorization, supposing that if he left the city to which he was sent, God would send someone else to its people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r4.anchor: يقتضي أنه خرج خروجا غير مأذون له فيه من الله . ظن أنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r5.claim: One reading takes naqdir as constrict or impose hardship; Jonah inferred that leaving would end his duty to remain with those people or deliver the message, but should have asked God what to do.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r5.anchor: أي ظن أن لن نضيق عليه تحتيم الإقامة مع القوم الذين أرسل إليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r6.claim: In al-Kashshaf, Muawiya asks Ibn Abbas whether a prophet could think God lacked power; Ibn Abbas answers that the word concerns restriction, not power.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس : هذا من القدر لا من القدرة ) . يعني التضييق عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r7.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك والكلبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r7.claim: They explain naqdir as decree or hold accountable, from divine power; this is also transmitted from Ibn Abbas, and al-Farra and al-Zajjaj prefer it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r7.anchor: ونقل هذا عن مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك والكلبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r8.claim: On the decree or accountability reading, Jonah made an erroneous judgment when he left without permission.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r8.anchor: وعلى هذا يكون يونس اجتهد وأخطأ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r9.claim: On this account, the thought arose as a hasty impulse of anger after departure, before Jonah considered its implications and consequences; reports say he was naturally narrow-chested.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p131/r9.anchor: الخروج منه بادرة بدافع الغضب عن غير تأمل في لوازمه وعواقبه ، قالوا : وكان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r1.speaker: سليمان بن المعتمر أو أبو المعتمر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r1.claim: A reading or interpretation supplies an omitted interrogative hamza: Did he think God would not constrain him? Mundhir ibn Sa'id says it was read this way.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r1.anchor: ونسب إلى سليمان بن المعتمر أو أبي المعتمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur offers the possibility that inside the whale Jonah thought God would not rescue him because escape seemed impossible under ordinary conditions; on this account the thought followed being swallowed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r2.anchor: أنه ظن وهو في جوف الحوت أن الله غير مخلصه في بطن الحوت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r3.claim: Alternatively, Jonah expected by ordinary causes to emigrate from his people's land and did not expect God to obstruct him, since no revelation had previously forbidden it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r3.anchor: أنه ظن بحسب الأسباب المعتادة أنه يهاجر من دار قومه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r4.claim: Jonah's call is repentance for negligence, haste, or mistaken judgment, and his statement magnifies his confession of self-wrongdoing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r4.anchor: فذلك توبة صدرت منه عن تقصيره أو عجلته أو خطأ اجتهاده ، ولذلك قال : { إني كنت من الظالمين }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r5.claim: The verb for being and the phrasing that places Jonah among wrongdoers present the quality as firmly rooted, strengthening his self-accusation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r5.anchor: فأسند إليه فعل الكون الدال على رسوخ الوصف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r6.claim: Inni functions as an explanatory clause for the verb of calling.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r7.claim: Leading with acknowledgment of God's oneness and glorification signifies that God alone governs and has power over everything.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r7.anchor: وتقديمه الاعتراف بالتوحيد مع التسبيح كنى به عن انفراد الله تعالى بالتدبير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r8.claim: The plural darknesses refers to the darkness of night, the ocean depths, and the whale's belly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r8.anchor: والمراد ظلمة الليل ، وظلمة قعر البحر ، وظلمة بطن الحوت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r9.claim: Another explanation treats the plural as an intensifier for profound darkness, as in the Qur'anic movement from darknesses into light.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p132/r9.anchor: وقيل : الظلمات مبالغة في شدة الظلمة كقوله تعالى : { يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور }

BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r1.claim: Yunus describes himself as unjust regarding God's majesty: his own description cannot do justice to the majesty of divine oneness.
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r1.anchor: في وصف جلالك إذ وصفي لا يليق بعزة وحدانيتك

BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r2.claim: The Prophet's confession that he cannot enumerate God's praise explains Yunus's modest confession.
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r2.anchor: سيد المرسلين حيث قال : "لا أحصي ثناء عليك أنت كما أثنيت على نفسك"

BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r3.claim: The Prophet said, Do not prefer me over my brother Yunus.
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r3.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "لا تفضلوني على أخي يونس"

BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r4.claim: After experiencing this state, Yunus feared he would not regain what he had attained in the world, became distressed when the Real was veiled from him, and called for rescue.
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r4.anchor: فغاب الحق عنه فاهتم ودعا بالنجاة

BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r7.claim: A hadith promises that any distressed person who calls with this supplication will be answered.
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r7.anchor: "ما من مكروب يدعو بهذا الدعاء إلا استجيب له"

BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says Yunus was saved only through his own admission of wrongdoing.
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r8.anchor: وعن الحسن ما نجاه والله إلا إقراره على نفسه بالظلم

BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r9.speaker: النبي ﷺ
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r9.claim: The Prophet identifies this confession of God's oneness as the greatest name: invoking it brings an answer and asking by it brings a gift.
BURSEVI:v5p395#2/r9.anchor: وفي "صحيح المستدرك" قال عليه السلام : "اسم الله الأعظم الذي إذا دعى به أجاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r1.claim: Dhu al-Nūn means the companion of the whale, Jonah son of Mattā, the prophet from Nineveh, named for the fish that swallowed him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r1.anchor: والنون الحوت وصاحبه يونس بن متى عليه السلام، ونسب إلى الحوت الذي التقمه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r2.claim: The Prophet warned against claiming superiority over Jonah son of Mattā, and in another report against claiming superiority over Moses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r2.anchor: «من قال إني خير من يونس بن متى فقد كذب» ، وفي حديث آخر «لا ينبغي لأحد أن يقول أنا خير من يونس بن متى» ، وهذا الحديث وقوله «لا تفضلوني على موسى»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r3.claim: One reconciliation says the Prophet's declaration that he is the chief of Adam's descendants came later, when God had informed him of that rank.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r3.anchor: أحدهما ذكره الناس وهو أن يكون قوله «أنا سيد ولد آدم» متأخرا في التاريخ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers that the prohibition reflects humility and avoids angering Jews, rather than denying the Prophet's enduring rank as chief of humanity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r4.anchor: والوجه الثاني وهو عندي أحرى مع حال النبي عليه السلام، أنه إنما نهي عن التفضيل بين شخصين مذكورين وذهب مذهب التواضع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r5.claim: The context was a Jew's oath that God favored Moses; an Anṣārī objected and slapped him, the dispute escalated, and the Prophet prohibited ranking himself above Moses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r5.anchor: وسبب الحديث يقتضي هذا، وذلك أن يهوديا قال لا والذي فضل موسى على العالمين، فقال له رجل من الأنصار تقول هذا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r6.claim: The Prophet's warning not to rank himself above Jonah protects against inferring that Jonah lacked merit from his ordeal; a general declaration of his own rank is compatible with that warning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r6.anchor: ونهى عليه السلام عن تفضيله على يونس لئلا يظن أحد بيونس نقص فضيلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r7.claim: A third prophetic report says not to rank the prophets against one another; ʿUmar told al-Ḥuṭayʾa to praise his patron without preferring people over others.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96/r7.anchor: وقوله في حديث ثالث «لا تفضلوا بين الأنبياء» . وهذا كله مع قوله «أنا سيد ولد آدم»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96#2/r1.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96#2/r1.claim: One view says Jonah left in anger at his people after their delay and obstinacy, despite God's command that he stay and patiently continue calling them; leaving that command was his fault.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96#2/r1.anchor: قيل إنه غاضب قومه حين طال عليه أمرهم وتعنتهم فذهب فارا بنفسه وقد كان الله تعالى أمره بملازمتهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96#2/r2.claim: A report portrays Jonah as a young prophet unable to bear prophecy's burden, like a young camel collapsing under its load; the Prophet was told to be patient like the companion of the whale.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96#2/r2.anchor: وروي أنه كان شابا فلم يحمل أثقال النبوءة وتفسخ تحتها كما يتفسخ الربع تحت الحمل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96#2/r3.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96#2/r3.claim: Another group says Jonah was angry with the king who ruled his people, a view that carries a similar implication for Jonah.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96#2/r3.anchor: وقالت فرقة إنما غاضب الملك الذي كان على قومه ع وهذا نحو من الأول فيما يلحق منه يونس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96#2/r4.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan and others say Jonah left angry with his Lord and was driven on by Satan; the author regards this account as plainly unsound and incompatible with a prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96#2/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن وغيره إنما ذهب مغاضبا ربه واستفزه إبليس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96#2/r5.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96#2/r5.claim: In their report, Jonah announced a date for his people's punishment; they repented together, God lifted it, and Jonah departed believing they had made him a liar.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p96#2/r5.anchor: فلما كان سحر ذلك اليوم قام يونس فرحل فأيقنوا بالعذاب فخرجوا بأجمعهم إلى البراز

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r1.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r1.claim: The account says Jonah swore never to return because his people supposedly killed liars, then left by ship; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects the account as weak and unsuitable for a prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r1.anchor: إليهم أبدا. وروي أنه كان من دينهم قتل الكذاب فغضب حينئذ على ربه وخرج على وجهه حتى دخل في سفينة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects the account of Jonah's anger at God as manifestly weak and unsuitable for a prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r2.anchor: وفي هذا القول من الضعف ما لا خفاء به مما لا يتصف به نبي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r3.claim: The compressed narrative skips ahead: Jonah entered the sea, was swallowed by a fish, and found himself in its belly's darkness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r3.anchor: المعنى فدخل البحر وكذا حتى التقمه الحوت وصار في ظلمة جوفه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r4.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r4.claim: One group says Satan misled Jonah into thinking God might be unable to punish him; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects this view.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r4.anchor: فقالت فرقة استزله إبليس ووقع في ظنه إمكان أن لا يقدر الله عليه بمعاقبة ع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r5.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r5.claim: Another group takes naqdira to mean constrain: Jonah thought God would not restrict his course, using the sense found in 17:30.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r5.anchor: وقالت فرقة ظن أن لن يضيق عليه في مذهبه من قوله تعالى: يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r6.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r6.claim: A separate group derives the phrase from qadar and understands it as Jonah thinking God would not decree punishment for him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r6.anchor: وقالت فرقة هو من القدر، أي ظن أن لن يقدر الله عليه بعقوبة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r7.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r7.claim: Another group reads the clause as a question: did he suppose God would not punish him?
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r7.anchor: وقالت فرقة الكلام بمعنى الاستفهام، أي أفظن أن لن يقدر الله عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r8.speaker: منذر بن سعيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r8.claim: Munḏir ibn Saʿīd reports that some read the clause with an interrogative hamza: afa-ẓanna.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r8.anchor: وحكى منذر بن سعيد أن بعضهم قرأ «أفظن» بالألف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r9.speaker: الزهري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r9.claim: Al-Zuhrī reads taqdir with a ḍamma on the nūn and a doubled dāl.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r9.anchor: وقرأ الزهري «تقدر» بضم النون وفتح القاف وشد الدال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r10.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads yaqdir; another reading from him is naqdir.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r11.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r11.claim: One group counts the darknesses as night, sea, and whale.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r11.anchor: فقالت فرقة ظلمة الليل وظلمة البحر وظلمة الحوت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r12.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r12.claim: Another group counts sea and whale darknesses; the plural could also refer to the many dark regions inside a single whale, as in 12:10.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r12.anchor: وقالت فرقة ظلمة البحر وظلمة الحوت التقم الحوت الأول الذي التقم يونس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r13.claim: A report says Jonah prostrated in the whale after hearing the fish glorify God at the sea floor and prayed that he had made a mosque where none before him had.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r13.anchor: وروي أن يونس سجد في جوف الحوت حين سمع تسبيح الحيتان في قعر البحر ثم قال في دعائه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r14.claim: He calls an in the prayer an explanatory particle, comparing 38:6, but expresses reservation about that analysis.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r14.anchor: وأن مفسرة نحو قوله تعالى أن امشوا [ص: 6] وفي هذا نظر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r15.claim: The best reading of Jonah's confession is that he had erred by failing to persist with his people and patiently call them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p97/r15.anchor: من الظالمين يريد فيما خالف فيه من ترك مداومة قومه والصبر عليهم هذا أحسن الوجوه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r1.claim: The one called Dhu al-Nun is Jonah ibn Matta; al-nun means the fish, to which he is attached because it swallowed him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى وذا النون يعني يونس بن متى والنون السمكة أضيف إليها لابتلاعها إياه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba notes that the reciprocal form mufaʿala usually involves two parties but can apply to one, as in “traveled” or “approached”; it is used this way here.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة المغاضبة مفاعلة وأكثر المفاعلة من اثنين كالمناظرة والمجادلة والمخاصمة وربما تكون من واحد كقولك سافرت وشارفت الأمر وهي هاهنا من هذا الباب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r3.speaker: أبو المتوكل وأبو الجوزاء وعاصم الجحدري وابن السميفع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r3.claim: Abu al-Mutawakkil, Abu al-Jawza, ʿAsim al-Jahdari, and Ibn al-Sumayfa read maghḍaban, without the alif, with a still ghayn and fatḥa on ḍād.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو المتوكل وأبو الجوزاء وعاصم الجحدري وابن السميفع مغضبا باسكان الغين وفتح الضاد من غير ألف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jonah was angry with his people. In one account, he left angry at the prophet Shaʿya, the king, and his people after they pressed him to approach a conquering king about Israelite captives; the episode is expanded at 10:98.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r4.anchor: أحدهما أنه غضب على قومه قاله أبن عباس والضحاك وفي غضبه عليهم ثلاثة أقوال أحدها أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى بني نبي يقال له شعيا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says Jonah endured severe abuse and denial, then left before his people believed, frustrated and not expecting this act to bring punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r5.anchor: والثاني أنه عانى من قومه أمرا صعبا من الأذى والتكذيب فخرج عنهم قبل أن يؤمنوا ضجرلا وما ظن أن هذا الفعل نوجب عليه ما جرى من العقوبة ذكره ابن الأنباري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r6.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r6.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih reports that the burden of prophecy overwhelmed Jonah; unable to bear it, he cast it from his hand and fled.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r6.anchor: وقد روي عن وهب بن منبه قال لما حملت عليه أثقال النبوة ضاق بها ذرعا ولم يصبر فقذفها من يده وخرج هاربا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r7.claim: Another account says Jonah's people repented after he threatened punishment; when God lifted it and told him to return, he feared they would call him a liar and left resentfully. Ibn al-Jawzi also refers to 10:98.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r7.anchor: والثالث أنه لما أوعدهم العذاب فتابوا ورفع عنهم قيل له ارجع إليهم فقال كيف أرجع فيجدوني كاذبا فانصرف مغاضبا لقومه عاتبا على ربه وقد ذكرنا هذا في يونس 98

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r8.speaker: الحسن وسعيد بن جبير والشعبي وعروة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r8.claim: Al-Hasan, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Shaʿbi, and ʿUrwa give the alternative view that Jonah left angry with his Lord.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r8.anchor: والثاني أنه خرج مغاضبا لربه قاله الحسن وسعيد بن جبير والشعبي وعروة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r9.speaker: أبو بكر النقاش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r9.claim: Abu Bakr al-Naqqash says Jonah was angry for the sake of his Lord, because his people persisted in rebellion.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r9.anchor: وقال أبو بكر النقاش المعنى مغاضبا من أجل ربه وإنما غضب لأجل تمردهم وعصيانهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r10.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r10.claim: Ibn Qutayba says Jonah was exasperated by his people's denial and wanted punishment to befall them; God chastised him for disliking their being forgiven.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p381/r10.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة كان مغيظا عليهم لطول ما عاناه من تكذيبهم مشتهيا أن ينزل بهم فعاقبه الله على كراهيته العفو عن قومه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r1.speaker: يعقوب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r1.claim: Yaʿqub reads the verb with yāʾ, ḍamma, a doubled dāl, and fatḥa.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r1.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب يفدر بضم الياء وتشديد الدال وفتحها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وأبو الجوزاء وابن أبي ليلى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Abu al-Jawza, and Ibn Abi Layla read with yāʾ, a still qāf, and a light dāl with fatḥa.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r2.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير وأبو الجوزاء وابن أبي ليلى يقدر بياء مرفوعة مع سكون القاف وتخفيف الدال وفتحها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r3.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r3.claim: Abu ʿImran al-Jawni reads with yāʾ, a still qāf, and a light dāl with kasra.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمران الجوني يقدر بياء مفتوحة وسكون القاف وكسر الدال خفيفة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r4.speaker: الزهري وابن يعمر وحميد بن قيس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r4.claim: Al-Zuhri, Ibn Yaʿmar, and Humayd ibn Qays read with nūn, fatḥa on qāf, kasra on doubled dāl.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r4.anchor: وقرأ الزهري وابن يعمر وحميد بن قيس نقدر بنون مرفوعة وفتح القاف وكسر الدال وتشديدها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r5.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r5.claim: The first explanation is that Jonah thought God would not decree punishment for him; al-ʿAwfi transmits it from Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Dahhak also hold it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r5.anchor: أحدها أن لن نقضي عليه بالعقوبة رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس وبه قال مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r6.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r6.claim: Al-Farra explains qadara here as qaddara, to decree or measure out, as Arabs use the two forms alike.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r6.anchor: قال الفراء معنى الآية فظن أن لن نقدر عليه ما قدرنا من العقوبة والعرب تقول قدر بمعنى قدر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r7.speaker: أبو صخر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj adduces Abu Sakhr's verse as evidence for the sense “decree”: its phrase mā taqdir witnesses that usage.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r7.anchor: وهذا مذهب الزجاج والثاني فظن أن لن نضيق عليه قاله عطاء قال ابن قتيبة يقال فلان مقدر عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r8.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r8.claim: ʿAta gives a second sense: Jonah thought God would not constrain him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r8.anchor: والثاني فظن أن لن نضيق عليه قاله عطاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r9.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r9.claim: Ibn Qutayba says qadara can mean to constrict, as in the verse about God constricting someone's provision at 89:16.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r9.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة يقال فلان مقدر عليه ومقتر عليه ومنه قوله تعالى فقدر عليه رزقه الفجر 16

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r10.speaker: النقاش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r10.claim: Al-Naqqash explains that Jonah thought God had left him free to stay or depart, although God had not granted permission to leave.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r10.anchor: قال النقاش والمعنى فظن أن لن يضيق عليه الخروج فكأنه ظن أن الله قد وسع له إن شاء أن يقيم وإن شاء أن يخرج ولم يؤذن له في الخروج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r11.speaker: الحسن وابن زيد وسليمان التيمي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r11.claim: A third view, transmitted by ʿAwf from al-Hasan and also held by Ibn Zayd and Sulayman al-Taymi, is that Jonah thought he could escape God's power.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r11.anchor: والثالث أن المعنى فظن أنه يعجز ربه فلا يقدر عليه رواه عوف عن الحسن وقال ابن زيد وسليمان التيمي المعنى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r12.claim: The escape-from-power interpretation requires an omitted interrogative alif: “Did he think We could not overpower him?” Ibn al-Jawzi says this is the only plausible reading of that view.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r12.anchor: فعلى هذا الوجه يكون استفهاما قد حذفت ألفه وهذا الوجه يدل على أنه من القدرة ولا يتصور إلا مع تقدير الاستفهام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r13.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وقتادة والأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r13.claim: The darknesses are the darkness of the sea, the fish's belly, and the night, according to Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Qatada, and most interpreters.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r13.anchor: أحدها أنها ظلمة البحر وظلمة بطن الحوت وظلمة الليل قاله سعيد ابن جبير وقتادة والأكثرون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r14.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r14.claim: Salim ibn Abi al-Jaʿd says another fish swallowed the fish holding Jonah, creating the darknesses of one fish, then the other, then the sea.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r14.anchor: والثاني أن حوتا جاء فابتلع الحوت الذي هو في بطنه فنادى في ظلمة حوت ثم في ظلمة حوت ثم في ظلمة البحر قاله سالم ابن أبي الجعد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r15.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r15.claim: Ibn al-Saib identifies the darknesses as water, the fish's intestine, and its belly.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r15.anchor: والثالث أنها ظلمة الماء وظلمة معى السمكة وظلمة بطنها قاله ابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r16.speaker: رسول الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r16.claim: Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas reports that the Prophet said no distressed person utters Jonah's prayer without God relieving him; no grading is stated.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r16.anchor: وقد روى سعد بن أبي وقاص عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال إني لأعلم كلمة لا يقولها مكروب إلا فرج الله عنه كلمة أخي يونس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r17.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r17.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r17.claim: Al-Hasan says Jonah's prayer admits his sin and repents from his error.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p382/r17.anchor: قال الحسن وهذا اعتراف من يونس بذنبه وتوبة من خطيئته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir says the Jonah story also appears in al-Saffat and Nun; God sent Jonah son of Matta to Nineveh near Mosul, whose people rejected his call.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366/r1.anchor: وذلك أن يونس بن متى، عليه السلام، بعثه الله إلى أهل قرية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366/r2.claim: Jonah left his people angrily after warning them of punishment in three days; believing a prophet would not lie, they went into the wilderness with their children and herds, separated mothers and young, cried to God, and were spared, as in 10:98.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366/r2.anchor: فلما تحققوا منه ذلك، وعلموا أن النبي لا يكذب، خرجوا إلى الصحراء بأطفالهم وأنعامهم ومواشيهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366/r3.claim: Jonah sailed with others, and when they feared the vessel would sink, lots were drawn three times to choose someone to cast away; each time they fell on him, as in 37:141.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366/r3.anchor: فاقترعوا على رجل يلقونه من بينهم يتخففون منه، فوقعت القرعة على يونس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366/r4.claim: Ibn Masud is cited for the whale being sent from the Green Sea.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366/r4.anchor: من البحر الأخضر -فيما قاله ابن مسعود-حوتا يشق البحار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366/r5.claim: After Jonah threw himself into the sea, the whale swallowed him; God ordered it not to eat his flesh or break his bones, since its belly was to be a prison for Jonah, not his food.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366/r5.anchor: فأوحى الله إلى ذلك الحوت ألا تأكل له لحما، ولا تهشم له عظما؛ فإن يونس ليس لك رزقا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366#2/r1.claim: Dhun-Nun means the whale; the possessive association is valid because of their relation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: {وذا النون} يعني: الحوت، صحت الإضافة إليه بهذه النسبة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366#2/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says Jonah left angrily toward his people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366#2/r2.anchor: وقوله: {إذ ذهب مغاضبا} : قال الضحاك: لقومه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، الضحاك، ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and others explain the phrase as thinking God would not constrict him in the whale; Ibn Kathir notes Ibn Jarir prefers this, citing 65:7.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366#2/r3.anchor: يروى نحو هذا عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد، والضحاك، وغيرهم، واختاره (7) ابن جرير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366#2/r4.speaker: عطية العوفي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366#2/r4.claim: Atiyya al-Awfi reads the phrase as thinking God would not decree against him; he takes qadara and qaddara as synonyms, citing Arabic usage, a poem, and 54:12.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p366#2/r4.anchor: وقال عطية العوفي: {فظن أن لن نقدر عليه} (8) ، أي: نقضي عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r1.claim: Ibn Masud identifies the darknesses as the whale's belly, the sea, and night.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r1.anchor: قال ابن مسعود: ظلمة بطن الحوت، وظلمة البحر، وظلمة الليل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، عمرو بن ميمون، سعيد بن جبير، محمد بن كعب، الضحاك، الحسن، قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r2.claim: The same three darknesses are also reported from Ibn Abbas, Amr ibn Maymun, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, and Qatada.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r2.anchor: وكذا روي عن ابن عباس (1) ، وعمرو بن ميمون، وسعيد بن جبير، ومحمد بن كعب، والضحاك، والحسن، وقتادة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r3.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r3.claim: Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd says the darkness was a whale inside another whale, in the darkness of the sea.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r3.anchor: وقال سالم بن أبي الجعد: ظلمة حوت في بطن حوت (2) ، في ظلمة البحر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود، ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r4.claim: Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, and others say the whale carried Jonah through the seas to the bottom, where he heard the pebbles glorifying God and prayed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r4.anchor: قال ابن مسعود، وابن عباس وغيرهما: وذلك أنه ذهب به الحوت في البحار يشقها، حتى انتهى به إلى قرار البحر، فسمع (3) يونس تسبيح الحصى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r5.speaker: عوف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r5.claim: Awf says Jonah thought he had died, moved his legs, then prostrated and called the whale's belly a prayer place where no one else had prayed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r5.anchor: وقال عوف: لما صار يونس في بطن الحوت، ظن أنه قد مات، ثم حرك رجليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r6.speaker: سعيد بن أبي الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r6.claim: Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri says Jonah remained in the whale's belly for forty days; Ibn Jubayr narrates both this and the preceding report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r6.anchor: وقال سعيد بن أبي الحسن البصري: مكث في بطن الحوت أربعين يوما. رواهما (7) ابن جبير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r7.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying the whale spared Jonah and he heard sea creatures glorify God; angels recognized his voice, recalled his daily righteous deeds, interceded, and God ordered him cast ashore sick (37:145). Al-Bazzar says the report is known only through this route.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r7.anchor: عن عبد الله بن رافع -مولى أم سلمة-سمعت أبا هريرة يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r8.speaker: علي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r8.claim: Ali reports a Prophetic warning that a servant should not claim superiority to Jonah son of Matta, who glorified God in the darknesses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p367/r8.anchor: عن علي مرفوعا: لا ينبغي لعبد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p368/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p368/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p368/r1.claim: The preceding hadith also circulates without the clause comparing oneself to Jonah, on routes from Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud, and Abdullah ibn Ja'far; further chains appear in Surat Nun.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p368/r1.anchor: وقد روي هذا الحديث بدون هذه الزيادة، من حديث ابن عباس، وابن مسعود، وعبد الله بن جعفر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p368/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p368/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p368/r2.claim: Anas tentatively raises a report to the Prophet: Jonah prayed the supplication in the whale, and it rose toward the Throne as angels heard a faint, familiar voice from a strange land.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p368/r2.anchor: أنس بن مالك -ولا أعلم إلا أن أنسا يرفع الحديث إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم- أن يونس النبي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p368/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p368/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p368/r3.claim: In Anas's report, God identifies Jonah as a servant whose accepted deeds and answered prayers were known to the angels; they ask God to show mercy in adversity because of his ease-time worship, and the whale casts him ashore.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p368/r3.anchor: أنس بن مالك -ولا أعلم إلا أن أنسا يرفع الحديث إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم- أن يونس النبي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p368#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p368#2/r3.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p368#2/r3.claim: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas tells how Uthman failed to return his greeting, Umar asked about it, and Uthman recalled that remembering a Prophetic saying made his sight and heart grow clouded.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p368#2/r3.anchor: عن أبيه سعد، -وهو ابن أبي وقاص -قال: مررت بعثمان بن عفان، رضي الله عنه، في المسجد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p368#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p368#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p368#2/r4.claim: The Prophet identifies Jonah's prayer in the whale and says no Muslim invokes God with it about any matter without being answered; Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas transmits the report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p368#2/r4.anchor: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكر لنا [أول دعوة]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p369/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p369/r1.speaker: سعد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p369/r1.claim: Sa'd reports the Prophet saying that anyone who supplicates with Jonah's prayer will be answered.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p369/r1.anchor: عن سعد (5) قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من دعا بدعاء يونس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p369/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p369/r3.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p369/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib reports Sa'd ibn Malik asking whether Jonah's supplication is exclusive to him; the Prophet says it is general for believers who use it, a divine condition for supplicants.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p369/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب قال: سمعت سعد بن مالك -وهو ابن أبي وقاص-يقول: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p369/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p369/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p369/r4.claim: Hasan identifies Jonah's prayer in the passage as God's greatest name, by which a prayer is answered and a request granted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p369/r4.anchor: سألت الحسن، قلت: يا أبا سعيد، اسم الله الأعظم الذي إذا دعي به أجاب

JISHUMI:v7p4872/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4872/r7.speaker: يعقوب
JISHUMI:v7p4872/r7.claim: Yaqub reads يقدر with a passive yā and light dāl.
JISHUMI:v7p4872/r7.anchor: قرأ يعقوب: فظن أن لن يقدر عليه بضم الياء وفتح الدال مخففة على المجهول

JISHUMI:v7p4872/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4872/r8.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
JISHUMI:v7p4872/r8.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz reads with first-person nūn and a doubled dāl, from the sense of measuring or determining.
JISHUMI:v7p4872/r8.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن عبد العزيز بضم النون وتشديد الدال مكسورة من التقدير

JISHUMI:v7p4872/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4872/r9.speaker: عبيد بن عمير وقتادة
JISHUMI:v7p4872/r9.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr and Qatada read يقدر with passive yā and doubled dāl.
JISHUMI:v7p4872/r9.anchor: وقرأ عبيد ابن عمير وقتادة: يقدر بالياء وضمها وتشديد الدال على المجهول

JISHUMI:v7p4872/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4872/r10.speaker: القراء السبعة
JISHUMI:v7p4872/r10.claim: The seven canonical readers read نقدر with first-person nūn and an undoubled dāl.
JISHUMI:v7p4872/r10.anchor: والقراء السبعة: نقدر بالنون وفتحها وكسر الدال مخففة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r1.claim: Al-nūn means whale, to which Dhū al-Nūn is attributed.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r2.claim: Jonah wearied of his unbelieving people and left angry, thinking zeal for God justified it, but should have waited for permission to migrate; he was tested in the whale.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r2.anchor: برم بقومه لطول ما ذكرهم فلم يذكروا وأقاموا على كفرهم ، فراغمهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r3.claim: Alternatively, he angered his people by leaving while they feared punishment would descend.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r3.anchor: ومعنى مغاضبته لقومه : أنه أغضبهم بمفارقته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r5.claim: The verb has light and heavy forms, a light yāʾ reading, and passive readings with either consonant weight.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r6.claim: It is interpreted as constricting Jonah or decreeing punishment; the light reading can mean not exercising power over him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r6.anchor: وفسرت بالتضييق عليه ، وبتقدير الله عليه عقوبة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās asks Muʿāwiya about the verse after being overwhelmed by it; Muʿāwiya says it concerns divine decree, not power.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : أنه دخل على معاوية فقال : لقد ضربتني أمواج القرآن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r8.claim: The light reading may be figurative; alternatively Satan’s whisper arose and Jonah rejected it by proof, as believers do, as in 33:10.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r8.anchor: وأن يكون من باب التمثيل ، بمعنى : فكانت حاله ممثلة بحال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r9.claim: The darkness was inside the whale, compared with imagery in 2:17 and 2:257.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r9.anchor: في الظلمة الشديدة المتكاثفة في بطن الحوت ، كقوله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r10.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r10.claim: One view counts the whale’s belly, sea, and night as the darknesses.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r10.anchor: وقيل : ظلمات بطن الحوت والبحر والليل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r11.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r11.claim: Another says a larger whale swallowed Jonah’s whale, adding two belly-darknesses to the sea’s darkness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r11.anchor: وقيل : ابتلع حوته حوت أكبر منه ، فحصل في ظلمتي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r12.claim: The particle can mean ‘that’ or act as the explanatory ‘namely.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p132/r12.anchor: أي بأنه { لا إلاه إلا أنت } أو بمعنى ( أي )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p133/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p133/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p133/r1.claim: A Prophetic report says no distressed person who invokes this supplication will fail to receive an answer; no grading is stated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p133/r1.anchor: ما من مكروب يدعو بهذا الدعاء إلا استجيب له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p133/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p133/r2.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p133/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Jonah was saved only by admitting his wrongdoing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p133/r2.anchor: وعن الحسن : ما نجاه والله إلا إقراره على نفسه بالظلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465/r1.claim: “Dhun-nun” is Yunus ibn Matta, called the companion of the fish because the fish swallowed him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465/r1.anchor: وذا النون } وهو يونس بن متى , سمي بذلك لأنه صاحب الحوت , كما قال تعالى :

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465/r2.claim: Al-nun is the fish; the cited passage in al-Qalam calls Yunus the companion of the fish.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465/r2.anchor: والحوت النون , نسب إليه لأنه ابتلعه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r1.claim: The cited line brings together land and sea game, people of means and mounts, and settled and nomadic people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r1.anchor: والضب والنون والملاح والحادي … يعني أنه يجتمع فيه صيد البر والبحر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r2.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r2.claim: One view takes Jonah as opposing the king, whose name was Hizqiya, though the king had done him no harm.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r2.anchor: أحدها : يعني مراغما للملك وكان اسمه حزقيا ولم يكن به بأس , حكاه النقاش .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says Jonah left angry with his people.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r4.speaker: الشعبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r4.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says Jonah was angry with his Lord.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r5.claim: Jonah did not defy God, which would be unbelief and impossible for prophets; his fault was leaving without permission.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r5.anchor: لأن مراغمة الله كفر لا تجوز على الأنبياء , وإنما هي خروجه بغير إذن , فكانت هي معصيته .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r6.speaker: وهب
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r6.claim: Wahb says Jonah had a constricted temperament and could not patiently bear prophethood's burdens; the Qurʾan commands the Prophet to be patient like the resolute messengers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r6.anchor: لم يصبر لها , وكذلك قال الله : ^ { فاصبر كما صبر أولوا العزم من الرسل } ^ [ الأحقاف : 35 ] قاله وهب .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r7.claim: Another explanation says his people killed anyone they thought lied; after the threatened punishment was lifted, Jonah feared returning as a liar and fled to avoid being killed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r7.anchor: أنه كان من عادة قومه أن من كذب قتلوه , ولم يجربوا عليه كذبا , فلما أخبرهم أن العذاب يحل بهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets this as Jonah thinking God would not constrict his way, using the sense of qadara in 65:7.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r8.anchor: فظن أن لن نضيق طرقه , ومنه قوله : ^ { ومن قدر عليه رزقه } ^ [ الطلاق : 7 ] أي ضيق عليه , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r9.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r9.claim: Qatada and Mujahid say Jonah thought God would not punish him for what he had done.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r9.anchor: الثاني : فظن أن لن نعاقبه بما صنع , قاله قتادة , ومجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r10.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r10.claim: Ibn Shajara says Jonah thought God would not judge him by the judgment God had decreed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r10.anchor: الثالث : فظن أن لن نحكم عليه بما حكمنا , حكاه ابن شجرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r11.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r11.claim: Al-Farraʾ explains qadara as decree or judgment rather than ability; God would not mete out the decreed punishment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r11.anchor: قال الفراء : معناه لن نقدر عليه من العقوبة ما قدرنا , مأخوذ من القدر , وهو الحكم دون القدرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reads the verb with a doubled d, matching al-Farraʾ's sense of decree; inability would imply unbelief.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس : نقدر بالتشديد , وهو معنى ما ذكره الفراء , ولا يجوز أن يكون محمولا على العجز عن القدرة عليه لأنه كفر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r13.speaker: سليمان بن المعتمر
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r13.claim: Sulayman ibn al-Muʿtamir treats it as a question, with the interrogative alif omitted for concision.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r13.anchor: الرابع : أنه على معنى استفهام , تقديره : أفظن أن لن نقدر عليه , فحذف ألف الاستفهام إيجازا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatada identify the darknesses as night, sea, and the whale's interior.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r14.anchor: أحدهما : أنها ظلمة الليل وظلمة البحر وظلمة جوف الحوت , قاله ابن عباس , وقتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r15.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r15.claim: Salim ibn Abi al-Jaʿd says the darkness is the whale's belly alone.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r15.anchor: الثاني : أنها ظلمة الحوت في بطن الحوت , قاله سالم بن أبي الجعد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r16.claim: The darknesses may also mean the darkness of sin, hardship, and solitude.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r16.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : أنها ظلمة الخطيئة , وظلمة الشدة , وظلمة الوحدة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r17.claim: Jonah wronged himself by leaving without God's permission.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r17.anchor: يعني لنفسي في الخروج من غير أن تأذن لي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r18.claim: God's treatment was discipline rather than punishment: prophets are not punished, and even children who do not deserve punishment may be disciplined.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p465#2/r18.anchor: ولم يكن ذلك عقوبة من الله , لأن الأنبياء لا يجوز أن يعاقبوا , وإنما كان تأديبا , وقد يؤدب من لا يستحق العقاب كالصبيان .

MUJAHID:v1p415/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p415/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v1p415/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jonah's prophetic mission began only after the fish cast him out.
MUJAHID:v1p415/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال إنما كانت رسالة يونس بعد ما نبذه الحوت

MUQATIL:21:87-90/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r1.claim: The man of the fish is Jonah, son of Matta.
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r1.anchor: { وذا النون } يعنى يونس بن متى، عليه السلام

MUQATIL:21:87-90/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r2.claim: Jonah left in defiance of his people, Hizqil b. Ajar and the Israelites with him, departing before they believed.
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r2.anchor: { إذ ذهب مغاضبا } يعنى مراغما لقومه، لحزقيل بن أجار، ومن معه من بنى إسرائيل

MUQATIL:21:87-90/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r3.claim: Jonah supposed God would not punish him for what he had done.
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r3.anchor: فحسب يونس أن لن نعاقبه بما صنع

MUQATIL:21:87-90/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r4.claim: The three darknesses are night, the sea, and the whale's belly.
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r4.anchor: ظلمات ثلاث ظلمة الليل، وظلمة البحر، وظلمة بطن الحوت

MUQATIL:21:87-90/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r5.claim: Jonah affirmed God's oneness and declared Him free of having wronged Jonah.
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r5.anchor: { أن لا إله إلا أنت } يوحد ربه، عز وجل: { سبحانك } نزه تعالى أن يكون ظلمه

MUQATIL:21:87-90/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r6.claim: Jonah acknowledged that he had wronged himself.
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r6.anchor: يقول يونس عليه السلام: إنى ظلمت نفسى.

MUQATIL:21:87-90/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r8.speaker: الفراء
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r8.claim: Al-Farra, as quoted by Tha'lab, says both forms carry the same sense, from measuring or apportioning, not from having power over someone.
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r8.anchor: قال أبو العباس ثعلب: قال الفراء: أن لن نقدر عليه. ونقدر عليه، لمعنى واحد

MUQATIL:21:87-90/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r9.claim: The usage is compared with 89:16, where constricting provision derives from allotment or restriction rather than inability.
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r9.anchor:
ومثله فى سورة الفجر:
فقدر عليه رزقه
[الفجر: 16]
من التقدير، والتقتير، لا من القدرة

MUQATIL:21:87-90/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r10.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says Jonah remained in the whale's belly for three days.
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r10.anchor:
بلغنا أن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:
" مكث يونس، عليه السلام، فى بطن الحوت

MUQATIL:21:87-90/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r11.speaker: كعب
MUQATIL:21:87-90/r11.claim: Ka'b said Jonah remained in the whale's belly for forty days.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r1.claim: “The man of the fish” means the companion of the whale; nūn is a word for whale.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r1.anchor: أي اذكر صاحب الحوت والنون الحوت فأضيف اليه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r2.claim: “Angry” means that Jonah left in opposition to his people, provoking them by departing because he feared punishment would come upon them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ إذ ذهب مغاضبا ﴾ حال أي مراغما لقومه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r3.claim: A report says Jonah grew frustrated because his people rejected his repeated reminders and persisted in disbelief, so he left in defiance.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r3.anchor: روى أنه برم بقومه لطول ما ذكرهم فلم يتعظوا وأقاموا على كفرهم فراغمهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r4.claim: Jonah thought departure was permissible because he acted from anger for God and hatred of disbelief, but he should have remained patient until God permitted him to migrate; he was tested in the whale’s belly.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r4.anchor: وظن أن ذلك يسوغ حيث لم يفعله الا غضبا لله وبغضا للكفر وأهله وكان عليه ان يصابروا وينتظر الاذن من الله تعالى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r5.claim: “We would not constrain him” is the meaning of the phrase, rather than “We would not have power over him.”
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r5.anchor: ﴿ فظن أن لن نقدر ﴾ نضيق ﴿ عليه ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r6.claim: In an exchange with Muawiya about the verse, Ibn Abbas distinguishes qadar, constraint, from qudra, power.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r6.anchor: وعنى ابن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه دخل يوما على معاوية

NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r7.claim: The darkness may be the intense darkness inside the whale, or the combined darkness of night, sea, and whale.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r7.anchor: في بطن الحوت كقوله ذهب الله بنورهم وتركهم في ظلمات أو ظلمة الليل والبحر بطن الحوت

NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r8.claim: “An” may mean “that,” or it may introduce an explanation equivalent to “that is.”
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r8.anchor: أو بمعنى أي ﴿ سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين ﴾ لنفسي في خروجي

NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r9.claim: Jonah admits he wronged himself by leaving his people before God gave permission.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r9.anchor: لنفسى في خروجي من قومي قبل ان تأذن لي

NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r10.claim: A hadith says no distressed person who calls upon God with this supplication fails to receive a response; no grading is stated.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r10.anchor: في الحديث ما من مكروب يدعو بهذا الدعاء الا استجيب له

NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r11.speaker: الحسن
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r11.claim: Hasan says God saved Jonah only because he acknowledged his own wrongdoing.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p89#3/r11.anchor: وعن الحسن ما نجاه ا لله الا باقراره على نفسه بالظلم

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r1.claim: Dhu al-Nun is the epithet of Yunus ibn Matta because a fish swallowed him; al-nun means fish.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r1.anchor: أي واذكر «ذا النون» وهو لقب ليونس بن متى لابتلاع النون إياه. والنون الحوت.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r2.speaker: عثمان وثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r2.claim: A report says ʿUthman told a handsome boy's family to darken his nūna against the evil eye; Thaʿlab transmits from Ibn al-Aʿrabi that nūna is a small child's chin dimple and dssimu means blacken.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r2.anchor: وفي حديث عثمان رضي الله عنه أنه رأى صبيا مليحا فقال: دسموا نونته كي لا تصيبه العين.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r3.speaker: الحسن والشعبي وسعيد بن جبير وابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r3.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Shaʿbi, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, and a report from Ibn Masʿud take مغاضبا as angry with his Lord; al-Tabari and al-Qutaybi chose it, al-Mahdawi approved, and al-Nahhas defends its Arabic usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r3.anchor: قال الحسن والشعبي وسعيد بن جبير: مغاضبا لربه عز وجل. واختاره الطبري والقتبي

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r4.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r4.claim: Al-Nahhas says this is sound Arabic: angry “for” someone means angry on that person's behalf, as in “I became angry for you”; a believer is angered for God when He is disobeyed.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r4.anchor: والمعنى: مغاضبا من أجل ربه، كما تقول: غضبت لك أي من أجلك. والمؤمن يغضب لله

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r5.claim: Most linguists connect the Prophet's words to ʿAʾisha, “Make the stipulation of loyalty for them,” with this usage; al-Qutaybi strongly supports the connection.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r5.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لعائشة: «اشترطي لهم الولاء»

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r6.claim: A report portrays Yunus as narrow-chested under the burdens of prophethood, which crushed him like a weak camel under a heavy load; his anger was a minor lapse, and he was angry for God when punishment was lifted from his people.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r6.anchor: وفي الخبر في وصف يونس: إنه كان ضيق الصدر فلما حمل أعباء النبوة تفسخ تحتها

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿud says Yunus fled from his Lord's command until ordered to return after the people were spared; they repented when the threatened punishment came, but Yunus left without knowing this and without explicit permission.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r7.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: أبق من ربه أي من أمر ربه حتى أمره بالعود إليهم بعد رفع العذاب عنهم

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r8.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says God ordered Yunus to go to his people; when Yunus asked to prepare and even requested a sandal, he was told the matter was urgent, and his narrow disposition led him to leave angry.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن: أمره الله تعالى بالمسير إلى قومه فسأل أن ينظر ليتأهب، فأعجله الله حتى سأل أن يأخذ نعلا

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r9.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r9.claim: Qurtubi calls al-Nahhas's gloss the best: Yunus was angry for his Lord, namely with his people for disbelieving in their Lord.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r9.anchor: فهذا قول وقول النحاس أحسن ما قيل في تأويله.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r10.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Dahhak report that Yunus angrily left his people because they were obstinate, though God had commanded him to remain and call them; the passage says he was young and did not bear the full weight of prophethood.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88/r10.anchor: وقيل: إنه غاضب قومه حين طال عليه أمرهم وتعنتهم فذهب فارا بنفسه، ولم يصبر على أذاهم

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r1.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash and a group say Yunus left angry with the king who ruled his people.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r1.anchor: وقالت فرقة منهم الأخفش: إنما خرج مغاضبا للملك الذي كان على قومه.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas recounts that the prophet Shaya and King Hizqiya sought a strong, trustworthy Israelite prophet to go to Nineveh's ruler, who had raided Israel and taken captives, and ask him to release them; Yunus questioned whether God had appointed or named him, then left angry with Shaya, the king, and his people.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أراد شعيا النبي والملك الذي كان في وقته اسمه حزقيا أن يبعثوا يونس إلى ملك نينوى

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r3.claim: In that account, Yunus went to the Mediterranean and was swallowed because he abandoned Shaya's command, as 37:142 says; alternatively he was not yet a prophet, but a king's envoy, and after rescue God sent him to the people who then believed.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r3.anchor: فأتى بحر الروم وكان من قصته ما كان فابتلي ببطن الحوت لتركه أمر شعيا

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r4.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r4.claim: Al-Qushayri considers it likelier that Yunus's anger came after God had sent him and lifted punishment from his people, whom Yunus resented seeing spared.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r4.anchor: وقال القشيري: والأظهر أن هذه المغاضبة كانت بعد إرسال الله تعالى إياه، وبعد رفع العذاب عن القوم

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r5.claim: Qurtubi calls al-Qushayri's account the best interpretation and says its details will be explained in Sūrat al-Saffat.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r5.anchor: قلت: هذا أحسن ما قيل فيه على ما يأتي بيانه في «والصافات» إن شاء الله تعالى.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r6.claim: Another account says Yunus feared his people, who killed anyone caught lying; he fled by ship, admitted being the runaway when the ship stopped, and was swallowed as expiation for a minor lapse.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: إنه كان من أخلاق قومه قتل من جربوا عليه الكذب فخشي أن يقتل فغضب، وخرج فارا على وجهه

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r7.claim: The discussion links prophetic lapses to the testing of the believers at Uhud: prophets' sins are forgiven, while such testing can deter repetition; it cites 3:152 and 3:141.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r8.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak also says Yunus was angry with his people for rejecting God's messenger, and that everyone should be angry when God is disobeyed.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#2/r8.anchor: وعن الضحاك أيضا خرج مغاضبا لقومه لأن قومه لما لم يقبلوا منه وهو رسول من الله عز وجل

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r1.claim: A fourth view reads غضب as “felt indignation”: Yunus returned after the people were spared, disdained the outcome, and fled. A cited line uses أغضب for “I feel indignation”; Qurtubi objects that indignation still entails anger, so the view cannot say he was angry at no one.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r1.anchor: وقول رابع: إنه لم يغاضب ربه، ولا قومه، ولا الملك، وأنه من قولهم غضب إذا أنف.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r2.claim: The verse أغضب أن تهجى تميم بدارم is cited for using غضب in the sense of feeling affronted or indignant.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r2.anchor: وينشد هذا البيت: وأغضب أن تهجى تميم بدارم أي آنف.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r3.claim: One reported gloss says Iblis misled Yunus into thinking God might be unable to punish him; Qurtubi rejects it as unbelief, reporting it from Saʿid ibn Jubayr via al-Mahdawi and from al-Hasan via al-Thaʿlabi.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r3.anchor: قيل: معناه استزله إبليس ووقع في ظنه إمكان ألا يقدر الله عليه بمعاقبته.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r4.speaker: عطاء وسعيد بن جبير والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r4.claim: ʿAta, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, and many scholars interpret the verb as “constrict”; al-Hasan cites 13:26 and 65:7, and Qurtubi says this best fits the reports from Saʿid and al-Hasan.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r4.anchor: وذكر الثعلبي وقال عطاء وسعيد بن جبير وكثير من العلماء معناه: فظن أن لن نضيق عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas also takes قدر as “constrict”; قدر, قتر, and their variants can all carry that sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r5.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس فيما ذكره الماوردي والمهدوي.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r6.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد والفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r6.claim: Qatada, Mujahid, and al-Farraʾ derive the phrase from divine decree and judgment: Yunus thought God would not decree punishment for him, not that God lacked power.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r6.anchor: قاله قتادة ومجاهد والفراء. مأخوذ من القدر وهو الحكم دون القدرة والاستطاعة.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r7.speaker: ثعلب
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r7.claim: Thaʿlab says the verb is from تقدير rather than قدرة; his cited poem says what God decrees and determines will occur.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#3/r7.anchor: وروى عن أبي العباس أحمد بن يحيى ثعلب، أنه قال في قول الله عز وجل: { فظن أن لن نقدر عليه } هو من التقدير ليس من القدرة

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r1.claim: Qurtubi connects the two interpretations of قدر to the hadith of a man who asked his family to burn and scatter him after death, fearing divine judgment; the hadith appears in the Muwatta and other collections.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r1.anchor: وهذان التأويلان تأولهما العلماء في قول الرجل الذي لم يعمل خيرا قط لأهله إذا مات فحرقوه

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r2.claim: On the constriction reading, the man's words mean that if God constricts him, rigorously reckons with him, and requites his sins, that will be his fate; he then ordered the burning out of extreme fear.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r2.anchor: فعلى التأويل الأول يكون تقديره: والله لئن ضيق الله علي وبالغ في محاسبتي وجزاني على ذنوبي

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r3.claim: On the decree reading, he means that if God had decreed punishment for every sinner, He will punish him as no one else; the hadith is reported by the leading collectors in the Muwatta and elsewhere.
