QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r3.anchor: وعلى التأويل الثاني: أي لئن كان سبق في قدر الله وقضائه أن يعذب كل ذي جرم على جرمه

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r4.claim: The man was a believing monotheist; one version says his only good deed was monotheism, and he said he acted from fear of God, which Qurtubi says only a believing person can feel, citing 35:28.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r4.anchor: والرجل كان مؤمنا موحدا. وقد جاء في بعض طرقه «لم يعمل خيرا إلا التوحيد»

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r5.speaker: سليمان أبو المعتمر
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r5.claim: Sulayman Abu al-Muʿtamir proposes an interrogative reading with the hamza omitted for brevity: أفظن, “Did he think?”
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r5.anchor: الاستفهام وتقديره: أفظن فحذف ألف الاستفهام إيجازا

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r6.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز والزهري وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r6.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz and al-Zuhri read نُقَدِّر with a ḍamma on ن and doubled د; al-Mawardi also reports this reading from Ibn ʿAbbas.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r6.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن عبد العزيز والزهري: «فظن أن لن نقدر عليه» بضم النون وتشديد الدال من التقدير.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r7.speaker: عبيد بن عمير وقتادة والأعرج
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r7.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, Qatada, and al-Aʿraj read أن لن يقدر عليه with a doubled dāl in the passive.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r7.anchor: وقرأ عبيد بن عمير وقتادة والأعرج: «أن لن يقدر عليه» بضم الياء مشددا على الفعل المجهول.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r8.speaker: يعقوب وعبد الله بن أبي إسحاق والحسن وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r8.claim: Yaʿqub, ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Ishaq, al-Hasan, and Ibn ʿAbbas read يقدر عليه with a light dāl in the passive; al-Hasan also has the form فظن أن لن يقدر عليه.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r8.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب وعبد الله بن أبي إسحاق والحسن وابن عباس أيضا «يقدر عليه» بياء مضمومة وفتح الدال مخففا على الفعل المجهول.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r9.speaker: الباقون
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r9.claim: The remaining readers use نقدر with an open ن and kasra on د; Qurtubi says all these readings carry the sense of decree.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#4/r9.anchor: الباقون «نقدر» بفتح النون وكسر الدال وكله بمعنى التقدير.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r1.speaker: منذر بن سعيد
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r1.claim: Mundhir ibn Sa'id reports a reading with an initial alif, أفظن.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r1.anchor: وحكى القاضى منذر بن سعيد: أن بعضهم قرأ «أفظن» بالألف

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada identify the three darknesses as night, sea, and the whale.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r2.anchor: فقالت فرقة منهم ابن عباس وقتادة: ظلمة الليل، وظلمة البحر، وظلمة الحوت

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r3.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Jonah heard stones glorifying God at the earth's depths, called from three darknesses, and was cast ashore sick like a featherless chick.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r3.anchor: عن عمرو بن ميمون قال: حدثنا عبد الله بن مسعود في بيت المال قال: لما ابتلع الحوت يونس عليه السلام أهوى به إلى قرار الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r4.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r4.claim: Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd says the darknesses were the sea and a whale that had swallowed the first whale.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r4.anchor: وقالت فرقة منهم سالم بن أبي الجعد: ظلمة البحر، وظلمة حوت التقم الحوت الأول

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r5.claim: The plural can refer just to the first whale's interior: every side is dark, so using the plural is idiomatic, as in the well's dark recesses.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r5.anchor: ويصح أن يعبر بالظلمات عن جوف الحوت الأول فقط كما قال: «في غيابات الجب» وفي كل جهاته ظلمة فجمعها سائغ

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r6.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r6.claim: Al-Mawardi suggests the darknesses may be sin, distress, and loneliness.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r6.anchor: وذكر الماوردي: أنه يحتمل أن يعبر بالظلمات عن ظلمة الخطيئة، وظلمة الشدة، وظلمة الوحدة

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r7.claim: A report says God told the whale not to harm even one hair: its belly was Jonah's prison, not his food.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r7.anchor: وروي: أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى الحوت: «لا تؤذ منه شعرة فإني جعلت بطنك سجنه ولم أجعله طعامك»

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r8.claim: A report says Jonah prostrated inside the whale after hearing the fish glorify God in the sea's depths.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r8.anchor: وروي: أن يونس عليه السلام سجد في جوف الحوت حين سمع تسبيح الحيتان في قعر البحر

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r9.speaker: سعيد بن أبي الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r9.claim: Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan reports that Jonah thought he had died, discovered he was alive, resumed his customary prayer, and called the whale's belly a mosque where none had prayed before.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r9.anchor: عن عوف عن سعيد بن أبي الحسن قال: لما التقم الحوت يونس عليه السلام ظن أنه قد مات فطول رجليه فإذا هو لم يمت

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r10.speaker: أبو المعالي
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r10.claim: Abu al-Ma'ali explains that the Prophet was no nearer to God at the Lote Tree than Jonah was in the whale at the sea's bottom; this shows God is not spatially located.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r10.anchor: وقال أبو المعالي: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لا تفضلوني على يونس بن متى " المعنى فإني لم أكن وأنا في سدرة المنتهى بأقرب إلى الله منه

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r11.claim: The comparison of the Prophet with Jonah supports the conclusion that God is not in any direction.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r11.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن الباري سبحانه وتعالى ليس في جهة

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r12.claim: Jonah called himself wrong for abandoning persistent care for his people and patience with them.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r12.anchor: يريد فيما خالف فيه من ترك مداومة قومه والصبر عليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r13.claim: An alternative explanation is that Jonah counted his departure wrong because he left without permission.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r13.anchor: وقيل: في الخروج من غير أن يؤذن له

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r14.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r14.claim: Al-Mawardi says Jonah's ordeal was purification rather than punishment, since prophets cannot be punished; even children who do not deserve punishment may be disciplined.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r14.anchor: وقد يؤدب من لا يستحق العقاب كالصبيان ذكره الماوردي

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r15.claim: Another interpretation is that Jonah meant his supplication against his people for punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#5/r15.anchor: وقيل: من الظالمين في دعائي على قومي بالعذاب

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#6/r1.claim: Noah also prayed against his people without being taken to account, as Jonah was not for this confession.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#6/r1.anchor: وقد دعا نوح على قومه فلم يؤاخذ

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#6/r2.speaker: الواسطي
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#6/r2.claim: Al-Wasiti says Jonah declared God free of injustice and assigned wrongdoing to himself, as Adam and Eve did because they placed themselves outside their proper station.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#6/r2.anchor: وقال الواسطي في معناه: نزه ربه عن الظلم وأضاف الظلم إلى نفسه اعترافا واستحقاقا

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#6/r3.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#6/r3.claim: Abu Dawud reports from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas that the Prophet said no Muslim ever invokes God with Jonah's prayer in a matter without being answered.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#6/r3.anchor: روى أبو داود عن سعد بن أبي وقاص عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " دعاء ذي النون في بطن الحوت

QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#6/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#6/r4.claim: Some say that Jonah's supplication contains God's greatest name.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:87-88#6/r4.anchor: وقد قيل: إنه اسم الله الأعظم

QASHANI:21:87-88/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:21:87-88/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:21:87-88/r1.claim: The fish-bearing one signifies a spirit that has not reached perfection.
QASHANI:21:87-88/r1.anchor: أي: الروح الغير الواصل إلى رتبة الكمال

QASHANI:21:87-88/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:21:87-88/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:21:87-88/r2.claim: His departure signifies separation from the body, while his anger is directed at psychic faculties veiled from him and stubbornly refusing and resisting him.
QASHANI:21:87-88/r2.anchor: بالمفارقة عن البدنية { مغاضبا } عن قومه، القوى النفسانية لاحتجابها وإصرارها

QASHANI:21:87-88/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:21:87-88/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:21:87-88/r3.claim: The phrase may mean that he thought God would not exercise power over him through a trial like his, or that God would not constrict him.
QASHANI:21:87-88/r3.anchor: أي: لن نستعمل قدرتنا فيه بالابتلاء بمثل ما ابتلي به، أو: لن نضيق عليه

QASHANI:21:87-88/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:21:87-88/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:21:87-88/r4.claim: The fish of mercy swallowed him because divine wisdom required his attachment to a body for use and service.
QASHANI:21:87-88/r4.anchor: فالتقمه حوت الرحمة لوجوب تعلقه بالبدن في حكمتنا للاستعمال

QASHANI:21:87-88/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:21:87-88/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:21:87-88/r5.claim: He called from the three darknesses of bodily nature, vegetative soul, and animal soul, speaking through innate preparedness.
QASHANI:21:87-88/r5.anchor: في ظلمات المراتب الثلاث من الطبيعة الجسمانية والنفس النباتية والحيوانية بلسان الاستعداد

QASHANI:21:87-88/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:21:87-88/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:21:87-88/r6.claim: He confessed the essential unity imprinted in him by the prior covenant and natural pledge, and declared God's transcendence through the first primordial detachment.
QASHANI:21:87-88/r6.anchor: فأقر بالتوحيد الذاتي المركوز فيه عند العهد السابق وميثاق الفطرة والتنزيه المستفاد من التجرد الأول

QASHANI:21:87-88/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:21:87-88/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:21:87-88/r7.claim: He admitted his deficiency and failure to exercise justice with his people; God answered by enabling his wayfaring, giving patient guidance, and rescuing him from veiling through theophany.
QASHANI:21:87-88/r7.anchor: واعترف بنقصانه وعدم استعمال العدالة في قومه فقال: { إني كنت من الظالمين فاستجبنا له } بالتوفيق بالسلوك

RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r1.claim: “Dhu al-Nun” is Jonah: al-nun means the fish, and an informative epithet is preferable to an empty title when its descriptive benefit is clear.
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r1.anchor: لا خلاف في أن ذا النون هو يونس عليه السلام لأن النون هو السمكة

RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas places the fish episode before Jonah’s mission: after resisting a king’s assignment, Jonah was cast from a storm-tossed ship, swallowed unharmed, and later sent to Nineveh, whose people repented and were spared.
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r2.anchor: فقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : كان يونس عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r3.claim: The pre-mission chronology is supported by al-Saffat, which says Jonah was cast ashore, recovered, and then sent to a hundred thousand or more.
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r3.anchor: ودليل هذا القول قوله تعالى في سورة الصافات : { فنبذناه بالعراء وهو سقيم

RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r4.claim: An additional version of the pre-mission account says Gabriel ordered Jonah to warn Nineveh; when Jonah asked for a mount, Gabriel said the matter was too urgent, and the story then follows the ship and fish episode until Jonah is cast at Nineveh.
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r4.anchor: وفي هذا القول رواية أخرى وهي أن جبريل عليه السلام قال ليونس عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r5.claim: A second chronology puts the fish after Jonah preached to Nineveh and warned of punishment: when punishment was lifted after their repentance, he left them angry.
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r5.anchor: أما القول الثاني : وهو أن قصة الحوت كانت بعد دعائه أهل نينوى وتبليغه

RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r6.claim: Reasons proposed for Jonah’s departure after the Ninevites’ reprieve are shame among people who had experienced him as a liar, fear of their custom of killing liars, wounded pride, or anger that punishment had not come.
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r6.anchor: وثانيها : أنه كان من عادتهم قتل الكاذب . وثالثها : أنه دخلته الأنفة

RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r7.speaker: أكثر العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r7.claim: Most scholars hold that Jonah’s departure in anger and the fish episode occurred after God had sent him to the people and after their punishment was lifted.
RAZI-FULL:v22p184/r7.anchor: وأكثر العلماء على القول بأن قصة الحوت وذهاب يونس عليه السلام مغاضبا بعد أن أرسله الله تعالى إليهم

RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس والحسن والشعبي وسعيد بن جبير ووهب وابن قتيبة ومحمد بن جرير
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r1.claim: Most exegetes, including the named authorities and authors selected by the source, are said to read Jonah as having gone away angry at God; proponents of prophetic sin treat that as a grave offense.
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r1.anchor: قول ابن مسعود وابن عباس والحسن والشعبي وسعيد بن جبير ووهب واختيار ابن قتيبة ومحمد بن جرير

RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r2.speaker: القائلون بجواز الذنب
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r2.claim: The proponents argue that if Jonah’s anger was directed at God it was a grave sin, while anger at the king or people would still be prohibited, as they read the warning against imitating Jonah.
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r2.anchor: احتج القائلون بجواز الذنب على الأنبياء عليهم السلام بهذه الآية من / وجوه

RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r3.speaker: القائلون بجواز الذنب
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r3.claim: They argue that “he thought We would not be able” implies Jonah doubted God’s power.
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r3.anchor: احتج القائلون بجواز الذنب على الأنبياء عليهم السلام بهذه الآية من / وجوه

RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r4.speaker: القائلون بجواز الذنب
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r4.claim: They take Jonah’s confession of wrongdoing as an admission of sin, noting that the Qur’an uses “wrongdoers” as a term of blame.
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r4.anchor: احتج القائلون بجواز الذنب على الأنبياء عليهم السلام بهذه الآية من / وجوه

RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r5.speaker: القائلون بجواز الذنب
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r5.claim: They argue that, if Jonah had not sinned, God would not have punished him by casting him into the fish’s belly.
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r5.anchor: احتج القائلون بجواز الذنب على الأنبياء عليهم السلام بهذه الآية من / وجوه

RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r6.speaker: القائلون بجواز الذنب
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r6.claim: They cite the description of Jonah as “blameworthy” in another passage: a person deserving blame must have sinned.
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r6.anchor: احتج القائلون بجواز الذنب على الأنبياء عليهم السلام بهذه الآية من / وجوه

RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r7.speaker: القائلون بجواز الذنب
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r7.claim: They infer guilt from the command not to be like Jonah: they argue that forbidding imitation only makes sense if his conduct was sinful.
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r7.anchor: احتج القائلون بجواز الذنب على الأنبياء عليهم السلام بهذه الآية من / وجوه

RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r8.speaker: القائلون بجواز الذنب
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r8.claim: They infer from the contrast with the resolute messengers that Jonah was not one of them, and invoke statements about Moses and the Prophet’s instruction not to rank him above Jonah; al-Razi says this last point is outside the verse’s exegesis.
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r8.anchor: احتج القائلون بجواز الذنب على الأنبياء عليهم السلام بهذه الآية من / وجوه

RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r9.claim: Al-Razi rejects anger directed at God: the verse does not identify its object, and a prophet could not be angry with his Lord, since that would imply ignorance of God’s sovereignty and negate faith.
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r9.anchor: لكنا نقطع على أنه لا يجوز على نبي الله أن يغاضب ربه

RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r10.claim: Reports that Jonah left over preparations or voluntary worship cannot describe a prophet disobeying a divine command; the Qur’an says believers have no choice against God and His Messenger’s decision.
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r10.anchor: وأما ما روي أنه خرج مغاضبا لأمر يرجع إلى الاستعداد ، وتناول النفل

RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r11.claim: Since Jonah’s anger could not be against God, he most likely left angry at his people, the king, or both; his departure angered the people because they feared punishment would descend after he left.
RAZI-FULL:v22p185/r11.anchor: وجب أن يكون المراد أنه خرج مغاضبا لغير الله ، والغالب أنه إنما يغاضب

RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r1.claim: Al-Razi rejects that leaving the people was itself forbidden: Jonah was commanded to deliver the message, not to remain with them forever, and the command did not require repeated delivery.
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r1.anchor: فإن الله تعالى أمره بتبليغ تلك الرسالة إليهم ، وما أمره بأن يبقى

RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r2.claim: Jonah’s anger was not a sin: before it was forbidden, he could think it permitted, and it arose from zeal for God, religious honor, and hatred of unbelief; still, he should have endured and waited for permission to migrate.
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r2.anchor: من حيث إنه لم يفعله إلا غضبا لله تعالى وأنفة لدينه وبغضا للكفر وأهله

RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r3.claim: Al-Razi explains the warning not to imitate Jonah as God’s way of granting Muhammad the highest and best station.
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r3.anchor: ولهذا قال تعالى : { ولا تكن كصاحب الحوت } كأن الله تعالى أراد لمحمد

RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r4.claim: One reading takes “naqdira” as “constrain”: Jonah thought God would not restrict his choice to stay or leave. Al-Razi treats this as an excuse, not deliberate disobedience, since he thought the timing was open though delaying was better.
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r4.anchor: لن نضيق عليه وهو كقوله تعالى : { الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء من عباده ويقدر }

RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r5.claim: Another explanation treats the phrase as a simile: Jonah’s state resembled that of someone who thinks he may leave his people without waiting for God’s command.
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r5.anchor: أن يكون هذا من باب التمثيل بمعنى فكانت حالته ممثلة بحالة من ظن أن لن نقدر عليه

RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r6.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك والكلبي ورواية العوفي عن ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r6.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, al-Dahhak, al-Kalbi, and al-Awfi’s report from Ibn Abbas take “naqdira” to mean “decree”; al-Farra and al-Zajjaj choose this sense, deriving it from measuring or determining something.
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r6.anchor: وهو قول مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك والكلبي ، ورواية العوفي عن ابن عباس

RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r7.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز والزهري وعبيد بن عمير ويعقوب
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r7.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz and al-Zuhri read the verb with a rounded nūn and doubled consonant; Ubayd ibn Umayr has a doubled passive form, while Yaqub reads a light passive form.
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r7.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن عبد العزيز والزهري : ( فظن أن لن نقدر عليه بضم ) النون والتشديد

RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r8.claim: A report says Ibn Abbas told Muawiya that the verse uses qadar in the sense of decree, not qudra in the sense of power, resolving Muawiya’s concern that it attributed doubt to a prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r8.anchor: فقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما هذا من القدر لا من القدرة

RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r9.claim: A further interpretation uses “be able” figuratively for “do”: ability and action are related, so one may stand for the other.
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r9.anchor: فلا يبعد جعل أحدهما مجازا عن الآخر

RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd reads the words as a reproachful question: “Did he think We would not decree against him?”
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r10.anchor: أنه استفهام بمعنى التوبيخ معناه أفظن أن لن نقدر عليه عن ابن زيد

RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r11.claim: If Jonah’s episode preceded his prophethood, the thought may have occurred through Satan’s suggestion before he was a prophet; such a possibility does not apply after his mission.
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r11.anchor: على قول من يقول هذه الواقعة كانت قبل رسالة يونس عليه السلام كان هذا الظن حاصلا قبل الرسالة

RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r12.claim: If the confession predates prophethood, no reinterpretation is needed; afterward, its surface sense would make a prophet deserving of a curse, so al-Razi takes it as Jonah having left what was better despite being able to do better.
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r12.anchor: لوجب القول بكون النبي مستحقا للعن ، وهذا لا يقوله مسلم ، وإذا وجب التأويل

RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r13.claim: The fish episode was a trial, not punishment, because prophets cannot be punished; many commentators call any harm connected with a sin a punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r13.anchor: أنا لا نسلم أن ذلك كان عقوبة إذ الأنبياء لا يجوز أن يعاقبوا ، بل المراد به المحنة

RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r14.claim: The “blame” attached to Jonah was for leaving the better course, not for a grave sin.
RAZI-FULL:v22p186/r14.anchor: أن الملامة كانت بسبب ترك الأفضل

RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r1.claim: Al-Kashshaf explains “the darknesses” as the dense darkness inside the fish’s belly, comparing the Qur’an’s use of darknesses elsewhere.
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r1.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) في الظلمات أي في الظلمة الشديدة المتكاثفة في بطن الحوت

RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r2.claim: Some interpreters count different layers of darkness: at night, night, sea, and fish belly; by day they add the fish’s intestines.
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r2.anchor: ومنهم من اعتبر أنواعا مختلفة من الظلمات فإن كان النداء في الليل فهناك ظلمة الليل والبحر وبطن الحوت

RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r3.claim: Other proposed explanations are that another fish swallowed the fish holding Jonah, or that the fish’s deep descent left darkness layered above it.
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r3.anchor: أو أن حوتا ابتلع الحوت الذي هو في بطنه ، أو لأن الحوت إذا عظم غوصه في قعر البحر

RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r4.claim: The claim that Jonah’s fish descended to the seventh earth needs a report to support it; if it is proposed only to explain the darknesses, the other explanations suffice.
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r4.anchor: فإن ثبت ذلك بخبر فلا كلام

RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r5.claim: The phrase can be understood as “that there is no god but You,” or as an explanatory “that is to say.”
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r5.anchor: فالمعنى بأنه لا إله إلا أنت ، أو بمعنى أي

RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r6.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said that no distressed person who supplicates with this prayer fails to receive a response; al-Razi gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r6.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( ما من مكروب يدعو بهذا الدعاء إلا استجيب له )

RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r7.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says God rescued Jonah only because Jonah admitted his own wrongdoing.
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r7.anchor: وعن الحسن : ما نجاه الله تعالى إلا بإقراره عن نفسه بالظلم

RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r8.claim: “Glory be to You” declares God free of every defect, including incapacity; it shows Jonah did not mean that God lacked power, but affirmed that God acted with rightful wisdom rather than injustice, vengeance, or inability to free him.
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r8.anchor: فهو تنزيه عن كل النقائص ومنها العجز ، وهذا يدل على أنه ما كان مراده

RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r9.claim: Jonah says he wronged himself by fleeing his people without permission; as a penitent and remorseful person, he asks for the trial to be lifted, as the following verse says God answered him.
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r9.anchor: فالمعنى ظلمت نفسي بفراري من قومي

RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r10.claim: An alternative reading pairs God’s complete lordship with Jonah’s human weakness and shortcoming in fulfilling the right of lordship; that contrast itself suffices as a supplication.
RAZI-FULL:v22p187/r10.anchor: وهو أنه عليه السلام وصفه بقوله

QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r1.claim: One account says Jonah left angrily at his people for refusing faith and driving him out.
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r1.anchor: ويقال مغاضبا على قومه لما امتنعوا عن الإيمان وخرج من بينهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r2.claim: Another reading makes Jonah angry at himself, resisting his desire and standing against religious opponents.
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r2.anchor: ويقال مغاضبا على نفسه أي شديد المخالفة لهواه ، وشديدا على أعداء الدين من مخالفيه

QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r3.claim: Here naqdir means constrain: Jonah thought God would not confine him in the whale's belly.
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r3.anchor: أي أن لن نضيق عليه بطن الحوت ، ومن قوله : { وأما إذا ما ابتلاه فقدر عليه رزقه } [ الفجر : 16 ] أي ضيق

QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r4.claim: Alternatively, Jonah thought God would not hold him inside the whale.
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r4.anchor: ويقال فظن أن لن نقدر عليه من حبسه في بطن الحوت

QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r5.claim: A narrative says Jonah left after learning his people would be punished; on the journey a lion killed his family, a tiger seized one son, and a wave drowned another.
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r5.anchor: وخرج من بين قومه لما أخبر بأن الله يعذب قومه ، وخرج بأهله . ويقال إن السبع افترس أهله في الطريق

QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r6.claim: In a storm, Jonah offered himself as the guilty one to be cast overboard; the sailors hesitated because he looked righteous, and the lot fell to him.
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r6.anchor: فقال لهم يونس : لا تلقوا أمتعتكم في البحر بل أطرحوني فيه فأنا المجرم فيما بينكم

QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r8.claim: Muleem describes someone who has done what invites blame; Jonah is described this way when the whale swallows him.
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r8.anchor: ( وهو مليم ) : أي أتى بما يلام عليه ، قال تعالى : { فالتقمه الحوت وهو مليم }

QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r9.claim: God told the fish not to wound Jonah or break his bones, because he was entrusted to it rather than given as food.
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r9.anchor: وأوحى الله إلى السمك : لا تخدش منه لحما ولا تكسر منه عظما ، فهو وديعة عندك وليس بطعمة لك

QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r10.claim: One story says Jonah remained in the whale forty days; another says he accompanied it only a few days, and the fish was made aware of the sea's contents.
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r10.anchor: فبقي في بطنه - كما في القصة - أربعين يوما . وقيل إن السمك الذي ابتلعه أمر بأن يطوف في البحر

QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r11.claim: Though one account has Jonah with the fish only a few days, Dhun-Nun remained his name until the Resurrection.
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r11.anchor: ويقال إن يونس عليه السلام صحب الحوت أياما قلائل فإلى القيامة يقال له : ذا النون

QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r12.claim: Qushayri draws hope from Jonah's lasting association: a servant who loves and knows God through seventy years of worship should not lose that bond.
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r12.anchor: فما ظنك بعبد عبده - سبحانه - سبعين سنة ، ولازم قلبه محبته ومعرفته طول عمره . . . ترى أيبطل هذا ؟

QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r13.claim: The darknesses can mean night, sea, and the whale's belly.
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r13.anchor: يقال ظلمة الليل وظلمة البحر وظلمة بطن الحوت - هذا بيان التفسير

QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r14.claim: Alternatively, the darknesses are the obscurity of Jonah's time and uncertainty about his state.
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r14.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون الظلمات ما التبس عليه من وقته واستبهم عليه من حاله

QUSHAYRI:v2p304/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p304/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p304/r1.claim: Jonah's confession that he was among the wrongdoers itself constitutes seeking forgiveness.
QUSHAYRI:v2p304/r1.anchor: ولم يقر بالظلم إلا وهو يستغفر منه

STUDYQURAN:21:87/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r1.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r1.claim: Dhu’l-Nūn, mentioned only here in the Quran, is another name for Jonah.
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r1.anchor: Dhu’l-Nūn, mentioned only in this verse of the Quran, is another name for Jonah (Ṭ

STUDYQURAN:21:87/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r2.claim: Nūn means a large fish or whale, so Dhu’l-Nūn means roughly “the man of the fish.”
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r2.anchor: nūn means a large fish or whale, making the name Dhu’l-Nūn mean something like “the man of the fish”

STUDYQURAN:21:87/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r3.claim: The Quran leaves Jonah’s story incomplete, assuming prior knowledge of his preaching to Nineveh, flight by ship, and being cast overboard and swallowed by a fish.
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r3.anchor: The Quran does not tell the story of Jonah in full, but assumes its audience had prior knowledge of Jonah’s preaching to Nineveh, his flight on a ship

STUDYQURAN:21:87/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r4.claim: The commentary refers readers to 37:139–45 and notes that 68:48–50 is also understood to concern Jonah.
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r4.anchor: for more, see commentary on 37:139–45; 68:48–50 is also understood to be about Jonah

STUDYQURAN:21:87/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r5.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r5.claim: One reported view is that Jonah was angry with God for sparing Nineveh after promising to destroy it.
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r5.anchor: his anger was directed against God because He spared Nineveh after having promised to destroy it

STUDYQURAN:21:87/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r6.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r6.claim: Another reported view is that Jonah’s anger was righteous anger on God’s behalf at his people’s disobedience.
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r6.anchor: he was expressing a just anger on behalf of God in the face of the disobedience of his people

STUDYQURAN:21:87/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r7.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r7.claim: One interpretation is that Jonah believed God would not punish him for his sins.
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r7.anchor: Either Jonah believed God would not punish him for his sins

STUDYQURAN:21:87/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r8.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r8.claim: Another interpretation is that Jonah did not think God could end his existing punishment and affliction.
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r8.anchor: he did not believe God could end the punishment and affliction he was already suffering

STUDYQURAN:21:87/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r9.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r9.claim: Some read the phrase as a rhetorical question: “Did he think We had no power over him?”
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r9.anchor: Some see this as a rhetorical question meaning, “Did he think We had no power over him?” (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:21:87/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r10.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r10.claim: Others understand it to mean that Jonah thought God would not straiten him.
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r10.anchor: for others it means, “He thought We would not straiten him”

STUDYQURAN:21:87/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r11.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r11.claim: Naqdir, from qadara, can mean “straiten” or “withhold,” as in God’s provision being outspread or straitened.
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r11.anchor: which can also have the sense of“straiten” or “withhold,” as in 13:26: God outspreads and straitens provision for whomsoever He will (Q)

STUDYQURAN:21:87/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r12.speaker: those who refuse to believe
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r12.claim: Those who reject the idea that a prophet could imagine escaping divine omnipotence prefer the “straiten him” interpretation.
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r12.anchor: preferred by those who refuse to believe that the thought that one could escape God’s Omnipotence would ever occur to the mind of a prophet

STUDYQURAN:21:87/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r13.speaker: Su
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r13.claim: A literal reading treats Jonah’s thought as good opinion of God: he did not expect to be punished by Him.
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r13.anchor: that he did not expect to be punished by Him (Su)

STUDYQURAN:21:87/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r14.speaker: Q and Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r14.claim: The plural darknesses are interpreted as the fish’s belly within the sea’s darkness within the night’s darkness.
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r14.anchor: the darkness of the belly of the fish within the darkness of the sea within the darkness of the night (Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:21:87/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r15.claim: The commentary points to the discussion of the significance of the plural form in 5:16.
STUDYQURAN:21:87/r15.anchor: on the significance of the plural formẓulumāt, see 5:16c.

TAB-FULL:v16p373#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p373#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p373#2/r1.claim: Dhu al-Nūn means the man of the fish, Jonah son of Mattā; al-Ṭabarī says Jonah's story was already recounted in Sūrat Yūnus.
TAB-FULL:v16p373#2/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره: واذكر يا محمد ذا النون، يعني صاحب النون. والنون: الحوت. وإنما عنى بذي النون: يونس بن متى

TAB-FULL:v16p373#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p373#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p373#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Jonah left angry at his people.
TAB-FULL:v16p373#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس،، قوله: {وذا النون إذ ذهب مغاضبا} [الأنبياء: 87] يقول: «غضب على قومه»

TAB-FULL:v16p373#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p373#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v16p373#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk likewise says Jonah's anger was directed at his people.
TAB-FULL:v16p373#2/r3.anchor: يقول في قوله: {إذ ذهب مغاضبا} [الأنبياء: 87] «أما غضبه فكان على قومه»

TAB-FULL:v16p373#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p373#2/r4.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v16p373#2/r4.claim: Another view says Jonah left his people angry at his Lord because He lifted the punishment after promising it to them.
TAB-FULL:v16p373#2/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: ذهب عن قومه مغاضبا لربه، إذ كشف عنهم العذاب بعدما وعدهموه

TAB-FULL:v16p373#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p373#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p373#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās recounts that after Jonah warned his town of a promised punishment, they left the town, separated animals from their young, and begged God, who accepted their repentance and delayed the punishment; Jonah then heard what happened and left in anger, vowing not to return as a liar.
TAB-FULL:v16p373#2/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، قال:

TAB-FULL:v16p376/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p376/r1.speaker: سعيد بن أبي الحسن
TAB-FULL:v16p376/r1.claim: Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Ḥasan reports that Jonah committed a sin, went away angry at his Lord, and was led astray by Satan.
TAB-FULL:v16p376/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن أبي الحسن، قال: بلغني «أن يونس، لما أصاب الذنب، انطلق مغاضبا لربه، واستزله الشيطان»

TAB-FULL:v16p376/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p376/r2.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v16p376/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says Jonah was angry at his Lord.
TAB-FULL:v16p376/r2.anchor: عن مجالد بن سعيد، عن الشعبي، في قوله: {إذ ذهب مغاضبا} [الأنبياء: 87] قال: «مغاضبا لربه»

TAB-FULL:v16p376/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p376/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v16p376/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr's version adds that Jonah saw no punishment, thought people would accuse him of lying, and went away angry at his Lord until he reached the sea.
TAB-FULL:v16p376/r3.anchor: عن إسماعيل بن عبد الملك، عن سعيد بن جبير، فذكر نحو حديث ابن حميد، عن سلمة، وزاد، فيه: قال: فخرج يونس ينظر العذاب، فلم ير شيئا

TAB-FULL:v16p377/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p377/r1.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v16p377/r1.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih portrays Jonah as a righteous but short-tempered servant overwhelmed by prophetic burdens; he cast them aside and fled, against the endurance urged in the cited commands to Muhammad.
TAB-FULL:v16p377/r1.anchor: عن ربيعة بن أبي عبد الرحمن، عن وهب بن منبه اليماني

TAB-FULL:v16p377/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p377/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p377/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that Jonah left angry at his Lord; the wording that he thought God would not constrain him supports this reading.
TAB-FULL:v16p377/r2.anchor: وهذا القول، أعني قول من قال: ذهب عن قومه مغاضبا لربه، أشبه بتأويل الآية، وذلك لدلالة قوله: {فظن أن لن نقدر عليه} [الأنبياء: 87] على ذلك.

TAB-FULL:v16p377/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p377/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p377/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects the concern that Jonah could not be angry at his Lord: claiming instead that he disobeyed God's order to remain, convey the message, and warn his people is a graver fault.
TAB-FULL:v16p377/r3.anchor: لأن ذهابه عن قومه مغاضبا لهم، وقد أمره الله تعالى بالمقام بين أظهرهم، ليبلغهم رسالته

TAB-FULL:v16p377/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p377/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v16p377/r4.claim: One explanation says Jonah feared being exposed as a liar among people who had seen the threatened punishment withheld; another says their custom might lead them to kill a prophet whose warning failed.
TAB-FULL:v16p377/r4.anchor: فقال بعضهم: إنما فعل ما فعل من ذلك كراهة أن يكون بين قوم قد جربوا عليه الخلف فيما وعدهم، واستحيا منهم، ولم يعلم السبب

TAB-FULL:v16p377/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p377/r5.speaker: الحسن البصري
TAB-FULL:v16p377/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan's reported explanation says Jonah was ordered to hurry to warn a people, asked for time to prepare, and became angry when told the matter was urgent and he had not even put on his sandal.
TAB-FULL:v16p377/r5.anchor: فقال: أعجلني ربي أن آخذ نعلا فذهب مغاضبا وممن ذكر هذا القول عنه: الحسن البصري

TAB-FULL:v16p377/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p377/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p377/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says Jonah truly committed a fault, since otherwise God would not have punished and described him as blameworthy; he cites the command not to be like the fish's companion and the fish swallowing him while blameworthy.
TAB-FULL:v16p377/r6.anchor: ولولا أنه قد كان صلى الله عليه وسلم أتى ما قاله الذين وصفوه بإتيان الخطيئة، لم يكن الله تعالى ذكره ليعاقبه العقوبة التي ذكرها في كتابه

TAB-FULL:v16p378/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains نقدر عليه as constrain or restrict him, citing Arabic usage قدر على فلان for constricting someone and the verse about restricted provision.
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {فظن أن لن، نقدر عليه} [الأنبياء: 87] يقول: «ظن أن لن يأخذه العذاب الذي أصابه»

TAB-FULL:v16p378/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses it as Jonah thinking that the punishment which struck him would not reach him.
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {فظن أن لن، نقدر عليه} [الأنبياء: 87] يقول: «ظن أن لن يأخذه العذاب الذي أصابه»

TAB-FULL:v16p378/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r3.claim: Another Ibn ʿAbbās report says Jonah thought no punishment or trial would be decreed for his angry treatment of his people and flight; his punishment was the fish taking him.
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {فظن أن لن، نقدر عليه} [الأنبياء: 87] يقول: «ظن أن لن نقضي عليه عقوبة، ولا بلاء فيما صنع بقومه في غضبه إذ غضب عليهم

TAB-FULL:v16p378/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r4.claim: Mujāhid glosses the phrase as thinking God would not punish him for his sin.
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، أنه قال في هذه الآية: {فظن أن لن نقدر عليه} [الأنبياء: 87] قال: «فظن أن لن نعاقبه بذنبه»

TAB-FULL:v16p378/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r5.claim: Qatāda likewise says Jonah thought God would not punish him.
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {فظن أن لن نقدر عليه} [الأنبياء: 87] قال: يقول: «ظن أن لن نعاقبه»

TAB-FULL:v16p378/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r6.speaker: قتادة والكلبي
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r6.claim: Qatāda and al-Kalbī explain it as thinking God would not decree punishment for him.
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r6.anchor: حدثنا محمد بن عبد الأعلى قال: ثنا محمد بن ثور، عن معمر، عن قتادة والكلبي

TAB-FULL:v16p378/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r7.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Jonah thought God would decree no punishment or trial for his anger at his people and departure from them.
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r7.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {فظن أن لن نقدر}

TAB-FULL:v16p378/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r8.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās through Manṣūr gives the terse gloss: the affliction that happened to him.
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r8.anchor: عن منصور، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {فظن أن لن نقدر عليه} [الأنبياء: 87] قال: «البلاء الذي أصابه»

TAB-FULL:v16p378/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r9.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r9.claim: Another reported interpretation takes the phrase to mean Jonah thought he could elude or defeat his Lord; al-Ṭabarī later rejects this as implying that a prophet denied God's power.
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r9.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك: فظن أنه يعجز ربه فلا يقدر عليه

TAB-FULL:v16p378/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r10.speaker: سعيد بن أبي الحسن
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r10.claim: Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Ḥasan reports that Satan misled Jonah after his sin; despite his prior worship, God seized him, kept him in the fish for forty, and then released him mercifully after he repented and praised God, making him righteous.
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r10.anchor: عن سعيد بن أبي الحسن، قال: بلغني

TAB-FULL:v16p378/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r11.speaker: عوف
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r11.claim: ʿAwf reports Jonah's supplication that he had built God a mosque in a place where no one before him had built one.
TAB-FULL:v16p378/r11.anchor: قال عوف: وبلغني " أنه قال في دعائه: وبنيت لك مسجدا

TAB-FULL:v16p381/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p381/r1.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v16p381/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Jonah's prior worship and glorification helped God preserve him from Satan.
TAB-FULL:v16p381/r1.anchor: عن الحسن: {فظن أن لن، نقدر عليه} [الأنبياء: 87] «وكان له سلف من عبادة وتسبيح، فتداركه الله بها فلم يدعه للشيطان»

TAB-FULL:v16p381/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p381/r2.speaker: إياس بن معاوية
TAB-FULL:v16p381/r2.claim: Ibn Isḥāq reports that when Jonah's story was raised, Iyās ibn Muʿāwiya would ask, Why did he flee?
TAB-FULL:v16p381/r2.anchor: عن إياس بن معاوية المدني، أنه كان إذا ذكر عنده يونس، وقوله: {فظن أن لن نقدر عليه} [الأنبياء: 87] يقول إياس: «فلم فر»

TAB-FULL:v16p381/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p381/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p381/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd reads the clause as a question, Did he think We would not constrain him? Al-Ṭabarī rejects this because the wording has no sign of an interrogative, and Arabic deletion requires an indication.
TAB-FULL:v16p381/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {فظن أن لن نقدر عليه} [الأنبياء: 87] قال: هذا استفهام

TAB-FULL:v16p381/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p381/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p381/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that Jonah thought God would not imprison and constrict him as punishment for his anger; the alternative implies disbelief by attributing incapacity to God.
TAB-FULL:v16p381/r4.anchor: وأولى هذه الأقوال في تأويل ذلك عندي بالصواب، قول من قال: عنى به: فظن يونس أن لن نحبسه، ونضيق عليه، عقوبة له على مغاضبته ربه

TAB-FULL:v16p383/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p383/r1.speaker: عمرو بن ميمون، وابن جريج، وابن عباس، ومحمد بن كعب، وقتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p383/r1.claim: These authorities identify the three darknesses as the whale's belly, the sea, and the night.
TAB-FULL:v16p383/r1.anchor: عن عمرو بن ميمون: {فنادى في الظلمات} [الأنبياء: 87] قال: «ظلمة بطن الحوت، وظلمة البحر، وظلمة الليل»

TAB-FULL:v16p383/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p383/r2.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
TAB-FULL:v16p383/r2.claim: Salim says the darkness was a whale inside another whale in the sea; God had ordered the whale not to harm Jonah's flesh or bones.
TAB-FULL:v16p383/r2.anchor: عن سالم بن أبي الجعد: {فنادى في الظلمات} [الأنبياء: 87] قال: " أوحى الله إلى الحوت أن لا تضر له لحما ولا عظما.

TAB-FULL:v16p383/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p383/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p383/r3.claim: Al-Tabari holds the belly and sea are certain; the third darkness may be night or a whale within a whale, and without proof he defers to the text.
TAB-FULL:v16p383/r3.anchor: ولا شك أنه قد عنى بإحدى الظلمات: بطن الحوت، وبالأخرى: ظلمة البحر، وفي الثالثة اختلاف

TAB-FULL:v16p383/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p383/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p383/r4.claim: Jonah called on God admitting his sin and repenting of his offense, which was disobedience to God.
TAB-FULL:v16p383/r4.anchor: يقول: نادى يونس بهذا القول معترفا بذنبه، تائبا من خطيئته {إني كنت من الظالمين} [الأنبياء: 87] في معصيتي إياك

TAB-FULL:v16p384/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p384/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p384/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains Jonah's words as confession of his sin and repentance from his offense.
TAB-FULL:v16p384/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، قال

TAB-FULL:v16p384/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p384/r2.speaker: محمد بن قيس
TAB-FULL:v16p384/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Qays glosses Jonah's words as saying he worshiped no one but God, and that he sinned when he disobeyed Him.
TAB-FULL:v16p384/r2.anchor: قال أبو معشر: قال محمد بن قيس: قوله: {لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك} [الأنبياء: 87] ما صنعت من شيء، فلم أعبد غيرك،

TAB-FULL:v16p384/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p384/r3.speaker: عوف الأعرابي
TAB-FULL:v16p384/r3.claim: Awf reports that Jonah thought he had died in the whale, moved his leg, prostrated, and called the whale's belly a prayer place no one else had used.
TAB-FULL:v16p384/r3.anchor: عن عوف الأعرابي، قال: " لما صار يونس في بطن الحوت ظن أنه قد مات. ثم حرك رجله، فلما تحركت سجد مكانه،

TAB-FULL:v16p384/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p384/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أبي هريرة
TAB-FULL:v16p384/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet: God kept Jonah unharmed in a whale at the sea floor; Jonah heard sea creatures glorifying God and joined, angels recognized his former worship, interceded, and the whale cast him ashore sick.
TAB-FULL:v16p384/r4.anchor: سمعت أبا هريرة يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لما أراد الله حبس يونس في بطن الحوت، أوحى الله إلى الحوت:

TAB-FULL:v19p630/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r8.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says Jonah uttered the supplication of 21:87, after which the whale cast him out at sunset.
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير: {فالتقمه الحوت وهو مليم} [الصافات: 142] قال: قال {لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين} [الأنبياء: 87] «فلما قالها، قذفه الحوت

SULAMI:v2p13#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r1.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r1.claim: Jonah was angry with himself as he departed and thought God would not seize him for his anger and departure.
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r1.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمة الله عليه : مغاضبا على نفسه في ذهابه

SULAMI:v2p13#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r2.speaker: ذو النون
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r2.claim: Among the subtle things by which a servant is deceived are spiritual gifts, extraordinary favors, and the sight of signs.
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r2.anchor: وقال ذو النون : أخفي ما يخدع به العبد من الألطاف

SULAMI:v2p13#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r3.claim: Do not be people of impulsive action and retaliation; be people of mercy through divine governance and grace.
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r3.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه في قوله : ﴿ إذ ذهب مغاضبا ﴾ قال : لا تكونوا من بني المبادرة

SULAMI:v2p13#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r4.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r4.claim: Jonah supposed that God would not decree punishment for him, out of his good opinion of his Lord.
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r4.anchor: قال القاسم في قوله : ﴿ فظن أن لن نقدر عليه ﴾ توهم أن لن نقضي عليه العقوبة

SULAMI:v2p13#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r5.speaker: فارس
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r5.claim: Faris says Jonah was angry at his people for resisting his call and thought God would not exact revenge on them, showing that obedience and disobedience have no weight with Him.
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r5.anchor: قال فارس في قوله : ﴿ إذ ذهب مغاضبا ﴾ قال : كان غضبه على قومه

SULAMI:v2p13#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r6.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r6.claim: Jonah thought God would show him the measure of his own self because he was displeased with God’s servants; he glosses his confession as ignorance, since obedience does not bring one near nor sin drive one away.
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r6.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمة الله عليه : ظن أن لن نقدر نريه قدر نفسه

SULAMI:v2p13#2/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r7.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r7.claim: In the prayer that saves believers (21:88), they begin with divine unity, ask well, declare God beyond injustice, and attribute wrongdoing to themselves in confession.
SULAMI:v2p13#2/r7.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه في قوله : ﴿ وذا النون إذ ذهب مغاضبا ﴾ إلى قوله ﴿ ننجي المؤمنين ﴾ إذا عرفوا أحسنوا الدعاء

TABATABAI:21:85-87/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r2.claim: Dhu al-Nun is Jonah son of Matta, the prophet associated with the whale and sent to Nineveh; after his people repented and believed as punishment approached, God lifted it, Jonah departed, and the whale swallowed him before God rescued and sent him back.
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r2.anchor: النون الحوت وذو النون هو يونس النبي ابن متى صاحب الحوت الذي بعث إلى أهل نينوى

TABATABAI:21:85-87/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r3.claim: Jonah left angry at his people because they had not believed in him.
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r3.anchor: أي واذكر ذا النون إذ ذهب مغاضبا أي لقومه حيث لم يؤمنوا به

TABATABAI:21:85-87/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r4.claim: The phrase can mean that Jonah thought God would not constrict him, using qadara in the sense of constricting as in ‘restricted his provision.’
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r4.anchor: أي لن نضيق عليه من قدر عليه رزقه أي ضاق كما قيل

TABATABAI:21:85-87/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r5.claim: The departure may be a figurative depiction: Jonah acted as one angry with his master and imagining he could escape the master’s reach, without literally intending that meaning.
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r5.anchor: واردا مورد التمثيل أي كان ذهابه هذا ومفارقة قومه

TABATABAI:21:85-87/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r6.claim: A literal claim that Jonah was angry with God or thought God could not overpower him is incompatible with the dignity and divinely protected infallibility of prophets.
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r6.anchor: وأما كونه عليه السلام مغاضبا لربه حقيقة وظنه أن الله لا يقدر عليه جدا فمما يجل ساحة الأنبياء

TABATABAI:21:85-87/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r7.claim: The verse uses ellipsis: God tested Jonah through the whale, it swallowed him, and he called to his Lord from inside it.
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r7.anchor: فيه إيجاز بالحذف والكلام متفرع عليه والتقدير فابتلاه الله بالحوت فالتقمه فنادى في بطنه ربه

TABATABAI:21:85-87/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r8.claim: The ‘darknesses’ most likely mean the darkness of night, the sea, and the whale’s belly, an explanation also reported from others.
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r8.anchor: ظلمة البحر وظلمة بطن الحوت وظلمة الليل

TABATABAI:21:85-87/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r9.claim: Jonah disavows what his departure could imply: that there was any refuge besides God, that God could object to him, or that anything might escape God’s power.
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r9.anchor: فتبرأ من ذلك بقوله لا إله ألا أنت

TABATABAI:21:85-87/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r10.claim: Jonah admits wrongdoing because his act represented injustice, though it was not intrinsically wrong and he did not intend sin; God disciplined him to purify his will for closeness.
TABATABAI:21:85-87/r10.anchor: اعتراف بالظلم من حيث إنه أتى بعمل كان يمثل الظلم وإن لم يكن ظلما في نفسه

TABATABAI:21:78-91/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:78-91/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:21:78-91/r7.claim: In the Abu al-Jarud report, Abu Ja‘far says Jonah left in anger over his people’s deeds and thought God would not punish him for what he had done.
TABATABAI:21:78-91/r7.anchor: وفي رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

TABATABAI:21:78-91/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:78-91/r8.speaker: أبو الجارود
TABATABAI:21:78-91/r8.claim: Abu al-Jarud’s report glosses the phrase as Jonah thinking that God would not punish him for his deed.
TABATABAI:21:78-91/r8.anchor: وفي رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله

TABATABAI:21:78-91/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:78-91/r9.speaker: الرضا
TABATABAI:21:78-91/r9.claim: In al-Rida’s debate with al-Ma’mun on prophetic infallibility, he says zan means Jonah was certain God would not constrict his provision, not that God lacked power; such a belief would be unbelief.
TABATABAI:21:78-91/r9.anchor: وفي العيون بإسناده عن أبي الصلت الهروي في حديث الرضا عليه السلام مع المأمون

TABATABAI:21:78-91/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:78-91/r10.speaker: الرضا
TABATABAI:21:78-91/r10.claim: Al-Rida supports the meaning ‘constrict’ by citing the phrase about God restricting a person’s provision.
TABATABAI:21:78-91/r10.anchor: ألا تسمع قول الله عز وجل

TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r1.claim: Unlike the biblical scriptures, which allow attributing even major sins to prophets, the Quran exempts prophets from sin, even minor sin; apparent implications must therefore be interpreted accordingly.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r1.anchor: بخلاف القرآن الكريم فإنه ينزه ساحتهم عن لوث المعاصي حتى الصغائر

TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r2.claim: Accordingly, the Quran's descriptions of Jonah as absconding, angry, and supposing God could not constrain him depict the apparent state and implication of his action, not actual sin.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r2.anchor: ولذا حملنا قوله { إذ أبق } وقوله { مغاضبا فظن أن لن نقدر } على حكاية الحال وإيهام فعله

AKHFASH:v2p449#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p449#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p449#2/r1.claim: نقدر عليه means impose punishment on him; Jonah had sinned by leaving his people and was angry with a king, not with God, whom he knew too well to oppose.
AKHFASH:v2p449#2/r1.anchor: أي: لن نقدر عليه العقوبة، لأنه قد اذنب بتركه قومه وانما غاضب بعض الملوك ولم يغاضب ربه

TABRISI:21:87/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:87/r1.speaker: يعقوب
TABRISI:21:87/r1.claim: Ya‘qub reads the verb with yā’ and ḍamma; the other readers use nūn and kasra on the dāl.
TABRISI:21:87/r1.anchor: قرأ يعقوب فظن أن لن يقدر بضم الياء والباقون نقدر بالنون وكسر الدال

TABRISI:21:87/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:87/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:87/r3.claim: The nūn reading takes in as a lightened form of the emphatic particle and means Jonah thought God would not constrain him; the passive yā’ reading has the same meaning.
TABRISI:21:87/r3.anchor: إن هذه مخففة من الثقيلة وتقديره ظن أنه لن نقدر عليه أي لن نضيق عليه

TABRISI:21:87/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:87/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:87/r6.claim: Dhā al-nūn means the man of the fish, Jonah son of Mattai.
TABRISI:21:87/r6.anchor: أي واذكر ذا النون والنون الحوت وصاحبها يونس بن متى

TABRISI:21:87/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:87/r7.speaker: ابن عباس، الضحاك
TABRISI:21:87/r7.claim: They say Jonah left angry at his people after a long call to faith, when they still disbelieved despite an announced punishment; he left before permission came.
TABRISI:21:87/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس والضحاك أي مراغما لهم من حيث إنه دعاهم إلى الإيمان مدة طويلة فلم يؤمنوا حتى أوعدهم الله بالعذاب

TABRISI:21:87/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:87/r8.speaker: عطاء وجماعة من المفسرين
TABRISI:21:87/r8.claim: The phrase means that Jonah thought God would not constrict him.
TABRISI:21:87/r8.anchor: أي لن نضيق عليه عن عطاء وجماعة من المفسرين

TABRISI:21:87/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:87/r9.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة، الكلبي، الجبائي
TABRISI:21:87/r9.claim: They explain it as Jonah thinking God would not decree against him what He had decreed; here qadar means decree.
TABRISI:21:87/r9.anchor: وقيل: ظن أن لن نقضي عليه ما قضيناه والقدر بمعنى القضاء عن مجاهد وقتادة والكلبي والجبائي

TABRISI:21:87/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:87/r10.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:21:87/r10.claim: Al-Jubba’i explains that God constricted Jonah’s route until he had to board a ship and was then swallowed by the fish.
TABRISI:21:87/r10.anchor: قال الجبائي: ضيق الله عليه الطريق حتى ألجأه إلى ركوب البحر ثم قذف فيه فابتلعته السمكة

TABRISI:21:87/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:87/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:87/r11.claim: It is improper to say Jonah was angry with God or thought God could not seize him: anger with God and attributing inability to Him would be grave sins or disbelief, unfit for a prophet.
TABRISI:21:87/r11.anchor: ومن قال إنه خرج مغاضبا لربه وأنه ظن أن لن يقدر الله على أخذه بمعنى أنه يعجز عنه

TABRISI:21:87/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:87/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:21:87/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the sentence as a reproachful question: did Jonah think We would not decree against him?
TABRISI:21:87/r12.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: إنه استفهام معناه التوبيخ وتقديره فظن إن لن نقدر عليه

TABRISI:21:87/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:87/r13.speaker: علي بن عيسى
TABRISI:21:87/r13.claim: Ali ibn Isa rejects the interrogative interpretation because an interrogative cannot be omitted without a cue, although grammarians cite Arabic poetry where it is omitted.
TABRISI:21:87/r13.anchor: وأنكره علي بن عيسى وقال لا يجوز حذف الاستفهام من غير دليل عليه

TABRISI:21:87#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:87#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة
TABRISI:21:87#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada identify the darknesses as night, sea, and the fish’s belly.
TABRISI:21:87#2/r1.anchor: قيل إنها ظلمة الليل وظلمة البحر وظلمة بطن الحوت عن ابن عباس وقتادة

TABRISI:21:87#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:87#2/r2.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
TABRISI:21:87#2/r2.claim: Salim ibn Abi al-Ja‘d says there was a fish inside the belly of another fish.
TABRISI:21:87#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: كان حوت في بطن حوت عن سالم بن أبي الجعد

TABRISI:21:87#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:87#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:87#2/r3.claim: Before asking and praying, Jonah first invokes divine oneness and justice.
TABRISI:21:87#2/r3.anchor: لما أراد السؤال والدعاء قدم ذكر التوحيد والعدل

TABRISI:21:87#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:87#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:87#2/r4.claim: Jonah says he belongs to those in whom wrongdoing may occur, expressing humility and submission.
TABRISI:21:87#2/r4.anchor: أي من الذين يقع منهم الظلم، وإنما قاله على سبيل الخشوع والخضوع

TABRISI:21:87#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:87#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:87#2/r5.claim: Human beings cannot be considered immune from the occurrence of wrongdoing.
TABRISI:21:87#2/r5.anchor: لأن جنس البشر لا يمتنع منه وقوع الظلم

TABRISI:21:87#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:87#2/r6.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:21:87#2/r6.claim: Al-Jubba’i says Jonah’s time inside the fish was discipline rather than punishment, since punishment entails enmity toward its recipient; such discipline may apply to accountable or nonaccountable people, and his survival was a miracle.
TABRISI:21:87#2/r6.anchor: قال الجبائي: لم يكن يونس في بطن الحوت على جهة العقوبة من الله تعالى لأن العقوبة عداوة للمعاقب

THALABI:v6p301/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p301/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p301/r1.claim: The one called Dhul-Nun in the verse is Jonah, whom the passage depicts calling himself the sinful, runaway servant.
THALABI:v6p301/r1.anchor: فقام يونس فقال: أنا الرجل العاصي والعبد الآبق، وألقى نفسه في الماء فجاء حوت فابتلعه

THALABI:v6p301/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p301/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p301/r2.claim: Jonah throws himself into the sea; a fish swallows him and a larger fish swallows that fish, while God commands the larger fish not to harm Jonah because its belly is his prison, not his food.
THALABI:v6p301/r2.anchor: وأوحى الله إلى الحوت: لا تؤذ منه شعرة فإني جعلت بطنك سجنه، ولم أجعله طعاما لك

THALABI:v6p301/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p301/r3.speaker: الآخرون
THALABI:v6p301/r3.claim: Others say Jonah left angry after God withheld the punishment he had promised his people; embarrassed to return seeming false, he did not know why their destruction had been averted.
THALABI:v6p301/r3.anchor: وقال الآخرون: بل ذهب عن قومه مغاضبا لربه إذ كشف عنهم العذاب بعد ما وعدهموه

THALABI:v6p301/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p301/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p301/r4.claim: Some accounts say Jonah feared his people would kill a prophet whose announced punishment failed to arrive, so he left without knowing why the punishment was diverted; the fuller account is in Surah Yunus.
THALABI:v6p301/r4.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار: إن قومه كان من عادتهم أن يقتلوا من جربوا عليه الكذب

THALABI:v6p301/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p301/r5.speaker: القتيبي
THALABI:v6p301/r5.claim: Al-Qutaybi says the reciprocal form mufaʿala usually involves two parties but can describe one person's action; here مغاضبا means Jonah was angry and resentful.
THALABI:v6p301/r5.anchor: قال القتيبي: المغاضبة مفاعلة، وأكثر المفاعلة من اثنين كالمناظرة والمخاصمة والمجادلة

THALABI:v6p301/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p301/r6.speaker: القتيبي
THALABI:v6p301/r6.claim: Al-Qutaybi explains that Arabs use anaf, literally associated with the nose, for anger because the two are closely linked; Jonah resented that his people could call him a liar.
THALABI:v6p301/r6.anchor: والعرب تسمي الغضب أنفا، والأنف غضبا لقرب أحدهما من الآخر

THALABI:v6p301/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p301/r7.speaker: القتيبي
THALABI:v6p301/r7.claim: Al-Qutaybi says Jonah had long endured his people and wished God's punishment would befall them; after the promised deadline passed without punishment, he left like a runaway slave.
THALABI:v6p301/r7.anchor: وكان من طول ما عاين وقاسى من بلاء قومه يشتهي أن ينزل الله بهم بأسه

THALABI:v6p301/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p301/r8.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v6p301/r8.claim: Al-Hasan gives another account: Jonah was ordered to warn his people, sought time to prepare, was told the mission could not wait even for shoes, and left angrily at the haste.
THALABI:v6p301/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن : إنما غاضب ربه من أجل أنه أمر بالمصير إلى قومه لينذرهم بأسه

THALABI:v6p302/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p302/r1.speaker: وهب بن منبه اليماني
THALABI:v6p302/r1.claim: Jonah was righteous but temperamentally constrained by prophethood, fled its burden, and was excluded from the resolute prophets; Muhammad is told to endure as they did and not imitate the man of the fish.
THALABI:v6p302/r1.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه اليماني: إن يونس بن متى كان عبدا صالحا، وكان في خلقه ضيق

THALABI:v6p302/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p302/r2.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p302/r2.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, al-Dahhak, al-Kalbi, and Ibn Abbas in al-Awfi’s report explain this as Jonah thinking God would not decree punishment for him.
THALABI:v6p302/r2.anchor: فظن أن لن نقدر عليه أن لن نقضي عليه العقوبة، قاله مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك والكلبي

THALABI:v6p302/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p302/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p302/r3.claim: The verb can mean to decree or measure, as in cited Qur’anic expressions and the poet’s use of taqdir for determining benefit.
THALABI:v6p302/r3.anchor: وقال الشاعر في القدر بمعنى التقدير:

THALABI:v6p302/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p302/r4.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز والزهري
THALABI:v6p302/r4.claim: They read with a damma on initial nūn and doubled dāl, supporting the sense of decree or determination.
THALABI:v6p302/r4.anchor: دليل هذا التأويل قراءة عمر بن عبد العزيز والزهري فظن أن لن نقدر عليه بضم النون وتشديد الدال من التقدير

THALABI:v6p302/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p302/r5.speaker: عبيد بن عمير وقتادة ويعقوب
THALABI:v6p302/r5.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr and Qatada read the verb passive with doubled dāl; Yaqub reads it passive without doubling.
THALABI:v6p302/r5.anchor: وقرأ عبيد بن عمير وقتادة: فظن أن لن يقدر عليه بالتشديد على المجهول، وقرأ يعقوب يقدر بالتخفيف على المجهول.

THALABI:v6p302/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p302/r6.speaker: عطاء وكثير من العلماء
THALABI:v6p302/r6.claim: They explain it as Jonah thinking God would not confine or constrict him, using the sense of constricting provision in the cited verses.
THALABI:v6p302/r6.anchor: وقال عطاء وكثير من العلماء: معناه فظن أن لن نضيق عليه الحبس من قوله سبحانه الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر

THALABI:v6p302/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p302/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v6p302/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd treats the wording as an interrogative: did Jonah think God would not have power over him?
THALABI:v6p302/r7.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: هو استفهام معناه: أفظن أن لن نقدر عليه؟.

THALABI:v6p302/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p302/r8.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v6p302/r8.claim: Al-Hasan, in a report from Awf, takes it to mean Jonah thought he could defeat his Lord, leaving God unable to punish him.
THALABI:v6p302/r8.anchor: وروى عوف عن الحسن أنه قال: معناه: فظن أنه يعجز ربه فلا يقدر عليه.

THALABI:v6p302/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p302/r9.speaker: عوف
THALABI:v6p302/r9.claim: Awf reports that Jonah sinned, left in anger against his Lord, and Satan misled him into thinking God could not constrain him.
THALABI:v6p302/r9.anchor: قال: وبلغني أن يونس لما أذنب انطلق مغاضبا لربه واستزله الشيطان حتى ظن أن لن يقدر عليه.

THALABI:v6p302/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p302/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p302/r10.claim: Jonah’s past worship meant God did not abandon him to Satan; the fish swallowed him, but God preserved his life until he repented and was released.
THALABI:v6p302/r10.anchor: وكان له سلف وعبادة فأبى الله أن يدعه للشيطان فقذفه في بطن الحوت

THALABI:v6p302/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p302/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p302/r11.claim: The account gives three alternative durations in the fish: forty days and nights, seven days, or three days.
THALABI:v6p302/r11.anchor: فمكث في بطن الحوت أربعين من بين يوم وليلة، وقيل: سبعة أيام، وقيل: ثلاثة

THALABI:v6p302/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p302/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p302/r12.claim: Jonah repented in the fish and returned to self-reproach; God brought him out through mercy.
THALABI:v6p302/r12.anchor: وأمسك الله نفسه فلم يقتله هناك، فتاب إلى ربه في بطن الحوت وراجع نفسه فقال

THALABI:v6p303/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p303/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p303/r1.claim: The preceding interpretations are more fitting for prophets and farther from error than the claim that Jonah thought he could escape or defeat God.
THALABI:v6p303/r1.anchor: والتأويلات المتقدمة أولى بالأنبياء وأبعد من الخطأ.

THALABI:v6p303/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p303/r2.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
THALABI:v6p303/r2.claim: Most commentators identify the darknesses as night, sea, and the fish’s belly.
THALABI:v6p303/r2.anchor: فنادى في الظلمات أي ظلمة الليل وظلمة البحر وظلمة بطن الحوت، قاله أكثر المفسرين

THALABI:v6p303/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p303/r3.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
THALABI:v6p303/r3.claim: Salim ibn Abi al-Ja‘d says the darkness was the first fish’s interior, then another fish’s interior, within the darkness of the sea.
THALABI:v6p303/r3.anchor: وقال سالم بن أبي الجعد: ظلمة جوف الحوت، ثم ظلمة جوف الحوت الآخر الذي ابتلعه في ظلمة البحر.

THALABI:v6p303/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p303/r4.speaker: محمد بن قيس
THALABI:v6p303/r4.claim: Muhammad ibn Qays says Jonah acknowledged disobedience while affirming that he had worshipped no one but God.
THALABI:v6p303/r4.anchor: قال محمد بن قيس: قال يونس: إني كنت من الظالمين حين عصيتك، وما صنعت من شيء فلم أعبد غيرك.

THALABI:v6p303/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p303/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v6p303/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying God instructed the fish not to injure Jonah; Jonah heard sea creatures’ praise, joined it, and angels heard his weak voice.
THALABI:v6p303/r5.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «لما أراد الله سبحانه حبس يونس في بطن الحوت أوحى الله إلى الحوت أن خذه ولا تخدش له لحما

THALABI:v6p303/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p303/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v6p303/r6.claim: The angels recall Jonah’s daily good deeds and intercede; God orders the fish to cast him ashore, sick, as the Qur’an says.
THALABI:v6p303/r6.anchor: قالوا: يا ربنا إنا لنسمع صوتا ضعيفا بأرض غريبة! قال: ذاك عبدي يونس عصاني، فحبسته في بطن الحوت، قالوا: العبد الصالح

THALABI:v6p303/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p303/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p303/r7.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says Gabriel directed Jonah to a ship; lots selected him, and a fish swallowed him as refuge and a place of worship rather than food.
THALABI:v6p303/r7.anchor: وروى أبو هلال محمد بن سليمان عن شهر بن حوشب عن ابن عباس قال: أتى جبرئيل يونس (عليهما السلام) فقال له: انطلق إلى السفينة

THALABI:v6p303/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p303/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p303/r8.claim: The fish carried Jonah past al-Abulla and the Tigris before depositing him at Nineveh.
THALABI:v6p303/r8.anchor: فالتقمه الحوت فانطلق به من ذلك المكان حتى مر به على الأبلة، ثم مر به على دجلة ثم انطلق حتى ألقاه في نينوى

THALABI:v6p303/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p303/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p303/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas held that Jonah’s mission began only after the fish cast him out, supported by the statement that God sent him to a hundred thousand or more.
THALABI:v6p303/r9.anchor: فكان ابن عباس يقول: إنما كانت رسالة يونس بعد ما نبذه الحوت، ودليل هذا القول أن الله تعالى ذكر قصة يونس

THALABI:v6p303/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p303/r10.speaker: عوف
THALABI:v6p303/r10.claim: Awf says he heard that Jonah declared he had built a mosque for God in a place where no one had built one before.
THALABI:v6p303/r10.anchor: قال عوف: وبلغني أنه قال: وبنيت لك مسجدا في مكان لم يبنه أحد قبلي.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p287#7/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p287#7/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p287#7/r1.claim: Al-nūn means fish, so Dhā al-Nūn is the one associated with the fish.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p287#7/r1.anchor: وذا النون} ذا الحوت. والنون: الحوت.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p287#7/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p287#7/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p287#7/r2.claim: Lan naqdira ʿalayhi means “to make things narrow for him,” as when someone's provision is restricted; the cited usage in 89:16 confirms this sense.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p287#7/r2.anchor: فظن أن لن نقدر عليه} أي نضيق عليه. يقال: فلان مقدر عليه، ومقتر عليه في رزقه.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r1.claim: “The man of the whale” is Jonah ibn Mattā; God named him for being held in the whale's belly, as another verse calls him the companion of the fish.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r1.anchor: وهو يونس بن متى (¬6) سماه الله تعالى ذا النون لما حبسه في بطن النون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r2.claim: The author supplies an implied command: “And remember the man of the whale.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى: {وذا النون} أي: واذكر ذا النون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Jonah went away angry with his people.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r4.claim: In al-ʿAwfī's report, Ibn ʿAbbās says the Israelites pressed Jonah to ask a conquering king to release their captives; after asking the prophet Shuʿyāʾ whether God had ordered or named him, Jonah left angry at Shuʿyāʾ, the king, and his people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r4.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس في رواية العوفي، قال: إن شعيا (¬2) النبي والملك الذي كان في وقته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r5.claim: On that account, Jonah was punished for leaving what Shuʿyāʾ and the people had ordered, since the Qurʾān says the whale swallowed him while he was blameworthy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r5.anchor: وعلى هذا عوقب بتركه ما أمره به شعيا وقومه لأن الله تعالى قال فيه: {فالتقمه الحوت وهو مليم}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن مسعود، سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r6.claim: Another view says Jonah went away angry with his Lord; this is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās through ʿAṭāʾ, Ibn Masʿūd, and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: إنه ذهب مغاضبا لربه. وهذا قول ابن عباس في رواية عطاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Jonah had warned his people of punishment and left; after God lifted it, Jonah heard and fled toward a loaded ship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما وعد قومه العذاب، وخرج من بينهم، ورفع عنهم العذاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r8.speaker: مسروق عن عبد الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r8.claim: Masrūq reports from ʿAbd Allāh the gloss “a servant who fled from his Lord.”
