WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r8.anchor: وروى مسروق عن عبد الله في قوله: {إذ ذهب مغاضبا} قال: عبد أبق من ربه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r9.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says Jonah went angry with his Lord, and al-Ḥasan gives a similar view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r9.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: ذهب مغاضبا لربه (¬2). ونحو هذا قال الحسن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r10.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r10.claim: Ibn Qutayba argues that people recoil from attributing sins to prophets and distort scripture to avoid it; he cites a report that prophets erred except Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā, and points to Joseph's admission in 12:53.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r10.anchor: وإلى هذه الطريقة مال ابن قتيبة، فإنه يقول في هذه الآية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r11.speaker: الحديث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r11.claim: A report Ibn Qutayba cites says every prophet erred and intended a sin except Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r11.anchor: [روي في الحديث: أنه] (¬5) ليس من نبي إلا (¬6) وقد أخطأ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r12.claim: The author invokes Joseph's “I do not acquit myself” and his soul's urging toward evil as a comparison; Ibn Qutayba reads this as inward thought when desire arose.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r12.anchor: ولذلك قال (¬1) يوسف عليه السلام: {وما أبرئ نفسي إن النفس لأمارة بالسوء}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r13.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p153#2/r13.claim: The author asks what fault would merit the whale and confinement if Jonah merely grew angry with his people; “blameworthy” means he committed an offense deserving blame.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that after Jonah left the whale, God gave him a gourd tree for shade; when it dried Jonah wept, and God reminded him that he had wanted more than 100,000 people destroyed and ordered him back to his people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r1.anchor: ما روي عن ابن عباس في قصته: أنه لما خرج من بطن الحوت أنبت الله له شجرة من يقطين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r2.claim: This shows Jonah desired punishment for his people and resented its being lifted; sailing away disobeyed God's order that he return to them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r2.anchor: وهذا يدل على أنه اشتهى نزول عذاب الله بقومه، وكره دفعه عنهم، وأن ركوبه البحر كان معصية لله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r3.claim: The author rejects saying Jonah was angry with God, calling that a grave claim that cannot be made about prophets.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r3.anchor: فأما أن يقال إنه غاضب ربه، فهم عظيم، ولا يجوز القول بذلك في الأنبياء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba chooses to read mughāḍiban as resentful or affronted: Jonah left upset that his warning of punishment had not come true and feared being seen as a liar.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r4.anchor: وروي وجه آخر من التأويل في قوله: {إذ ذهب مغاضبا} وهو أن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r5.speaker: أبو صالح
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r5.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ reports that a king ordered Jonah, at Shuʿyāʾ's direction, to go to Nineveh; Jonah resented being sent by anyone but God, was swallowed, and was then sent to preach to the people, who believed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r5.anchor: وفي رواية أبي صالح: أن ملكا من ملوك بني إسرائيل كان أمره بالمسير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r6.claim: On Abū Ṣāliḥ's account, Jonah's resentment occurred before his mission.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا مغاضبته كانت قبل رسالته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r7.claim: The author prefers the repeatedly transmitted account that Jonah's departure followed his mission and God's lifting the impending punishment; Jonah resented the reprieve and feared appearing to have lied, so he fled aboard the loaded ship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p159/r7.anchor: ولكن الصحيح الذي تواترت به الرواية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r1.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r1.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, al-Dahhak, al-Kalbi, and Ibn Abbas in Atiyya’s transmission take this as Jonah thinking God would not decree punishment for him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r1.anchor: قول مجاهد، وقتادة، والضحاك، والكلبي، ورواية عطية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says ظن is actual conjecture here, not knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أراد الظن بعينه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r3.claim: Al-Farra explains that Jonah thought God would not decree the punishment that God had decreed for him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: ظن أن لن نقدر عليه من العقوبة ما قدرنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says نقدر here has the sense of نقدر, supporting the interpretation as decreeing punishment.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r5.claim: The verb قدر can mean to decree; the author supports this sense with a line describing a camel’s leg being measured.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r5.anchor: ويقال: قدر الله الشيء وقدره، أي: قضاه. والقدر يكون بمعنى التقدير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r6.claim: The cited verse of poetry uses قدرت to mean measured or determined, as evidence for قدر meaning decree or measure.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r6.anchor: ومفرهة عنس قدرت لساقها ... فخرت كما تتايع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r7.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz and al-Zuhri read with a doubled د; Ubayd ibn Umayr and Qatada read the passive with a doubled د. The two forms also occur at 56:60 and 87:3.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r7.anchor: قراءة عمر بن عبد العزيز والزهري (فظن أن لن نقدر عليه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r8.claim: The second explanation takes the phrase to mean that Jonah thought God would not confine or constrict him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r8.anchor: القول الثاني: فظن أن لن يضيق عليه الحبس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r9.claim: In the transmission of Ata, Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as meaning God would not punish Jonah.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r9.anchor: قال] (¬5) في رواية عطاء: أن لن نعاقبه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r10.claim: In Mansur’s transmission, Ibn Abbas says it refers to the affliction that befell Jonah.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r10.anchor: وقال في رواية منصور: يعني (¬7) البلاء الذي أصابه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r11.speaker: أبو الهيثم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r11.claim: Abu al-Haytham takes نقدر as constrict, citing 65:7 and 89:16; God confined Jonah in the whale more severely than any worldly punishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r11.anchor: قال أبو الهيثم: المعنى: فظن أن لن يضيق عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r12.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r12.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains the phrase as God not constricting Jonah, noting that Arabic calls a person’s provision both مقدر and مقتر when it is restricted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p161/r12.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: {فظن أن لن نقدر عليه} أي: لن نضيق عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r1.claim: God punished Jonah for his indignation and pride, fleeing, and reluctance to pardon his people and accept their repentance, by confining him inside the whale.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r1.anchor: عاقب الله يونس عن حميته وأنفته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r2.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r2.claim: Al-Hasan, in a report from Awf, says Jonah thought he could defeat or escape his Lord.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r2.anchor: وروى عوف، عن الحسن، أنه (¬10) قال: معناه: فظن أنه يعجز ربه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r3.claim: The author rejects this reading as remote and impermissible for a prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r3.anchor: وهذا التأويل بعيد، ولا يجوز مثله على الأنبياء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r4.speaker: أبو الهيثم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r4.claim: Abu al-Haytham says belief that Jonah thought God powerless is disbelief, since Jonah was a messenger.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r4.anchor: قال أبو الهيثم: من اعتقد أن يونس ظن أن لن يقدر الله عليه فهو كافر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r5.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r5.claim: Al-Azhari argues نقدر cannot mean ability: that would make Jonah doubt God’s power, a disbelief from which prophets are protected; only an ignorant reader of Arabic would hold it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r5.anchor: وقال الأزهري: قوله (أن لن نقدر عليه) لا يجوز أن يكون من القدرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r6.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash adopts the interpretation attributed to al-Hasan: Jonah thought he would escape God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r6.anchor: وقد ذهب الأخفش إلى مثل ما روي عن الحسن، فقال: فظن أن يفوتنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r7.speaker: أبو حاتم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r7.claim: Abu Hatim criticizes al-Akhfash for understanding نقدر as ability rather than constriction, saying he knew grammar but not Arabic usage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r7.anchor: فقال أبو حاتم: لم يدر الأخفش ما معنى (نقدر) وذهب إلى القدرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd reads the wording as an implicit question, “Did he suppose…?” The author rejects this because omitting the interrogative is allowed only by poetic necessity, especially without a contextual cue.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p164/r8.anchor: وروي عن ابن زيد أنه قال: هذا إستيفاه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and all commentators identify the darknesses as night, sea, and the whale’s belly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r1.anchor: يعني: ظلمة الليل، وظلمة البحر، وظلمة بطن الحوت. قاله ابن عباس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r2.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r2.claim: Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d gives the sequence as the first whale’s interior, the interior of another whale that swallowed it, and then the sea.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r2.anchor: وروي عن سالم بن أبي الجعد أنه قال: ظلمة جوف الحوت، ثم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r3.claim: Al-Farra says the darknesses are the sea, the whale’s belly, and its intestines where Jonah was.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: يقال: ظلمة البحر، وبطن الحوت ومعاؤها الذي كان فيه يونس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r4.speaker: محمد بن قيس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r4.claim: Muhammad ibn Qays explains Jonah’s confession as admitting that he disobeyed God in what he did, while worshipping no one else.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r4.anchor: قال محمد بن قيس (¬5): {إني كنت من الظالمين} حين عصيتك، وما صنعت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r5.claim: The declaration that none is deity except God and that He is exalted explains Jonah’s confession of wrongdoing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r5.anchor: وهذا معنى قوله: {لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r6.speaker: رسول الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r6.claim: The Prophet says that no Muslim who invokes with the prayer of Dhun-Nun in the whale is left unanswered; the source gives no grading.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r6.anchor: عن أبيه، أن رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r7.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r7.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada interpret Jonah’s words as confession of sin and repentance, returning to God and reconsidering himself inside the whale.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p166/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتاده: هذا القول من يونس اعتراف بذنبه، وتوبة من خطيئة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:87-89/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:87-89/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:87-89/r1.claim: Dhu al-Nun, the man of the fish, is Jonah.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:87-89/r1.anchor: اذكر صاحب الحوت، وهو يونس عليه السلام

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:87-89/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:87-89/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:87-89/r2.claim: Jonah left his people angry with them before God had commanded him to leave.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:87-89/r2.anchor: من بين قومه { مغاضبا } لهم قبل أمرنا له بذلك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:87-89/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:87-89/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:87-89/r3.claim: Jonah thought God would not decree for him the confinement in the fish's belly that God had decreed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:87-89/r3.anchor: أن لن نقضي عليه ما قضينا من حبسه في بطن الحوت

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:87-89/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:87-89/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:87-89/r4.claim: The three darknesses were the fish's belly, the sea, and the night.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:87-89/r4.anchor: ظلمة بطن الحوت، وظلمة البحر، وظلمة الليل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:87-89/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:87-89/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:87-89/r5.claim: Jonah confessed wrongdoing because he had been angry with his people and left them before receiving permission.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:87-89/r5.anchor: حيث غاضبت قومي وخرجت من بينهم قبل الإذن

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p335#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p335#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p335#2/r3.claim: The man called Dhun-Nun is Jonah.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p335#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p335#2/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p335#2/r4.claim: The Qur'an also calls Jonah the companion of the fish; nun means fish.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p335#2/r4.anchor: وقال في آية أخرى: {كصاحب الحوت} [القلم: 48] والحوت، النون

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p335#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p335#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p335#2/r5.claim: Hasan glosses his departure as enduring hardship for his Lord's religion.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p335#2/r5.anchor: يعني مكابدا لدين ربه في تفسير الحسن

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p335#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p335#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p335#2/r6.claim: Qatadah says Jonah thought God would not punish him for what he had done.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p335#2/r6.anchor: قال قتادة: فظن أن لن نعاقبه بما صنع

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p335#2/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p335#2/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p335#2/r7.claim: Yahya recounts that Jonah warned his people of a fixed coming punishment; they repented in humility, and God turned it away, but Jonah returned to find the city unchanged and left in distress.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p335#2/r7.anchor: وبلغنا أن يونس دعا قومه زمانا إلى الله عز وجل، فلما طال ذلك وأبوا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p337/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p337/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p337/r1.claim: After Jonah's prayer, God answered and rescued him by ordering the fish to cast him onto land.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p337/r1.anchor: فأوحى الله إلى الحوت أن يلقيه إلى البر

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p337/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p337/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p337/r2.claim: Yahya says Jonah was weak on the bare shore, like a nursing infant.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p337/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p337/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p337/r4.claim: Jonah found a flock, miraculously milked a sheep said to have no milk, and identified himself to its shepherd; the sheep and a tree later testified to his presence when the people feared breaking their oath not to lie.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p337/r4.anchor: فأخذ شاة منها فمسح بيده على ظهرها، فدرت فشرب من لبنها

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p337/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p337/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p337/r5.claim: Nineveh, Jonah's city, is in the land of Mosul on the Tigris.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p337/r5.anchor: وهي مدينة يقال لها: نينوى من أرض الموصل، وهي على دجلة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p337/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p337/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p337/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jonah boarded a boat on the Tigris, was swallowed, reached the sea, then returned by the Tigris and was cast onto its shore.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p337/r6.anchor: أن عبد الله بن عباس قال: في دجلة ركب السفينة، وفيها التقمه الحوت

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p338/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p338/r1.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p338/r1.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the darknesses as the sea, the night, and the fish's belly.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p338/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p338/r2.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p338/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says Jonah meant that he had sinned.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p338/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p338/r3.speaker: النبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p338/r3.claim: The Prophet says this was the prayer of Dhun-Nun inside the fish, and that no Muslim uses it to supplicate God for anything without receiving an answer.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p338/r3.anchor: عن جده سعد قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " دعوة ذي النون إذ دعا وهو في بطن الحوت

ELMALILI:21:87-88/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:87-88/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:87-88/r1.claim: Elmalılı renders Jonah's prayer as affirming God's sole divinity, offering Him glorification, and confessing that he was among the wrongdoers.
ELMALILI:21:87-88/r1.anchor: Senden başka ilâh yok, Sana arz-ı tesbih ederim, ben doğrusu zâlimlerden oldum

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r1.claim: “Dhu al-Nun” is Jonah’s epithet, reportedly given because a fish swallowed him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r1.anchor: Zünnûn, Yûnus peygamberin lakabıdır. Balık tarafından yutulduğu için kendisine Zünnûn lakabı verildiği söylenir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r2.claim: Jonah was sent to call Nineveh’s idol-worshipping people to monotheism; after few believed despite his long preaching, he lost hope, grew angry, and left by ship to escape their coming affliction.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r2.anchor: Putlara tapan Ninevâ (Ninova) halkını tevhid dinine davet etmekle görevlendirilmiş olan Hz. Yûnus, halkı uzun süre dine davet etmesine rağmen kendisine çok az kimse iman etmişti

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r3.claim: When the overloaded ship nearly sank, a lot was drawn to lighten its load; Jonah was cast into the sea and swallowed by a fish.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r3.anchor: Bindiği gemi, yükünün fazla olması sebebiyle batmaya yüz tutunca geminin yükünü hafifletmek üzere çekilen kura neticesinde denize atılmış ve bir balık tarafından yutulmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r4.claim: The prayer in the darkness was made inside the fish’s belly; God accepted it, rescued Jonah, and the fish left him sick in an open place, after which he recovered and returned to his people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r4.anchor: İşte Yûnus’un karanlıklar içinde yaptığı duadan maksat bu balığın karnında iken yaptığı duadır. Yüce Allah Yûnus’un duasını kabul ederek onu bu sıkıntıdan kurtarmış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r5.claim: The people Jonah had abandoned eventually recognized the truth, left idolatry, repented, and escaped punishment by returning to belief in God’s oneness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r5.anchor: Kendilerinden ümit keserek terkettiği kavmi ise, sonunda gerçeği görerek putperestliği bırakmışlar, tövbe edip Allah’ın birliği inancına döndükleri için azaptan kurtulmuşlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r6.speaker: başka bir rivayet
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r6.claim: Another report says Jonah warned Nineveh of punishment if they disbelieved; they repented and believed, so the punishment did not occur, but Jonah left angrily without knowing they had believed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r6.anchor: Başka bir rivayete göre Hz. Yûnus kavmine, inanmadıkları takdirde bir azaba uğrayacaklarını bildirmiş, ancak onlar tövbe edip imana geldikleri için bu azap tahakkuk etmemiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r7.speaker: başka bir rivayet
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r7.claim: In this report, Jonah left when the announced punishment failed to arrive on time, fearing that his people would mock him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r7.anchor: Onların imana geldiklerinden habersiz olan Yûnus, belirttiği azabın vaktinde gerçekleşmediğini görünce kendisinin alay konusu olacağını düşünerek kızgın bir halde kavminden ayrılıp gitmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r8.claim: For further accounts of Jonah and his people, the commentary refers to Qur’an 10:98 and 37:139 onward.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:87/r8.anchor: Yûnus ve kavmi hakkında daha fazla bilgi için bk. Yûnus 10/98; Sâffât 37/139-148

BURHAN:v3p206/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p206/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p206/r3.claim: An omitted verb can be supplied from another passage or context: “remember” with Jonah and the judges David and Solomon, “We sent” with Salih, and “We subjected” with Solomon's wind; other remembrance verses support this ellipsis.
BURHAN:v3p206/r3.anchor: بل علم بذكر النبي والمرسل إليه أن فيه إضمار أرسلنا

BURHAN:v3p206/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p206/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p206/r4.claim: The implied “remember” also has an omitted object, such as “your brother”; supplying it keeps إذ adverbial, since the author says it does not leave that function.
BURHAN:v3p206/r4.anchor: وما قاله ظاهر إلا أن مفعول اذكر يكون محذوفا أيضا تقديره واذكروا أخا لكم ونحوه

BURHAN:v1p33/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p33/r1.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
BURHAN:v1p33/r1.claim: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas reports in al-Bukhari's al-Adab al-Mufrad that four revelations concerned him: his mother's oath against his Islam, his request for a sword, his request to bequeath half then a third of his estate, and an injury after drinking wine with Ansar followed by the prohibition.
BURHAN:v1p33/r1.anchor: روى البخارى فى كتاب الأدب المفرد فى بر الوالدين عن سعد بن أبى وقاص رضى الله عنه قال نزلت فى أربع آيات

BURHAN:v1p33/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p33/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p33/r2.claim: Commentators usually begin with the occasion of revelation, but the author prefers first stating coherence unless that connection depends on the occasion; when it does, give the occasion first as a means to the interpretive end.
BURHAN:v1p33/r2.anchor: والتحقيق التفصيل بين أن يكون وجه المناسبة متوقفا على سبب النزول

NAHHAS:v3p77/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p77/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
NAHHAS:v3p77/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr explains Jonah as having gone away angry for his Lord.
NAHHAS:v3p77/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير أنه قال مغاضبا لربه جل وعز وربما أنكر هذا

NAHHAS:v3p77/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p77/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p77/r3.claim: Al-Naḥḥās endorses the gloss as angry for his Lord’s sake, like غضبت لك; believers are angered for God when He is disobeyed, as illustrated by the Prophet’s instruction to ʿĀʾisha.
NAHHAS:v3p77/r3.anchor: وهذا قول صحيح والمعنى مغاضبا من أجل ربه كما تقول غضبت لك أي من أجلك والمؤمن يغضب لله جل وعز إذا عصي وأكثر أهل اللغة يذهب إلى أن قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لعائشة رضي الله عنها اشترطي لهم الولاء من هذا

NAHHAS:v3p77/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p77/r4.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v3p77/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Jonah went away angry with his people over their disobedience.
NAHHAS:v3p77/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك إذ ذهب مغاضبا أي لقومه فيكون معنى هذا إنه غاضبهم لعصيانهم

NAHHAS:v3p77/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p77/r5.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v3p77/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash says Jonah had quarreled with one of the kings.
NAHHAS:v3p77/r5.anchor: وقال الأخفش إنما غاضب بعض الملوك

NAHHAS:v3p77/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p77/r6.speaker: الحسن ويعقوب القارئ
NAHHAS:v3p77/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Yaʿqūb read يقدر عليه instead of نقدر عليه.
NAHHAS:v3p77/r6.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( فظن أن لن يقدر عليه ) وقرأ يعقوب القارىء ( فظن أن لن يقدر عليه )

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r1.claim: Expressions first devised with distinction can become so familiar and commonplace that their merit is overlooked.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r1.anchor: حتى صارت في الاشتراك كالشىء المشترك من أوله والمبتذل الذي لم يكن الصون من شانه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r2.claim: Scarcity can win something more admiration than its actual benefit warrants, while widely available things lose esteem despite broader benefit.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r2.anchor: رب شىء نال فوق ما يستحقه من شغف النفوس به وأكثر مما توجبه المنافع الراجعة إليه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن حسان
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r3.claim: An anecdote attributed to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān says that as a crying child after a sting, he described it as wrapped in a striped cloak; his father Ḥassān declared him a poet.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r3.anchor: حديث عبد الرحمن بن حسان وذلك أنه رجع إلى أبيه حسان وهو صبي يبكي ويقول لسعنى طائر فقال حسان صفه يا بني فقال كأنه ملتف

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r4.claim: Ḥassān treats the child's apt comparison as evidence of strong poetic instinct and a way to distinguish a poetic mind.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r4.anchor: قال حسان قال ابني الشعر ورب الكعبة أفلا تراه جعل هذا التشبيه مما يستدل به على مقدار قوة الطبع

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r5.claim: The objection that the wording's charm lies only in ملتف and merely shows general wit is rejected: that phrase is the simile's intended core.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r5.anchor: قيل مسلم لك أن نكته الحسن في قوله ملتف ولكن لا يسلم أنه خارج من الغرض بل هو عين المراد من التشبيه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r6.claim: ملتّف conveys the wasp's particular arrangement and colors as if it wore them, completing a detailed likeness rather than a generic one.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p166/r6.anchor: وذلك انه يفيد الهيئة الخاصة في ذلك الوشى والصبغ وصورة الرنبور في اكتسائه بهما ويؤدى الشبه كما مضى من طريق التفصيل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p35/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p35/r1.speaker: حسان
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p35/r1.claim: Hassan is reported as saying that anyone whose hand benefits the Prophet must be thanked.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p35/r1.anchor: وروي من وجه آخر أن حسان قال : يا رسول الله من نالتك يده وجب علينا شكره .

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p35/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p35/r2.speaker: عائشة
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p35/r2.claim: Aisha says the Prophet often asked for her verses; after she recited a poem on repaying kindness, he reported God's teaching that thanking God requires thanking the person through whom the benefit came.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p35/r2.anchor: ومن المعروف في ذلك خبر عائشة رضوان الله عليها أنها قالت : كان رسول الله كثيرا ما يقول : ' أبياتك '

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p35/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p35/r3.speaker: عائشة
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p35/r3.claim: When Sawda recited a poem, Aisha and Hafsa thought it targeted their clans; the Prophet clarified that it concerned the Adi and Taym of Banu Tamim, and the poet was Qays ibn Ma'dan al-Kalbi.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p35/r3.anchor: فأخبر النبي فدخل عليهن وقال : ' يا ويلكن ! ليس في عديكن ولا تيمكن قيل هذا .

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p35/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p35/r4.speaker: الزبير بن بكار
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p35/r4.claim: Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar reports that the Prophet corrected a man's recitation from 'Abd al-Dar to 'Abd Manaf and affirmed that was how he had heard the poem.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p35/r4.anchor: فقال النبي : ' يا أبا بكر أهكذا قال الشاعر ؟ ' قال : لا يا رسول الله ، ولكنه قال

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p35/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p35/r5.speaker: النابغة الجعدي
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p35/r5.claim: The source cites a report of the Prophet appreciating poetry: al-Nabigha al-Ja'di recited a verse about his ancestors' glory reaching heaven and hoping to rise further; no grading is stated.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p35/r5.anchor: وأما ارتياحه للشعر ، واستحسانه له فقد جاء فيه الخبر من وجوه . من ذلك حديث النابغة الجعدي ؛ قال

BURHAN:v4p278/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p278/r4.speaker: السهيلي
BURHAN:v4p278/r4.claim: Al-Suhaylī says annexation to ذو is more honorific than to صاحب, as Jonah is ذو النون in praise and صاحب الحوت elsewhere.
BURHAN:v4p278/r4.anchor: وقال السهيلي والاضافة ل ذي اشرف من الاضافة لصاحب

BURHAN:v4p278/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p278/r5.speaker: السهيلي
BURHAN:v4p278/r5.claim: For Jonah's praised state, ذو النون is more apt; النون is nobler than الحوت because it occurs in the surah initials.
BURHAN:v4p278/r5.anchor: فانه ذكر في موضع الثناء عليه ذو النون ولم يقل صاحب النون لان الاضافة بذي اشرف من صاحب

BURHAN:v1p161/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p161/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p161/r4.claim: Dhu al-Nun means Yunus; the honorific Dhu and the alphabetic name Nun are more dignified than “companion” and “fish.”
BURHAN:v1p161/r4.anchor: فأضافه إلى الحوت والمراد يونس وقال فى سورة القلم

BURHAN:v4p61/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p61/r3.speaker: السهيلي
BURHAN:v4p61/r3.claim: Al-Suhayli says praise calls Yunus Dhu al-Nun, not companion of the fish; Nun is more dignified, as it appears among the opening letters and is paired with the exalted pen.
BURHAN:v4p61/r3.anchor: وقال أيضا فى الكتاب المذكور فى قوله تعالى

ITQAN:v2p473/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p473/r2.speaker: السهيلي
ITQAN:v2p473/r2.claim: Al-Suhayli says dhu is more honorific than sahib: Jonah is praised as dhu al-nun, but called sahib al-hut in a warning; nun also sounds nobler than hut.
ITQAN:v2p473/r2.anchor: قال السهيلي والوصف ب ذو أبلغ من الوصف بصاحب والإضافة بها أشرف فإن ذو يضاف للتابع وصاحب يضاف إلى المتبوع

ITQAN:v4p437/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p437/r5.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
ITQAN:v4p437/r5.claim: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas transmits that no Muslim invoking God with Jonah’s prayer in the whale’s belly for any matter fails to receive a response.
ITQAN:v4p437/r5.anchor: عن سعد بن أبي وقاص ( دعوة ذي النون إذ دعا وهو في بطن الحوت ﴿ لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين

ITQAN:v4p437/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p437/r6.speaker: ابن السني
ITQAN:v4p437/r6.claim: Ibn al-Sunni reports the saying that Jonah’s prayer is a word no distressed person utters without relief.
ITQAN:v4p437/r6.anchor: وعن ابن السني ( إني لأعلم كلمة لا يقولها مكروب إلا فرج عنه كلمة أخي يونس

DAMGHANI:v1p309/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p309/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p309/r9.claim: The three darknesses are three conditions in the womb; Jonah’s darknesses are night, water, and the whale; layered sea-darkness is glossed as heart, chest, and body.
DAMGHANI:v1p309/r9.anchor: الظلمات اي ثلاث ظلمات يعني ثلاث خصال قوله تعالى في سورة الزمر

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r1.claim: He rejects the claim that Jonah was angry at his people after they believed: anger at the very faith for which he was chosen and sent would be intolerable.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r1.anchor: وإن كان الغضب عليهم بعد أن آمنوا، فهذا أغلظ مما أنكروا، وأفحش مما استقبحوا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r2.claim: مغاضبة is a reciprocal pattern from anger, as in غضبت فلانا or ضاربته and قاتلته, where both parties may act on each other.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r2.anchor: والقول في هذا أن المغاضبة: المفاعلة من الغضب، والمفاعلة تكون من اثنين، تقول: غاضبت فلانا مغاضبة وتغاضبنا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r3.claim: A reciprocal form can also describe one actor alone: غاضبت من كذا means غضبت, like سافرت, ناولت, and the other listed verbs.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r3.anchor: وقد تكون المفاعلة من واحد، فنقول: غاضبت من كذا: أي غضبت

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r4.claim: Here مغاضبة means taking offense or feeling resentment: anger and dignified refusal are close and can be expressed by one another.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r4.anchor: ومعنى المغاضبة هاهنا: الأنفة، لأن الأنف من الشيء يغضب

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r5.claim: A poem alternates غضبت لكم and أنفت لكم for the same sentiment, showing that resentment and anger are near in meaning.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r5.anchor: يروى مرة: (أنفت لكم) ، ومرة: (غضبت لكم) ، لأن المعنيين متقاربان

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r6.claim: The verb أعبد can mean I resent or disdain; the poet's وأعبد أن تهجى means I feel affronted if Tamim is insulted through Darim.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r6.anchor: وقال الشاعر : وأعبد أن تهجى تميم بدارم يريد: آنف

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r8.claim: Jonah feared being branded a liar when the announced punishment did not arrive on time; after prolonged denial, mockery, and injury, he felt offended and wanted God's punishment to descend, while his patience was limited.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p232/r8.anchor: فدخلته الأنفة والحمية، وكان مغيظا بطول ما عاناه من تكذيبهم وهزئهم وأذاهم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p229#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p229#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p229#2/r1.claim: People reluctant to attribute sins to prophets resort to forced readings that conflict with scripture, though the wording and meaning do not support those evasions.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p229#2/r1.anchor: يستوحش كثير من الناس من أن يلحقوا بالأنبياء ذنوبا، ويحملهم التنزيه لهم، صلوات الله عليهم، على مخالفة كتاب الله جل ذكره

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p233/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p233/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p233/r2.claim: Lan naqdira ʿalayhi means 'We will not constrict him' or leave him without consequence, not that God cannot overpower him; Arabic uses the root for restricted provision.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p233/r2.anchor: أي لن نضيق عليه، وأنا نخليه ونهمله. والعرب تقول: فلان مقدر عليه في الرزق، ومقتر عليه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p233/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p233/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p233/r3.claim: Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ says qatar/qattara and qadara/qaddara are equivalent, all meaning to constrict.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p233/r3.anchor: قال أبو عمرو بن العلاء: قتر وقتر وقدر وقدر، بمعنى واحد، أي ضيق

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p233/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p233/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p233/r4.claim: God punished Jonah's proud flight and reluctance to pardon his people and accept their repentance by confining him in the whale's belly.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p233/r4.anchor: فعاقبه الله عن حميته وأنفته وإباقته، وكراهيته العفو عن قومه، وقبول إنابتهم- بالحبس له، والتضييق عليه في بطن الحوت

NASHR:v2p323/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p323/r7.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v2p323/r7.claim: Yaʿqūb reads the verb with yāʾ in ḍamma and dāl in fatḥa; the others read nūn in fatḥa and dāl in kasra.
NASHR:v2p323/r7.anchor: فقرأ يعقوب بالياء مضمومة وفتح الدال

ITQAN:v1p259/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p259/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p259/r4.claim: A semantic cause for lengthening is emphatic negation; Arabs use it for magnification in prayer, invocation, and denial, though reciters rank it below a phonological cause.
ITQAN:v1p259/r4.anchor: وأما السبب المعنوي فهو قصد المبالغة في النفي وهو سبب قوي مقصود عند العرب

ITQAN:v1p259/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p259/r5.speaker: ابن مهران
ITQAN:v1p259/r5.claim: Ibn Mihran calls this madd al-mubālagha: it emphasizes that no deity exists besides God, following a known Arab practice of lengthening emphatic expressions.
ITQAN:v1p259/r5.anchor: قال ابن مهران في كتاب المدات إنما سمي مد المبالغة لأنه طلب للمبالغة في نفي إلهية سوى الله تعالى

ITQAN:v2p321/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p321/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p321/r5.claim: The phrase means he thought the punishment that befell him would not seize him.
ITQAN:v2p321/r5.anchor: 1807 ﴿ فظن أن لن نقدر عليه ﴾ أن لن يأخذه العذاب الذي أصابه
